description: People, places and peoples named in the translated text, for the reader's cards. Keyed by Strong's number (G or H) and the lemma, which is copied from MACULA. A name used of more than one person has one sense per referent: a sense with "verses" applies to those verse ids, a sense without them to every other verse. Notes are English, written from what the passages say and widely agreed history and geography; every entry is an AI draft until a named reviewer approves it.

senses.name: Arni
senses.note: Named in Luke's genealogy of Jesus between Admin and Hezron. He probably corresponds to Ram, the son of Hezron in Matthew's list and in Ruth.

senses.name: the Alpha and the Omega
senses.note: A title of God, and in Revelation 22 of Jesus, taken from the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet: the beginning and the end of all things.

senses.name: Abiud
senses.note: Son of Zerubbabel and father of Eliakim in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Boaz
senses.note: A landowner of Bethlehem who married Ruth the Moabite; their son Obed was David's grandfather. His mother is named as Rahab in Matthew's genealogy.

senses.name: Boaz
senses.note: A landowner of Bethlehem who married Ruth the Moabite and became great-grandfather of David. Luke lists him among Jesus' ancestors.

senses.name: Beor
senses.note: The father of Balaam, the prophet hired to curse Israel in Numbers; Peter points to Balaam as an example of greed.

senses.name: Gabbatha
senses.note: The local name for the paved area outside the governor's residence in Jerusalem where Pilate sat in judgment over Jesus. Its exact site is uncertain.

senses.name: Gabriel
senses.note: An angel who stands in God's presence. He announced the birth of John the Baptist to Zechariah and the birth of Jesus to Mary.

senses.name: Gad
senses.note: The tribe of Israel descended from Gad, a son of Jacob; listed among the tribes from which 12,000 were sealed.

senses.name: the Gadarenes
senses.note: The people of Gadara, a city of the Decapolis south-east of the Sea of Galilee, whose territory ran toward the lake.

senses.name: Gaza
senses.note: An old Philistine city near the Mediterranean coast in the far south-west of the land, on the road toward Egypt.

senses.name: Gaius
senses.note: A believer in Corinth who hosted Paul and the whole church, probably the Gaius Paul baptized there (1 Corinthians 1:14).

senses.name: Gaius the Macedonian
senses.note: A Macedonian travelling companion of Paul who was dragged into the theatre at Ephesus during the riot over the goddess Artemis.

senses.name: Gaius of Derbe
senses.note: A believer from Derbe in Galatia who travelled with Paul toward Jerusalem with the collection for the poor.

senses.name: Gaius
senses.note: A dear friend of John the elder, to whom Third John is addressed. He was praised for welcoming travelling believers; he is probably not the same as the other men named Gaius.

senses.name: the Galatians
senses.note: The believers in the churches of Galatia in central Asia Minor (modern Turkey), to whom Paul wrote his letter.

senses.name: Galatia
senses.note: A region and Roman province in central Asia Minor (modern Turkey), home to some of the scattered believers Peter addresses.

senses.name: the Galatian region
senses.note: The country of the Galatians in central Asia Minor (modern Turkey), part of the Roman province of Galatia. Paul passed through it on his second and third journeys.

senses.name: Galilee
senses.note: The northern region of the land of Israel, west of the Sea of Galilee and the Jordan, ruled in Jesus' day by Herod Antipas. Jesus grew up there and did much of his work in its towns.

senses.name: the Galileans
senses.note: The people of Galilee, the northern region of the land where Jesus grew up and did much of his work. Many had seen what he did at the festival in Jerusalem.

senses.name: Judas the Galilean
senses.note: A rebel leader who drew a following at the time of the Roman census (about AD 6) and was killed. Gamaliel mentions him as an example of a movement that came to nothing.

senses.name: Galileans
senses.note: People from Galilee, the northern region of the land where Jesus grew up and called his first disciples. Galileans had a recognisable accent, which gave Peter away.

senses.name: Gallio
senses.note: Lucius Junius Gallio, Roman proconsul of Achaia around AD 51 and brother of the philosopher Seneca. At Corinth he refused to hear the Jewish leaders' charges against Paul.

senses.name: Gamaliel
senses.note: A respected Pharisee and teacher of the law on the Jewish council, who advised leaving the apostles alone. Paul says he was trained under him.

senses.name: Gideon
senses.note: A judge of Israel who with a small band of men delivered Israel from the Midianites. Hebrews names him among those who acted in faith.

senses.name: Gethsemane
senses.note: A place, probably an olive grove, on the Mount of Olives just east of Jerusalem, where Jesus prayed on the night of his arrest; the name probably means oil press.

senses.name: Azor
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus after the exile, son of Eliakim and father of Zadok in Matthew's genealogy. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Azotus
senses.note: The Greek name of Ashdod, an old Philistine city near the Mediterranean coast, where Philip appeared after baptizing the Ethiopian official.

senses.name: lake of Gennesaret
senses.note: Another name for the Sea of Galilee, taken from the plain on its north-western shore.

senses.name: Gennesaret
senses.note: A small, fertile plain on the north-west shore of the Sea of Galilee, between Capernaum and Magdala, where Jesus and his disciples came ashore.

senses.name: the Gerasenes
senses.note: The people of the region around Gerasa, on the east side of the Sea of Galilee, where Jesus freed a man from many demons. Manuscripts vary between Gerasenes, Gadarenes and Gergesenes; the exact place is uncertain.

senses.name: Abraham
senses.note: The ancestor of Israel, to whom God gave promises of land and descendants. Isaac was his son, and Jews traced their descent from him; these passages debate what it means to be his true children.

senses.name: Golgotha
senses.note: The place outside Jerusalem where Jesus was crucified; the Aramaic name means Place of a Skull. Its exact site is uncertain.

senses.name: Gomorrah
senses.note: A city near the Dead Sea, destroyed with Sodom in Genesis 19 for its wickedness. The two cities became a byword for God's judgment; the exact site is uncertain.

senses.name: Gog and Magog
senses.note: Names taken from Ezekiel's prophecy of a northern enemy; in Revelation they stand for the hostile nations of the whole earth gathered for a final battle.

senses.name: David
senses.note: The second king of Israel, around 1000 BC, a shepherd from Bethlehem who founded a royal line. The Christ was expected to come from his family, and many psalms are attributed to him.

senses.name: Dalmanutha
senses.note: A place on the shore of the Sea of Galilee where Jesus landed after feeding the four thousand. Its location is unknown; Matthew names Magadan here instead.

senses.name: Dalmatia
senses.note: A region on the east coast of the Adriatic Sea (in modern Croatia and its neighbours), part of the Roman province of Illyricum. Titus had gone there.

senses.name: Damaris
senses.note: A woman in Athens who believed after Paul spoke at the Areopagus; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: the Damascenes
senses.note: The people of Damascus, the ancient city in Syria, whose city was guarded by King Aretas's governor to arrest Paul.

senses.name: Damascus
senses.note: An ancient city in Syria, north-east of Galilee, with a large Jewish community. Saul is travelling there to arrest believers when the risen Jesus meets him, and he is later let down its wall in a basket to escape.

senses.name: Daniel
senses.note: A Jewish exile in Babylon in the sixth century BC whose book speaks of a horrifying desecration of the temple. Jesus refers to that prophecy.

senses.name: Athens
senses.note: The famous Greek city, a centre of philosophy and learning. Paul waited there for Silas and Timothy, was troubled by its idols, and spoke before the Areopagus.

senses.name: the Athenians
senses.note: The people of Athens, the famous Greek centre of learning, where Paul spoke before the council of the Areopagus.

senses.name: the Decapolis
senses.note: A group of about ten Greek-style cities, mostly east of the Jordan and the Sea of Galilee. Crowds came from there to Jesus, and a man he freed from demons spread the news there.

senses.name: Derbe
senses.note: A town in Lycaonia in southern Asia Minor, visited by Paul and Barnabas. Gaius, one of Paul's travelling companions, came from there.

senses.name: Derbe
senses.note: A town of Lycaonia in south-central Asia Minor (modern Turkey). Paul and Barnabas preached there, and Paul revisited it on later journeys; his companion Gaius came from there.

senses.name: Demas
senses.note: A co-worker of Paul who sends greetings with Luke. Elsewhere Paul says Demas later deserted him; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Demetrius the silversmith
senses.note: A silversmith of Ephesus who made silver shrines of Artemis and stirred up a riot against Paul because the gospel threatened his trade.

senses.name: Demetrius
senses.note: A believer whom the elder commends to Gaius as well spoken of by everyone; he may have carried the letter. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: the devil
senses.note: The chief enemy of God and deceiver of the world, also called Satan. Revelation pictures him as the great dragon and the ancient serpent who is thrown down and bound.

senses.name: the Egyptian rebel
senses.note: An unnamed Egyptian who, a few years before Paul's arrest, led a large following into the wilderness against Rome; the commander first mistook Paul for him. The historian Josephus also tells of him.

senses.name: the Egyptian Moses killed
senses.note: The Egyptian whom Moses struck down for mistreating an Israelite, as Stephen retells the story.

senses.name: the Egyptians
senses.note: The people of Egypt. Moses was educated in their learning, and their army drowned when it followed Israel into the Red Sea.

senses.name: Egypt
senses.note: The land of the Nile, south-west of Israel. Israel's ancestors lived and were enslaved there until God brought them out under Moses; Joseph, Mary and the child Jesus also fled there from Herod.

senses.name: the Ethiopians
senses.note: The people of the kingdom of Cush on the upper Nile, south of Egypt (in what is now Sudan), ruled by a queen called the Candace. A court official of hers was baptized by Philip.

senses.name: Agabus
senses.note: A Christian prophet from Judea. He foretells a famine in the time of Claudius and later binds his own hands and feet with Paul's belt to show that Paul will be handed over in Jerusalem.

senses.name: Aeneas
senses.note: A man of Lydda, paralysed and bedridden for eight years, whom Peter healed in the name of Jesus.

senses.name: Didymus
senses.note: A Greek nickname meaning "twin", given to Thomas, one of the Twelve disciples. Whose twin he was is not stated.

senses.name: Dionysius
senses.note: A member of the Areopagus council in Athens who believed after hearing Paul speak there. Nothing more is known of him for certain.

senses.name: the Twin Brothers
senses.note: Castor and Pollux, twin sons of Zeus in Greek myth and protectors of sailors, whose figures served as the emblem of the Alexandrian ship that took Paul to Italy.

senses.name: Diotrephes
senses.note: A church leader who loved to be first and refused to receive the elder's messengers or other travelling believers. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Aenon
senses.note: A place near Salim where John the Baptist baptized because there was plenty of water. The location is uncertain; it was probably in the Jordan valley or Samaria.

senses.name: Dorcas
senses.note: A disciple at Joppa, also called Tabitha, known for her good works and clothes made for widows. Peter raised her from death.

senses.name: Drusilla
senses.note: The wife of Governor Felix, a Jewish woman, daughter of Herod Agrippa I. With Felix she heard Paul speak about faith in Christ.

senses.name: Eber
senses.note: A descendant of Shem, son of Shelah and father of Peleg, in Luke's genealogy of Jesus; he is often linked with the name Hebrew.

senses.name: Hebrews
senses.note: A name for the Israelite people. By calling himself a Hebrew born of Hebrews, Paul stresses his pure Jewish descent and probably his use of the ancestral language.

senses.name: Hebrew-speaking believers
senses.note: Jewish believers in Jerusalem whose home language was Hebrew or Aramaic, as distinct from the Greek-speaking Jewish believers who complained that their widows were overlooked.

senses.name: Hebrew
senses.note: The language of the Jewish people. In these passages it probably means the Aramaic spoken in Judea at the time, which used names such as Gabbatha and Golgotha.

senses.name: Hezekiah
senses.note: King of Judah around 715 to 686 BC, son of Ahaz and father of Manasseh, remembered as a faithful reformer. He is listed among the kings in Jesus' genealogy.

senses.name: the Mount of Olives
senses.note: The ridge just east of Jerusalem across the Kidron Valley, with Bethany and Bethphage on its slopes. Jesus often spent the night there during his last days in Jerusalem.

senses.name: Elamites
senses.note: People from Elam, an ancient land east of Babylon in today's south-west Iran, among the Jews and converts in Jerusalem at Pentecost.

senses.name: Eleazar
senses.note: Son of Eliud and father of Matthan, the great-grandfather of Joseph in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Eliakim
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus after the exile, listed in Matthew's genealogy as son of Abiud and father of Azor; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Eliakim
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus listed in Luke's genealogy, in the line from David's son Nathan, some generations after David; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Eliezer
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy, between David and the exile; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Eliud
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus after the exile to Babylon, listed in Matthew's genealogy as son of Achim and father of Eleazar; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Elizabeth
senses.note: A woman of priestly descent, wife of the priest Zechariah and relative of Mary. Childless into old age, she became the mother of John the Baptist.

senses.name: Elisha
senses.note: The prophet who succeeded Elijah in the northern kingdom of Israel. Jesus recalls that he healed Naaman, a foreigner from Syria, of his skin disease.

senses.name: Greece
senses.note: The Greek mainland, here probably the province of Achaia with Corinth, where Paul stayed three months on his third journey.

senses.name: Greeks
senses.note: People of Greek language and culture; in the New Testament the word often stands for non-Jews in general. Paul pairs "Jew and Greek" to mean all people alike.

senses.name: Greeks
senses.note: People of Greek language and culture. In Mark the word marks the woman as a Gentile rather than a Jew; in Acts it describes women of standing in Berea.

senses.name: the Greek-speaking Jews
senses.note: Jews, often from outside the land of Israel, whose main language was Greek. In Acts some were believers whose widows were overlooked; others in Jerusalem argued with Saul.

senses.name: the Greek-speaking Gentiles
senses.note: Greek-speaking non-Jews in Antioch to whom believers from Cyprus and Cyrene first announced the good news. Manuscripts differ here between "Hellenists" and "Greeks".

senses.name: Greek
senses.note: The Greek language, widely spoken across the eastern Roman empire, and the language in which the New Testament was written.

senses.name: Elmadam
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy, between David and the exile; he is known only from this list.

senses.name: Elymas
senses.note: A Jewish magician, also called Bar-Jesus, at the court of the proconsul Sergius Paulus on Cyprus. He opposed Paul and Barnabas and was struck blind for a time.

senses.name: Immanuel
senses.note: A name from Isaiah's prophecy meaning God is with us. Matthew applies it to Jesus, born of Mary.

senses.name: Emmaus
senses.note: A village about seven miles from Jerusalem where the risen Jesus ate with two disciples; its exact location is uncertain.

senses.name: Hamor
senses.note: The ruler of Shechem in Jacob's time; Stephen mentions the tomb bought from his sons there.

senses.name: Enos
senses.note: Son of Seth and grandson of Adam (Enosh in Genesis), listed in Luke's genealogy of Jesus.

senses.name: Enoch
senses.note: Son of Jared and father of Methuselah, seventh in line from Adam. Genesis says he walked with God and was taken by God without dying.

senses.name: Hakeldama
senses.note: A field near Jerusalem, called Field of Blood in Aramaic, linked with the death of Judas Iscariot.

senses.name: Epaenetus
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets as dear to him and the first convert in the province of Asia. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Epaphras
senses.note: A believer from Colossae who probably brought the gospel there and served the church. He was with Paul when Colossians was written and prayed earnestly for the Colossians.

senses.name: Epaphroditus
senses.note: A believer from Philippi who brought the church's gift to Paul in prison and helped him there. He fell seriously ill, recovered, and Paul sent him home with this letter.

senses.name: Epicureans
senses.note: Followers of the Greek philosopher Epicurus, who taught that the gods do not intervene in human life and that the good life is calm, untroubled pleasure. Some debate with Paul in Athens.

senses.name: Aaron
senses.note: The brother of Moses and Israel's first high priest, from the tribe of Levi. Hebrews contrasts his priesthood with that of Christ, and Elizabeth was descended from him.

senses.name: Erastus
senses.note: The city treasurer, probably of Corinth, where Paul wrote Romans, who sends greetings. A Latin inscription found at Corinth names an official called Erastus, possibly the same man.

senses.name: Erastus, Paul's assistant
senses.note: One of the men who helped Paul, sent ahead with Timothy to Macedonia, who later stayed in Corinth. He may be the same as the city treasurer, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Hermas
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Hermes
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets along with others in a group. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Hermes
senses.note: The Greek messenger god. At Lystra the crowd took Paul, the main speaker, for Hermes and Barnabas for Zeus.

senses.name: Hermogenes
senses.note: A man in the province of Asia who deserted Paul; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: the Red Sea
senses.note: The sea Israel crossed when God brought them out of Egypt. The Greek name covered the Red Sea and its gulfs; the exact crossing place is uncertain.

senses.name: Esli
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's family line, after the exile. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Aquila
senses.note: A Jewish believer and tentmaker, husband of Priscilla, who worked with Paul and risked their lives for him; a church met in their house.

senses.name: Hezron
senses.note: A son of Perez and grandson of Judah, listed in Matthew's family line of Jesus. Nothing more is told of him in these passages.

senses.name: Eve
senses.note: The first woman, wife of Adam. Paul refers to her creation after Adam and to the serpent's deception of her.

senses.name: Eubulus
senses.note: A believer in Rome who sends greetings to Timothy at the end of Paul's last letter; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Eunice
senses.note: Timothy's mother, a Jewish believer, and daughter of Lois. Paul praises her sincere faith, which Timothy shares.

senses.name: Euodia
senses.note: A woman in the church at Philippi who had worked alongside Paul; he urges her and Syntyche to settle their disagreement.

senses.name: Eutychus
senses.note: A young man in Troas who fell asleep during Paul's long talk, fell from a third-floor window and was taken up dead, but Paul brought him back alive.

senses.name: Euphrates
senses.note: The great river of Mesopotamia, flowing from eastern Turkey through Syria and Iraq to the Persian Gulf. In Revelation it marks the frontier from which threatening powers come.

senses.name: the Ephesians
senses.note: The people of Ephesus, the great port city of the Roman province of Asia, famed for its temple of the goddess Artemis.

senses.name: Ephesus
senses.note: A major port city on the west coast of Asia Minor (modern Turkey), capital of the Roman province of Asia. Paul worked there for over two years; some early manuscripts of Ephesians lack the name in its opening.

senses.name: Ephraim
senses.note: A town near the wilderness where Jesus withdrew with his disciples before his last Passover. It is probably the village of et-Taiyibeh north-east of Jerusalem, but the location is uncertain.

senses.name: Zebulun (the region)
senses.note: The tribal land of Zebulun in lower Galilee, west of the Sea of Galilee. Matthew links Jesus' move to Capernaum with Isaiah's promise of light for this region.

senses.name: Zebulun (the tribe)
senses.note: The tribe descended from Zebulun, a son of Jacob and Leah; it is listed among the tribes of Israel sealed in Revelation.

senses.name: Zacchaeus
senses.note: A rich chief tax collector in Jericho who climbed a tree to see Jesus. Jesus stays at his house, and he promises to give half his goods to the poor and repay what he took by fraud.

senses.name: Zerah
senses.note: A son of Judah and Tamar, twin brother of Perez, named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus.

senses.name: Zechariah father of John
senses.note: A priest of the division of Abijah, husband of Elizabeth and father of John the Baptist. He was struck silent for doubting the angel's message until John was named.

senses.name: Zechariah son of Barachiah
senses.note: A man of God killed between the sanctuary and the altar, named by Jesus as the last martyr of the scriptures; probably the Zechariah son of Jehoiada stoned in 2 Chronicles 24, though identification is debated.

senses.name: Zebedee
senses.note: A Galilean fisherman, father of the disciples James and John. He was in his boat mending nets with them when Jesus called his sons to follow him.

senses.name: Zeus
senses.note: The chief god of the Greeks. At Lystra people took Barnabas for Zeus, and the priest of Zeus's temple there wanted to offer sacrifice to him and Paul.

senses.name: Simon the Zealot
senses.note: One of the Twelve apostles. Zealot probably means he had been zealous for the law or linked with Jewish nationalists; Matthew and Mark call him the Cananaean.

senses.name: the Alexandrians
senses.note: People from Alexandria, the great port city of Egypt on the Nile delta, home to a large Jewish community. Apollos came from there, and Alexandrian Jews in Jerusalem debated with Stephen.

senses.name: Zenas
senses.note: A lawyer whom Paul asks Titus to help on his journey along with Apollos. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Zerubbabel
senses.note: A descendant of David and grandson of King Jehoiachin who led a group of exiles back from Babylon around 538 BC and served as governor of Judah while the temple was rebuilt.

senses.name: Alexandria
senses.note: The great port city of Egypt on the Mediterranean, founded by Alexander the Great. Grain ships from Alexandria carry Paul toward Italy.

senses.name: Alexander, opponent of Paul
senses.note: A man who, with Hymenaeus, abandoned the faith and whom Paul handed over to Satan; possibly the same as the metalworker in 2 Timothy.

senses.name: Alexander the metalworker
senses.note: A metalworker who did Paul much harm and strongly opposed his message; perhaps the Alexander named in 1 Timothy.

senses.name: Alexander of Ephesus
senses.note: A Jew of Ephesus whom the Jewish community pushed forward to speak during the riot over Artemis; the crowd shouted him down.

senses.name: Alexander of the high priest's family
senses.note: A member of the high priest's family who sat with the council when Peter and John were questioned; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Alexander son of Simon
senses.note: Son of Simon of Cyrene, the man made to carry Jesus' cross; Mark names him and his brother Rufus as if readers knew them.

senses.name: Heli
senses.note: The father of Joseph in Luke's genealogy of Jesus. Matthew names Joseph's father as Jacob, and the difference is explained in various ways.

senses.name: Elijah
senses.note: A prophet of the northern kingdom of Israel in the ninth century BC who opposed the worship of Baal. Malachi foretold his return before the Day of the LORD, so people asked John the Baptist if he was Elijah.

senses.name: Er
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy, son of Joshua and father of Elmadam. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Herod the Great
senses.note: King of Judea under Rome from about 37 to 4 BC, famous for his building works. He ruled when Jesus was born and ordered the killing of the boys of Bethlehem.

senses.name: Herod Agrippa I
senses.note: Grandson of Herod the Great, king over Judea from AD 41 to 44. He had James the brother of John killed and imprisoned Peter, and died suddenly at Caesarea.

senses.name: Herod the tetrarch
senses.note: Herod Antipas, son of Herod the Great, who ruled Galilee and Perea from 4 BC to AD 39. He married Herodias, beheaded John the Baptist, and questioned Jesus before his death.

senses.name: the Herodians
senses.note: Supporters of the Herod family and its rule, probably of Herod Antipas in Galilee. They joined with Pharisees in plotting against Jesus and in testing him about paying tax to Caesar.

senses.name: Herodias
senses.note: A granddaughter of Herod the Great who left her husband, Herod's son Philip, to marry his half-brother Herod Antipas. John the Baptist condemned the marriage, and she brought about his execution.

senses.name: Herodion
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets as a fellow Jew; his name may suggest a link to the household of the Herods. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Isaiah
senses.note: An Israelite prophet in Jerusalem in the eighth century BC, whose prophecies make up the book of Isaiah. New Testament writers often quote him, as John the Baptist and Paul do here.

senses.name: Esau
senses.note: The elder twin son of Isaac and Rebekah, brother of Jacob and ancestor of the Edomites. Paul cites the choice of Jacob over Esau to show that God's choice does not depend on human merit.

senses.name: Thaddaeus
senses.note: One of the twelve apostles. He is probably the same as the apostle Luke calls Judas son of James; nothing he did is recorded.

senses.name: the Red Sea
senses.note: The sea Israel crossed when the LORD brought them out of Egypt, recalled by Stephen among the wonders done through Moses.

senses.name: Tamar
senses.note: The daughter-in-law of Judah who bore him twin sons, Perez and Zerah (Genesis 38). She is one of the women named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus.

senses.name: Terah
senses.note: Father of Abraham, Nahor and Haran, who moved from Ur toward Canaan and died in Harran. He is listed in Jesus' genealogy.

senses.name: Theophilus
senses.note: The man to whom Luke addresses his Gospel and Acts. He was probably a person of rank; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: the Thessalonians
senses.note: The people of Thessalonica, the chief city of Macedonia on the Via Egnatia. Paul founded a church there and wrote two letters to it; Aristarchus and Secundus came from the city.

senses.name: Thessalonica
senses.note: A port city and capital of the Roman province of Macedonia, in northern Greece; the Philippian believers sent Paul help while he was there.

senses.name: Theudas
senses.note: A man who claimed to be someone great and gathered about 400 followers before he was killed and they scattered; Gamaliel cites him as a warning. His date is uncertain.

senses.name: Thyatira
senses.note: A trading city in the province of Asia (western Turkey), known for its trade guilds and dyed cloth. Lydia came from there, and it is one of the seven churches addressed in Revelation.

senses.name: Thomas
senses.note: One of the Twelve, also called Didymus, meaning the Twin. He is ready to go with Jesus to Judea to die with him, and later doubts and then confesses the risen Jesus.

senses.name: Jairus
senses.note: A leader of a synagogue in Galilee who begged Jesus to heal his dying twelve-year-old daughter; Jesus raised her from death.

senses.name: Jacob
senses.note: Son of Isaac and grandson of Abraham, also named Israel; his twelve sons became the ancestors of Israel's tribes. Paul and the Samaritans alike look back to him as an ancestor, and his name can stand for the whole people.

senses.name: Jacob, father of Joseph
senses.note: Son of Matthan and father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: James son of Zebedee
senses.note: A Galilean fisherman, brother of John, called by Jesus to be one of the twelve apostles and one of the three closest to him. Herod Agrippa I had him executed with the sword.

senses.name: James son of Alphaeus
senses.note: One of the twelve apostles, named only in the lists of the Twelve. Some identify him with James the younger, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: James father of Judas
senses.note: The father of Judas, one of the twelve apostles (not Judas Iscariot); nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: James the Lord's brother
senses.note: A brother of Jesus who became a leader of the church in Jerusalem after the risen Jesus appeared to him. He spoke at the Jerusalem council, and the letter of James is traditionally linked with him.

senses.name: James the younger
senses.note: Son of a Mary who watched the crucifixion and went to the tomb, and brother of Joses. He may be the same as James son of Alphaeus, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Jambres
senses.note: Named with Jannes as opponents of Moses. Jewish tradition gave these names to Pharaoh's magicians, who are unnamed in Exodus.

senses.name: Jannai
senses.note: Named in Luke's genealogy of Jesus as an ancestor a few generations before Joseph; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Jannes
senses.note: Named with Jambres as an opponent of Moses, according to Jewish tradition one of Pharaoh's magicians; Exodus does not name them.

senses.name: Jared
senses.note: A descendant of Seth and the father of Enoch, named in Luke's genealogy of Jesus.

senses.name: Jason
senses.note: A Jewish believer with Paul when he wrote Romans, who sends greetings. He may be the Jason who hosted Paul in Thessalonica, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Jason of Thessalonica
senses.note: A believer in Thessalonica who hosted Paul and Silas. When a mob could not find them, it dragged Jason before the city officials, who made him post a bond.

senses.name: Idumea
senses.note: The Greek and Roman name for the region south of Judea, settled by descendants of the Edomites; Herod the Great's family came from there.

senses.name: Jezebel
senses.note: A woman in the church at Thyatira who claimed to be a prophet and led believers into immorality and idol food. Revelation probably calls her by the name of King Ahab's idolatrous queen.

senses.name: Hierapolis
senses.note: A city in the Lycus valley of Asia Minor, near Laodicea and Colossae, where Epaphras also worked for the believers.

senses.name: Jeremiah
senses.note: A prophet of Judah around 627 to 586 BC who warned of Jerusalem's fall to Babylon. Matthew cites words spoken through him as fulfilled.

senses.name: Jericho
senses.note: An ancient oasis town in the Jordan valley north of the Dead Sea, about 25 km north-east of Jerusalem. Its walls fell before Israel; Jesus healed a blind man and met Zacchaeus there.

senses.name: Jerusalem
senses.note: The chief city of Judea and site of the temple, where Jews went up for the great festivals. Much of Jesus' ministry in John takes place there during the feasts.

senses.name: the people of Jerusalem
senses.note: Residents of Jerusalem, the city of the temple and the centre of Jewish religious life. Some of them wonder whether Jesus is the one the authorities want to kill.

senses.name: Jerusalem
senses.note: The chief city of Judea and site of the temple, home of the first church. Paul was taking a collection from the Gentile churches to its poor believers.

senses.name: Jesse
senses.note: A man of Bethlehem, grandson of Ruth and Boaz and father of King David. Isaiah's phrase 'root of Jesse' refers to a promised king from his line.

senses.name: Jephthah
senses.note: A judge of Israel from Gilead who led Israel against the Ammonites. Hebrews lists him among those who acted by faith.

senses.name: Jechoniah
senses.note: A king of Judah, also called Jehoiachin, who was taken into exile in Babylon. Matthew lists him in Jesus' genealogy at the turning point of the deportation.

senses.name: Iconium
senses.note: A city in south-central Asia Minor (modern Konya, Turkey), in the Roman province of Galatia. Paul and Barnabas preached there and were driven out by opposition.

senses.name: Illyricum
senses.note: A Roman province on the eastern shore of the Adriatic Sea, roughly the western Balkans. Paul names it as the limit of his preaching from Jerusalem.

senses.name: Joppa
senses.note: An old port town on the Mediterranean coast of Judea, modern Jaffa beside Tel Aviv. Peter raised Tabitha there and, while staying at the house of Simon the tanner, saw the vision that led him to Cornelius.

senses.name: the Jordan River
senses.note: The river running from the Sea of Galilee south to the Dead Sea, the main river of Israel. John the Baptist baptized along it, at a Bethany on its east side.

senses.name: Judah
senses.note: The southern region of the land of Israel, once the territory of the tribe of Judah, including Bethlehem and the hill country around Jerusalem.

senses.name: Judea
senses.note: The southern region of the land of Israel around Jerusalem, under direct Roman rule in Jesus' day. Jesus travels between Judea and Galilee, and Paul speaks of unbelievers there opposing him.

senses.name: the Jews
senses.note: The Jewish people. Paul warns Titus against Jewish myths taught in Crete, probably speculative stories built on the Scriptures.

senses.name: the Jews
senses.note: Here the word describes living by Jewish customs and the law of Moses. Paul rebukes Peter for pressing Gentiles to live that way when he himself did not.

senses.name: the Jews
senses.note: The Jewish people, descendants of Israel who keep the law of Moses. In John the word often means the religious authorities in Jerusalem who oppose Jesus, and sometimes Judeans or Jewish crowds generally; Paul pairs Jew and Greek to cover all humanity.

senses.name: Judaism
senses.note: The Jewish way of life, with its law, customs and traditions of the ancestors. Paul describes his zeal in it before he came to follow Christ.

senses.name: Judah
senses.note: The fourth son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the tribe of Judah. By Tamar he was the father of Perez and Zerah, and Matthew traces the line of David and Jesus through him.

senses.name: Judas Iscariot
senses.note: Judas son of Simon Iscariot, one of the Twelve disciples, who betrayed Jesus to the authorities.

senses.name: Judas son of James
senses.note: One of the Twelve apostles, called Judas son of James to tell him apart from Judas Iscariot, who is named beside him in Luke's list. He is probably the same as Thaddaeus in Matthew and Mark.

senses.name: Judah
senses.note: A man named in Luke's genealogy of Jesus between Simeon and Joseph, several generations after David; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: the tribe of Judah
senses.note: The tribe descended from Judah, son of Jacob, and later the southern kingdom named after it. David came from this tribe, and Jesus is traced to it.

senses.name: Judas Barsabbas
senses.note: A leader and prophet in the Jerusalem church, also called Barsabbas, chosen with Silas to carry the apostles' letter to the believers in Antioch.

senses.name: Judas the Galilean
senses.note: A Jewish rebel who led a revolt at the time of a Roman census, around AD 6. Gamaliel mentions him as a leader whose movement came to nothing after he died.

senses.name: Judas of Straight Street
senses.note: A man in Damascus at whose house, on the street called Straight, Saul of Tarsus stayed after his vision; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Judas, brother of Jesus
senses.note: One of the brothers of Jesus named by the people of Nazareth. He is probably the Jude who wrote the letter of Jude.

senses.name: Jude
senses.note: The writer of the letter of Jude, who calls himself a brother of James. He is usually taken to be Judas, one of the brothers of Jesus.

senses.name: Joda
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy, after the exile; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Julia
senses.note: A woman in the church in Rome whom Paul greets, perhaps the wife or sister of Philologus. Nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Julius
senses.note: A Roman centurion of the Augustan cohort who escorted Paul and other prisoners to Rome. He treated Paul kindly, letting him visit friends at Sidon.

senses.name: Junia
senses.note: A Jewish believer, probably a woman and possibly Andronicus's wife, who had been in prison with Paul and became a believer before him; Paul calls the pair prominent among the apostles.

senses.name: Titius Justus
senses.note: A God-fearing Gentile in Corinth whose house was next to the synagogue; Paul taught from there after leaving the synagogue.

senses.name: Jesus called Justus
senses.note: A Jewish believer with Paul when he wrote Colossians, one of the few Jewish co-workers who had been a comfort to him. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Joseph Barsabbas, called Justus
senses.note: A follower of Jesus from the time of John's baptism, put forward with Matthias to replace Judas among the Twelve. The lot fell on Matthias.

senses.name: Titius Justus
senses.note: A Gentile who worshipped God in Corinth. Paul moved his teaching to his house, next door to the synagogue, after opposition there.

senses.name: Isaac
senses.note: Son of Abraham and Sarah, husband of Rebecca and father of Jacob and Esau. He is the son through whom God's promise to Abraham was to continue.

senses.name: the tribe of Issachar
senses.note: The Israelite tribe descended from Jacob's son Issachar, listed among the twelve tribes sealed in Revelation.

senses.name: Judas Iscariot
senses.note: One of the Twelve, who betrayed Jesus to the chief priests. The meaning of Iscariot is uncertain; it may mean 'man of Kerioth'.

senses.name: Iscariot
senses.note: The surname of Judas, son of Simon, the disciple who betrayed Jesus. Its meaning is uncertain; it may mean 'man from Kerioth'.

senses.name: Israel
senses.note: The people descended from Jacob, whom God renamed Israel, and the nation formed from his twelve sons' tribes. In Romans Paul wrestles with why much of Israel has not believed in Jesus as the Messiah.

senses.name: Israelites
senses.note: Members of the people of Israel, descended from Jacob, who was also named Israel. Paul counts himself among them, and Jesus calls Nathanael a true Israelite.

senses.name: Italy
senses.note: The Roman homeland in the central Mediterranean, with Rome as its capital. Aquila and Priscilla had come from there, Paul was sent there as a prisoner, and believers from Italy send greetings in Hebrews.

senses.name: the Italian Cohort
senses.note: A Roman auxiliary unit, probably first recruited from Roman citizens in Italy, stationed at Caesarea; Cornelius was a centurion in it.

senses.name: Ituraea
senses.note: A region north-east of Galilee, around the Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon mountains, ruled by Philip the tetrarch together with Trachonitis.

senses.name: Jotham
senses.note: Son of Uzziah and king of Judah in the eighth century BC. He is listed in Matthew's family line of Jesus as the father of Ahaz.

senses.name: Joanna
senses.note: The wife of Chuza, a steward of Herod Antipas. She was among the women who supported Jesus from their own means and who found the tomb empty.

senses.name: Joanan
senses.note: Named in Luke's genealogy of Jesus as the son of Rhesa and grandson of Zerubbabel; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: John son of Zebedee
senses.note: One of the Twelve, brother of James and son of Zebedee, a fisherman called by Jesus. With Peter and James he was in Jesus' inner circle, and later a leader of the Jerusalem church.

senses.name: John Mark
senses.note: Also called Mark; son of a Mary whose Jerusalem house was a meeting place for believers. He set out with Barnabas and Paul but turned back at Perga, which later caused Paul and Barnabas to part.

senses.name: John (of the high priest's family)
senses.note: A member of the high priest's family who sat with Annas and Caiaphas when Peter and John were questioned. Nothing more is known of him for certain.

senses.name: John (of Revelation)
senses.note: The servant of Jesus who received the visions of Revelation while on the island of Patmos and wrote them to seven churches in the province of Asia. Early tradition identifies him with John son of Zebedee; this is debated.

senses.name: John, father of Simon Peter
senses.note: The father of Simon Peter and Andrew, named when Jesus first meets Simon; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: John the Baptist
senses.note: A prophet sent by God who baptized people near the Jordan River and pointed his own disciples to Jesus. He was later imprisoned and executed by Herod Antipas; he is not the same person as John the apostle.

senses.name: Job
senses.note: The man of the book of Job, who lost his wealth, children and health yet held on to God, and whom God later restored.

senses.name: Joel
senses.note: An Israelite prophet whose book foretells God pouring out his Spirit on all people. Peter quotes him at Pentecost.

senses.name: Jonam
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy, between David and Joseph; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Jonah
senses.note: The prophet sent to preach to Nineveh, who spent three days inside a great fish. Jesus pointed to him as the only sign his generation would be given.

senses.name: Joram
senses.note: A king of Judah, also called Jehoram, son of Jehoshaphat. Matthew's list passes from him to Uzziah, leaving out several kings named in Kings and Chronicles.

senses.name: Jorim
senses.note: Named in Luke's genealogy of Jesus as an ancestor between David and the exile; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Jehoshaphat
senses.note: A king of Judah in the ninth century BC, son of Asa; he is listed among the ancestors of Jesus.

senses.name: Joshua
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus listed in Luke's genealogy, son of Eliezer, in the line between David and the exile; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Joses, brother of Jesus
senses.note: One of the brothers of Jesus named by the people of Nazareth, along with James, Judas and Simon.

senses.name: Joses, son of Mary
senses.note: A son of one of the women named Mary who watched the crucifixion and burial, and brother of James the younger. He may be the same as the brother of Jesus of that name, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Joseph, son of Jacob
senses.note: One of the twelve sons of Jacob, the patriarch. Jacob gave him a piece of land near Shechem, close to where the Samaritan town of Sychar later stood.

senses.name: the tribe of Joseph
senses.note: In Revelation's list of the sealed tribes, the tribe named after Joseph, Jacob's son; Manasseh, one of his sons, is listed separately.

senses.name: Joseph called Barsabbas
senses.note: Also known as Justus; one of the two men put forward to replace Judas among the Twelve, having followed Jesus from the start. The lot fell to Matthias.

senses.name: Joseph called Barnabas
senses.note: A Levite from Cyprus whom the apostles named Barnabas, "one who encourages". He sold a field and gave the money to the apostles, and later worked alongside Paul.

senses.name: Joseph of Arimathea
senses.note: A rich member of the council from the town of Arimathea and a secret disciple of Jesus, who asked Pilate for Jesus' body and laid it in his own new rock tomb.

senses.name: Joseph, brother of Jesus
senses.note: Named among the brothers of Jesus by the people of his home town. Mark gives the same name in the form Joses. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Joseph, son of Mary
senses.note: The brother of James, whose mother Mary watched the crucifixion. He may be the same as the Joseph named among Jesus' brothers, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Joseph, son of Jannai
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's family line, a few generations before Joseph the husband of Mary. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Joseph, son of Jonam
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's family line, between David and Zerubbabel. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Joseph
senses.note: The husband of Mary, the mother of Jesus, and a descendant of David. Living in Nazareth, he was known as Jesus' father; Matthew describes him as a righteous man guided by dreams.

senses.name: Josech
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus after the exile, listed in Luke's genealogy; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Josiah
senses.note: A king of Judah in the seventh century BC, remembered for his reforms of worship; he is listed among the ancestors of Jesus.

senses.name: Caiaphas
senses.note: The Jewish high priest in Jerusalem from about AD 18 to 36, son-in-law of Annas. He urged that Jesus should die for the nation.

senses.name: Cain
senses.note: The first son of Adam and Eve, who murdered his brother Abel out of jealousy when God accepted Abel's offering. The New Testament holds him up as a warning.

senses.name: Cainan, son of Arphaxad
senses.note: An ancestor of Abraham in Luke's genealogy, between Arphaxad and Shelah; he appears in the Greek Old Testament but not in the Hebrew text of Genesis.

senses.name: Cainan, son of Enos
senses.note: Son of Enos and grandson of Seth, called Kenan in Genesis 5, listed in Luke's genealogy of Jesus.

senses.name: the emperor
senses.note: The Roman emperor, probably Nero at the time. His household included slaves and freed staff serving him, some of whom were believers sending greetings.

senses.name: Caesar Augustus
senses.note: The first Roman emperor, who ruled from 27 BC to AD 14. His order for a census brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem.

senses.name: Tiberius Caesar
senses.note: The Roman emperor from AD 14 to 37, ruling when Jesus taught and was crucified. Questions about paying him tax and loyalty to him shaped the charges against Jesus.

senses.name: Caesar
senses.note: The Roman emperor; in Paul's travels this is probably Claudius and later Nero. Paul was accused of defying his decrees, and as a Roman citizen Paul appealed to have his case heard by him.

senses.name: Caesarea
senses.note: A port city on the Mediterranean coast built by Herod the Great, the seat of the Roman governors of Judea. Cornelius lives there, Philip settles there, and Paul is held there for two years.

senses.name: Caesarea Philippi
senses.note: A town near the springs of the Jordan at the foot of Mount Hermon, rebuilt by Herod's son Philip. Near it Jesus asks his disciples who people say he is.

senses.name: Alphaeus father of James
senses.note: Father of James, one of the twelve apostles; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Alphaeus father of Levi
senses.note: Father of Levi the tax collector, whom Jesus called to follow him; whether he is the same as the father of James is unknown.

senses.name: Fair Havens
senses.note: A small bay on the south coast of Crete, near the town of Lasea, where Paul's ship sheltered on the voyage to Rome.

senses.name: Cana
senses.note: A village in Galilee where Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding, his first sign, and later healed an official's son. Its exact site is uncertain, probably a few miles north of Nazareth.

senses.name: Simon the Zealot
senses.note: One of the twelve apostles, distinguished from Simon Peter by this title. It may mean he had belonged to the Jewish movement opposed to Roman rule, or simply that he was zealous; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Candace
senses.note: The title of the queens of the Ethiopians, the kingdom of Meroe on the upper Nile south of Egypt; the eunuch Philip met managed her treasury.

senses.name: Capernaum
senses.note: A fishing town on the north-west shore of the Sea of Galilee. Jesus made it a base for his work in Galilee; in John he heals an official's son there and teaches in its synagogue.

senses.name: Cappadocia
senses.note: A Roman province in central Asia Minor (modern Turkey). It is one of the regions where the believers addressed in 1 Peter lived.

senses.name: Carpus
senses.note: A believer at Troas with whom Paul left his cloak; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Cenchreae
senses.note: The eastern port of Corinth on the Saronic Gulf in Greece. Phoebe, whom Paul commends, served the church there.

senses.name: the Kidron Valley
senses.note: The valley east of Jerusalem, between the city and the Mount of Olives; Jesus crossed it to the garden where he was arrested.

senses.name: Cephas
senses.note: The Aramaic name, meaning rock, that Jesus gave to Simon son of John; Peter is its Greek equivalent.

senses.name: Cilicia
senses.note: A region and Roman province in the south-east corner of Asia Minor, on the coast of modern Turkey. Paul's home city of Tarsus was there, and he strengthened churches in the area.

senses.name: Kish
senses.note: A man of the tribe of Benjamin, father of Saul, Israel's first king.

senses.name: Hagar
senses.note: Sarah's Egyptian slave woman, who bore Ishmael to Abraham. Paul uses her as a picture of the covenant from Mount Sinai and of slavery.

senses.name: Cauda
senses.note: A small island south of Crete, behind which Paul's storm-driven ship sheltered for a while.

senses.name: Claudia
senses.note: A believer in Rome who sends greetings to Timothy at the end of Paul's last letter; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Claudius
senses.note: Roman emperor from AD 41 to 54. A severe famine came in his reign, and around AD 49 he expelled Jews from Rome, which brought Aquila and Priscilla to Corinth.

senses.name: Claudius Lysias
senses.note: The Roman commander of the garrison in Jerusalem who rescued Paul from a mob and sent him under guard to Governor Felix in Caesarea with a letter.

senses.name: Cleopas
senses.note: One of two disciples walking to Emmaus on the day of the resurrection, who talked with the risen Jesus without recognising him at first.

senses.name: Clement
senses.note: A fellow worker of Paul at Philippi who had shared in his work for the gospel. Nothing more is known of him for certain.

senses.name: Clopas
senses.note: The husband of one of the women named Mary who stood near the cross; nothing more is certainly known of him. He may be the Cleopas who met Jesus on the road to Emmaus.

senses.name: Cnidus
senses.note: A port at the tip of a peninsula on the south-west coast of Asia Minor, passed on Paul's voyage to Rome.

senses.name: Amminadab
senses.note: Son of Ram and father of Nahshon, an ancestor of David in the tribe of Judah listed in Jesus' genealogy.

senses.name: Colossae
senses.note: A small city in the Lycus valley of Asia Minor (modern Turkey), near Laodicea and Hierapolis. The church there, apparently founded through Epaphras, received this letter.

senses.name: Korah
senses.note: A Levite, son of Izhar, who led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness and perished with his followers. Jude uses him as a warning.

senses.name: the Corinthians
senses.note: The people of Corinth, a large trading city in southern Greece, where Paul founded a church and to whose believers he wrote at least two letters.

senses.name: Corinth
senses.note: A large, wealthy port city in southern Greece and capital of the Roman province of Achaia. Paul founded a church there, stayed about eighteen months, and later wrote at least two letters to it.

senses.name: Cornelius
senses.note: A Roman centurion at Caesarea who feared God. After an angel told him to send for Peter, he and his household heard the message and received the Holy Spirit, among the first Gentiles to do so.

senses.name: Quartus
senses.note: A believer with Paul in Corinth who sends greetings to Rome; Paul calls him a brother. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Ampliatus
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets as dear to him in the Lord; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Cretans
senses.note: The people of Crete, a large island south of Greece. Some were present at Pentecost, and Paul quotes a Cretan poet's harsh saying about them in his letter to Titus.

senses.name: Crescens
senses.note: A companion of Paul who had gone to Galatia at the time of Paul's last imprisonment; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Crete
senses.note: A large island in the Mediterranean south of Greece. Paul's ship sheltered along its south coast on the way to Rome, and Paul later left Titus there to organize the churches.

senses.name: Crispus
senses.note: The leader of the synagogue in Corinth, who came to believe in the Lord with all his household. Paul baptized him himself.

senses.name: Amphipolis
senses.note: A city in Macedonia in northern Greece, on the Roman road east of Thessalonica, through which Paul and Silas passed.

senses.name: Cyprus
senses.note: The large island in the eastern Mediterranean; these verses speak of people from there, such as Barnabas and Mnason, among the early believers.

senses.name: Cyprus
senses.note: A large island in the eastern Mediterranean, the home of Barnabas. Paul and Barnabas preached there on their first journey, and later ships passed it on voyages to and from Syria.

senses.name: Cyrene
senses.note: A Greek city on the coast of North Africa, in modern Libya, with a large Jewish community. Simon, who carried Jesus' cross, came from there, and Cyrenian believers were among the first to preach to Gentiles in Antioch.

senses.name: Cyrene
senses.note: A Greek city in Libya, in North Africa, with a large Jewish community; visitors from its region were in Jerusalem at Pentecost.

senses.name: Quirinius
senses.note: A Roman governor of Syria whose census Luke links with the birth of Jesus. How this fits with the known dates of his governorship is debated.

senses.name: Cos
senses.note: A small Greek island off the south-west coast of Asia Minor, where Paul's ship stopped on the way to Jerusalem.

senses.name: Cosam
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy, in the generations after the exile. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Lazarus of Bethany
senses.note: The brother of Mary and Martha, living in the village of Bethany near Jerusalem. Jesus loved him, and after he died Jesus called him out of his tomb alive.

senses.name: Lazarus (in Jesus' story)
senses.note: The poor man covered with sores in Jesus' story of the rich man and Lazarus, who lay at the rich man's gate and after death was comforted beside Abraham.

senses.name: Lamech
senses.note: Son of Methuselah and father of Noah, named in Luke's genealogy of Jesus that runs back to Adam.

senses.name: Laodicea
senses.note: A wealthy city in the Lycus valley of Asia Minor (modern Turkey), near Colossae and Hierapolis. Paul asks the Colossians to share letters with the church there.

senses.name: Laodicea
senses.note: A wealthy city in the Lycus valley of Asia Minor, about ten miles from Colossae. Paul asks that letters be exchanged between the churches there; the letter from Laodicea is not known to survive.

senses.name: Lasea
senses.note: A town on the south coast of Crete near Fair Havens, where Paul's ship sheltered on the voyage to Rome.

senses.name: Abaddon
senses.note: The name of the angel of the abyss who rules the locusts in John's vision. The Hebrew name means destruction, and its Greek equivalent is Apollyon, destroyer.

senses.name: Amon
senses.note: A king of Judah, son of Manasseh and father of Josiah, who reigned only two years before being assassinated. Many Greek manuscripts of Matthew spell his name Amos.

senses.name: Amos
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus listed in Luke's genealogy, son of Nahum; not the prophet. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Levi son of Jacob
senses.note: The third son of Jacob and Leah and ancestor of the tribe of Levi, from which Israel's priests came. Hebrews contrasts the Levitical priests with Melchizedek.

senses.name: Levi son of Melchi
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy, father of Matthat and son of Melchi; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Levi son of Simeon
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy, between David and the exile, father of Matthat and son of Simeon; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Levi the tax collector
senses.note: A tax collector, son of Alphaeus, whom Jesus called to follow him at his tax booth. He is usually identified with Matthew.

senses.name: Levi
senses.note: A tax collector, son of Alphaeus, whom Jesus called to follow him; Matthew's Gospel calls him Matthew.

senses.name: Levites
senses.note: Members of the tribe of Levi who assisted the priests in the temple at Jerusalem. The Jewish leaders sent priests and Levites to question John the Baptist.

senses.name: the Levites
senses.note: The priestly tribe descended from Levi; Israel's priests came from it. Hebrews argues that their priesthood could not bring things to completion.

senses.name: the Freedmen
senses.note: A synagogue in Jerusalem probably made up of freed slaves or their descendants; some of its members disputed with Stephen.

senses.name: Libya
senses.note: The region of north Africa west of Egypt; Cyrene was its chief city. Jews from there were in Jerusalem at Pentecost.

senses.name: Fair Havens
senses.note: A small bay on the south coast of Crete, near the town of Lasea, where Paul's ship sheltered before the storm.

senses.name: Linus
senses.note: A believer in Rome who sends greetings to Timothy. Early tradition names a Linus as an early leader of the Roman church.

senses.name: Luke
senses.note: A doctor and close companion of Paul who sends greetings to Colossae; traditionally the author of the Gospel of Luke and Acts.

senses.name: Lucius
senses.note: A Jewish believer with Paul in Corinth who sends greetings to Rome. He may be Lucius of Cyrene from Antioch, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Lucius of Cyrene
senses.note: One of the prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch when Barnabas and Saul were sent out. He came from Cyrene in North Africa.

senses.name: Lydda
senses.note: A town on the coastal plain about 18 kilometres (11 miles) south-east of Joppa, modern Lod. Peter healed Aeneas there.

senses.name: Lydia
senses.note: A trader in purple cloth from Thyatira who worshiped God and lived at Philippi. She believed Paul's message, was baptized, and hosted Paul and his companions in her house.

senses.name: Lycaonia
senses.note: A region in south-central Asia Minor (modern Turkey) containing the towns of Lystra and Derbe, where Paul and Barnabas preached.

senses.name: Lycaonian
senses.note: The local language of Lycaonia, a region in south-central Asia Minor around Lystra and Derbe. The crowd at Lystra cried out in it, so Paul and Barnabas did not at first grasp what was happening.

senses.name: Lycia
senses.note: A region on the south-west coast of Asia Minor (modern Turkey). At its port of Myra, Paul and his guards changed ships on the voyage to Rome.

senses.name: Lysanias
senses.note: The ruler (tetrarch) of Abilene, a small territory north-west of Damascus, when John the Baptist began his work.

senses.name: Claudius Lysias
senses.note: The Roman tribune commanding the garrison in Jerusalem who rescued Paul from a mob and sent him under guard to Governor Felix in Caesarea.

senses.name: Lystra
senses.note: A small Roman colony in Lycaonia, in south-central Asia Minor (modern Turkey). The crowd there takes Paul and Barnabas for gods, then Paul is stoned; Timothy comes from there.

senses.name: Lois
senses.note: Timothy's grandmother, mother of Eunice. Paul remembers the sincere faith that lived first in her.

senses.name: Lot
senses.note: Abraham's nephew, who settled in the city of Sodom. Peter describes him as a righteous man distressed by the wickedness around him, whom God rescued when Sodom was destroyed.

senses.name: Maath
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy, after the exile; he is known only from this list.

senses.name: Magadan
senses.note: A place on the Sea of Galilee where Jesus went by boat after feeding the four thousand. The location is uncertain; it may be the same as Magdala.

senses.name: Mary Magdalene
senses.note: A woman from Magdala in Galilee whom Jesus freed from seven demons. She followed and supported him, watched the crucifixion, and was the first to see him risen.

senses.name: Magog
senses.note: In Ezekiel, the land of Gog; in Revelation, Gog and Magog stand for the nations Satan gathers for a last war against God's people.

senses.name: Midian
senses.note: A land east of the Gulf of Aqaba in north-west Arabia, home of the Midianites, where Moses lived as a foreigner after fleeing Egypt.

senses.name: Methuselah
senses.note: Son of Enoch and grandfather of Noah, listed in Jesus' genealogy; Genesis gives him the longest life recorded, 969 years.

senses.name: Menna
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's family line, a few generations after David. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Macedonia
senses.note: The Roman province in northern Greece, including Philippi and Thessalonica. Paul founded churches there, and they gave generously to the poor believers in Jerusalem.

senses.name: the Macedonians
senses.note: People of Macedonia, the Roman province in northern Greece. Several of Paul's companions, such as Aristarchus of Thessalonica, were Macedonians, and Paul held up the Macedonian churches' giving to the Corinthians.

senses.name: Mahalalel
senses.note: A descendant of Seth before the flood and father of Jared, named in Luke's family line of Jesus.

senses.name: Malchus
senses.note: The high priest's slave whose ear Simon Peter cut off when Jesus was arrested.

senses.name: Manaen
senses.note: A prophet or teacher in the church at Antioch who had grown up with Herod Antipas.

senses.name: Manasseh
senses.note: A king of Judah in the seventh century BC, son of Hezekiah and grandfather of Josiah, known for his long and idolatrous reign; listed among the ancestors of Jesus.

senses.name: the tribe of Manasseh
senses.note: The Israelite tribe descended from Manasseh, son of Joseph, named among the tribes sealed in Revelation.

senses.name: Martha
senses.note: Sister of Mary and Lazarus in Bethany near Jerusalem, a family Jesus loved. When Lazarus died she met Jesus on the road and spoke with him about the resurrection.

senses.name: Mary of Bethany
senses.note: Sister of Martha and Lazarus, living in the village of Bethany near Jerusalem, who stayed in the house while Martha went to meet Jesus.

senses.name: Mary, mother of Jesus
senses.note: A young woman engaged to Joseph of Nazareth who became pregnant through the Holy Spirit and gave birth to Jesus.

senses.name: Mary Magdalene
senses.note: A woman from Magdala in Galilee whom Jesus freed from seven demons. She followed and supported him, watched the crucifixion, and was the first to see him risen.

senses.name: Mary, mother of James and Joses
senses.note: A follower of Jesus from Galilee, often called 'the other Mary', who watched the crucifixion and burial and went to the tomb with Mary Magdalene; her sons James and Joses were known to the first readers.

senses.name: Mary, wife of Clopas
senses.note: A woman who stood near the cross with the mother of Jesus and Mary Magdalene. She may be the same as Mary the mother of James and Joses, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Mary, mother of John Mark
senses.note: A believer in Jerusalem whose house was a meeting place for the church; Peter went there after his release from prison. Her son was John Mark.

senses.name: Mary of Bethany
senses.note: Sister of Martha and Lazarus, living in the village of Bethany near Jerusalem. She anointed Jesus with perfume and met him in grief after Lazarus died.

senses.name: Mary in Rome
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets for her hard work on the church's behalf; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Mary the mother of Jesus
senses.note: A young woman of Nazareth engaged to Joseph, to whom the angel Gabriel announced the birth of Jesus. She was with the disciples in Jerusalem after the resurrection.

senses.name: Mary Magdalene
senses.note: A follower of Jesus, probably from Magdala on the Sea of Galilee. She watched his burial and was the first to see him risen; in Matthew another Mary is with her at the tomb.

senses.name: Mark
senses.note: John Mark, cousin of Barnabas, who travelled with Paul and was later with him in his imprisonment. Peter calls him his son, probably meaning spiritual son; early tradition links him with the Gospel of Mark.

senses.name: Matthew
senses.note: A tax collector whom Jesus called to follow him and who became one of the twelve apostles. Mark and Luke call the tax collector Levi; early tradition names Matthew as the author of the first Gospel.

senses.name: Matthan
senses.note: Grandfather of Joseph, the husband of Mary, in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Matthat, son of Levi
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's family line, grandfather of Joseph the husband of Mary. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Matthat, father of Jorim
senses.note: An earlier ancestor of Jesus in Luke's family line, between David and Zerubbabel, also called son of Levi. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Matthias
senses.note: A disciple who had followed Jesus from his baptism; he was chosen by lot to take Judas Iscariot's place among the Twelve. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Mattatha
senses.note: A son of Nathan son of David, listed in Luke's genealogy of Jesus. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Mattathias son of Amos
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy, son of Amos; he is known only from this list.

senses.name: Mattathias son of Semein
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy, father of Maath and son of Semein; he is known only from this list.

senses.name: Melea
senses.note: A man named in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, a few generations after David's son Nathan; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Malta
senses.note: An island south of Sicily where Paul's ship was wrecked on the way to Rome.

senses.name: Melchi, son of Jannai
senses.note: An ancestor of Joseph in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, a few generations before Joseph. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Melchi, son of Addi
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy, in the generations after the exile. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Melchizedek
senses.note: King of Salem and priest of God Most High, who blessed Abraham and received a tenth from him. Hebrews, following Psalm 110, presents Jesus as a priest of his order.

senses.name: Mesopotamia
senses.note: The land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, roughly modern Iraq. Abraham lived there before moving to Haran, and Jews from there were in Jerusalem at Pentecost.

senses.name: Medes
senses.note: A people of the Iranian plateau, in what is now north-western Iran. Jews from that region were in Jerusalem at Pentecost and heard the apostles in their own language.

senses.name: Miletus
senses.note: A port city on the west coast of Asia Minor (modern Turkey), south of Ephesus. Paul meets the Ephesian elders there for a farewell, and later leaves Trophimus there ill.

senses.name: Mitylene
senses.note: The main city of the island of Lesbos, off the west coast of what is now Turkey, where Paul's ship stopped on his way to Jerusalem.

senses.name: Michael
senses.note: An archangel, the leader of angels who fights the dragon in Revelation and who disputed with the devil over the body of Moses.

senses.name: Mnason
senses.note: A disciple from Cyprus, a believer from the early days, who gave Paul and his companions lodging on the way to Jerusalem.

senses.name: Moloch
senses.note: A god of the Ammonites and other neighbours of Israel, linked with child sacrifice. Stephen quotes Amos to say Israel carried his shrine in the wilderness.

senses.name: Myra
senses.note: A port in Lycia on the southern coast of Asia Minor, where Paul, as a prisoner, was transferred to a grain ship bound for Italy.

senses.name: Mysia
senses.note: A region in the north-west of Asia Minor (modern Turkey). Paul and his companions pass by it on their way down to Troas when the Spirit stops them going on into Bithynia.

senses.name: Moses
senses.note: The Israelite leader who brought Israel out of Egypt and through whom God gave the law at Sinai. In these passages he stands for the law itself, and his writings are said to point to Jesus.

senses.name: Nahshon
senses.note: A leader of the tribe of Judah in Moses' time, son of Amminadab and father of Salmon; an ancestor of David and of Jesus.

senses.name: Naggai
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy, in the generations after the exile. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Nazareth
senses.note: A small village in the hills of Galilee where Jesus grew up and later taught in the synagogue.

senses.name: Nazareth
senses.note: A small town in the hills of lower Galilee where Mary and Joseph lived and where Jesus grew up, so that he was known as Jesus of Nazareth.

senses.name: Nazareth
senses.note: A small village in the hills of Galilee where Jesus grew up. Nathanael's doubt that anything good could come from it reflects its obscurity.

senses.name: Nazareth
senses.note: The village in Galilee where Jesus grew up. People called him the Nazarene, that is, the man from Nazareth, to say where he came from.

senses.name: the Nazarenes
senses.note: A name opponents used for Jesus' followers, after his home town of Nazareth; Paul's accusers call him a ringleader of this sect.

senses.name: Jesus of Nazareth
senses.note: A common way of naming Jesus by his home town in Galilee. It appears in the mouths of crowds, soldiers, apostles and on the notice Pilate placed on the cross.

senses.name: Nathan son of David
senses.note: A son of David born in Jerusalem, through whom Luke traces Jesus' ancestry, rather than through Solomon.

senses.name: Nathanael
senses.note: A man from Cana in Galilee whom Philip brought to Jesus. At first doubtful about Nazareth, he declared Jesus Son of God and King of Israel. He is often thought to be the Bartholomew of the other Gospels, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Nain
senses.note: A village in Galilee, south-east of Nazareth, where Jesus raised a widow's only son as he was being carried out for burial.

senses.name: Nahum
senses.note: A man named in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, son of Esli and father of Amos; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Narcissus
senses.note: The head of a household in Rome, some of whose members were believers. He himself is not greeted and was probably not a believer, or no longer living; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Nahor
senses.note: The father of Terah and grandfather of Abraham, named in Luke's genealogy of Jesus.

senses.name: Neapolis
senses.note: The port of Philippi in Macedonia, modern Kavala in northern Greece, where Paul first landed in Europe.

senses.name: Naaman
senses.note: An army commander from Syria (Aram) whom Elisha healed of a skin disease. Jesus cites him as a foreigner who received God's help.

senses.name: Naphtali
senses.note: The territory of the tribe of Naphtali, west of the Sea of Galilee. Matthew links Jesus' move to Capernaum with Isaiah's promise of light for this region.

senses.name: Naphtali
senses.note: The tribe descended from Jacob's son Naphtali, one of the twelve tribes of Israel from which people are sealed in Revelation.

senses.name: Nereus
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets along with his sister; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Neri
senses.note: A man named in Luke's genealogy of Jesus as the father of Shealtiel; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Simeon called Niger
senses.note: One of the prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch. Niger, a Latin nickname meaning black, may point to an African origin; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Nicanor
senses.note: One of the seven men chosen in Jerusalem to oversee the daily distribution to widows; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Nicodemus
senses.note: A Pharisee and member of the Jewish ruling council who came to Jesus at night to question him. He later spoke up for a fair hearing for Jesus and helped bury him.

senses.name: the Nicolaitans
senses.note: A group in the churches of Ephesus and Pergamum whose teaching and practices Jesus condemns; little is known of them, though they seem to have allowed compromise with idolatry and immorality.

senses.name: Nicolaus
senses.note: A convert to Judaism from Antioch, one of the seven men chosen to oversee the daily distribution of food in the Jerusalem church.

senses.name: Nicopolis
senses.note: A city where Paul planned to spend the winter, most likely the Nicopolis in Epirus on the west coast of Greece.

senses.name: the people of Nineveh
senses.note: The inhabitants of the Assyrian capital, who repented when Jonah preached to them. Jesus contrasts them with his own generation.

senses.name: the people of Nineveh
senses.note: The inhabitants of Nineveh, the Assyrian capital, who turned from their sins when Jonah preached. Jesus says they will condemn his own generation.

senses.name: Nympha
senses.note: A believer in or near Laodicea in whose house a church met. Paul sends her greetings; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Noah
senses.note: The son of Lamech and father of Shem, Ham and Japheth. God kept him and his family safe in the ark through the flood; Peter cites him as an example of rescue amid judgment.

senses.name: Uzziah
senses.note: A king of Judah in the eighth century BC, also called Azariah, who reigned for many years. He is listed in Matthew's family line of Jesus as the father of Jotham.

senses.name: Olympas
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets along with Philologus, Julia and others; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Ananias (husband of Sapphira)
senses.note: A member of the early Jerusalem church who sold land with his wife Sapphira, kept back part of the price while claiming to give it all, and fell dead when Peter confronted him.

senses.name: Ananias of Damascus
senses.note: A devout Jewish disciple in Damascus whom the Lord sent to Saul after his encounter on the road. He laid hands on Saul, whose sight returned.

senses.name: Ananias the high priest
senses.note: The high priest in Jerusalem around AD 47 to 59, son of Nedebaeus. He ordered Paul struck at his hearing and later brought charges against him before the governor Felix.

senses.name: Onesimus
senses.note: A believer from Colossae, sent with Tychicus to bring news of Paul. He is probably the runaway slave on whose behalf Paul wrote to Philemon.

senses.name: Onesiphorus
senses.note: A believer, probably from Ephesus, who searched for Paul in Rome and often cheered him in prison; Paul sends greetings to his household.

senses.name: Urbanus
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets as a co-worker in Christ. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Uriah
senses.note: A Hittite soldier in David's army whose wife Bathsheba David took; David then had Uriah killed. Matthew names Solomon's mother as Uriah's wife.

senses.name: Pamphylia
senses.note: A coastal region on the south coast of Asia Minor (modern Turkey), with Perga and Attalia among its towns. Paul and Barnabas passed through it, and John Mark left them there.

senses.name: Parthians
senses.note: People from the Parthian empire east of the Euphrates, in modern Iran and Iraq. Jews from there heard the apostles speak in their own language at Pentecost.

senses.name: Parmenas
senses.note: One of the seven men chosen in Jerusalem to oversee the daily distribution of food; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Patara
senses.note: A port city in Lycia on the south-west coast of Asia Minor, where Paul changed ships for Phoenicia.

senses.name: Patmos
senses.note: A small island in the Aegean Sea off the west coast of Asia Minor, where John received the visions of Revelation.

senses.name: Patrobas
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Paul
senses.note: A Jewish follower of Jesus, formerly a Pharisee who persecuted the church, who became an apostle to the Gentiles. He wrote the letters that open with his name and travelled widely founding churches.

senses.name: Sergius Paulus
senses.note: The Roman proconsul (governor) of Cyprus, based at Paphos, who sent for Barnabas and Saul to hear their message and came to believe after the magician Bar-Jesus was struck blind.

senses.name: Paphos
senses.note: The Roman capital of Cyprus, on the island's west coast, where Paul met the proconsul Sergius Paulus and the magician Bar-Jesus.

senses.name: Pergamum
senses.note: A city in the Roman province of Asia, in western Asia Minor, an old royal capital with famous temples. It received one of the seven messages in Revelation.

senses.name: Perga
senses.note: A city of Pamphylia near the southern coast of Asia Minor. Paul and Barnabas passed through it on their first journey; John Mark left them there.

senses.name: Andrew
senses.note: A fisherman from Bethsaida, brother of Simon Peter and one of the Twelve. He had followed John the Baptist, and he brought his brother to Jesus.

senses.name: Persis
senses.note: A woman in the church in Rome whom Paul greets as dear and as one who has worked hard in the Lord. Nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Simon Peter
senses.note: Simon son of John, a fisherman from Bethsaida and brother of Andrew, whom Jesus named Cephas or Peter, meaning "rock". He became a leading apostle, and two New Testament letters bear his name.

senses.name: Andronicus
senses.note: A Jewish believer in Rome, greeted with Junia, who had been in prison with Paul and became a believer before him. They were well known among the apostles; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Pilate
senses.note: Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor (prefect) of Judea from about AD 26 to 36. He questioned Jesus, found no case against him, yet handed him over to be crucified.

senses.name: Pisidia
senses.note: A mountainous region in southern Asia Minor (modern Turkey), north of Pamphylia. Paul and Barnabas passed through it, preaching at Antioch near Pisidia.

senses.name: Neapolis
