senses.note: A port town in Macedonia, the harbour of Philippi, where Paul first landed in Europe; modern Kavala in Greece.

senses.name: Pontus
senses.note: A region of northern Asia Minor (modern Turkey) along the Black Sea, where Aquila was born.

senses.name: Pontius Pilate
senses.note: The Roman governor of Judea from about AD 26 to 36, who sentenced Jesus to crucifixion.

senses.name: Pontus
senses.note: A Roman region on the southern coast of the Black Sea in northern Asia Minor (modern Turkey), one of the areas where the believers Peter writes to were living.

senses.name: Publius
senses.note: The leading official of Malta, who welcomed Paul after the shipwreck. Paul healed his father of fever and dysentery.

senses.name: Porcius Festus
senses.note: The Roman governor of Judea who succeeded Felix around AD 59. He heard Paul's case and sent him to Rome after Paul appealed to Caesar.

senses.name: Puteoli
senses.note: A busy port on the Bay of Naples in Italy, modern Pozzuoli, where Paul landed and stayed a week with believers before going on to Rome.

senses.name: Pudens
senses.note: A believer in Rome who sent greetings to Timothy in Paul's last letter; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Prisca
senses.note: A Jewish believer, also called Priscilla, wife of Aquila and co-worker with Paul. The couple risked their lives for him and hosted a church in their home.

senses.name: Priscilla
senses.note: A Jewish believer, wife of Aquila, expelled from Rome under Claudius. The couple worked with Paul as tentmakers in Corinth, travelled with him to Ephesus, and taught Apollos.

senses.name: Prochorus
senses.note: One of the seven men chosen in Jerusalem to oversee the daily distribution to widows. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Ptolemais
senses.note: A port on the coast north of Mount Carmel, the earlier Akko (modern Acre). Paul stayed a day with the believers there on his way to Jerusalem.

senses.name: Pyrrhus
senses.note: The father of Sopater of Berea, one of Paul's travel companions; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Rahab
senses.note: A prostitute in Jericho who hid the Israelite spies and was spared when the city fell. Hebrews and James both hold her up as an example of faith shown in action.

senses.name: Reu
senses.note: Son of Peleg and an ancestor of Abraham in the line of Shem, listed in Luke's genealogy of Jesus.

senses.name: Ramah
senses.note: A town of Benjamin about five miles north of Jerusalem, near where Rachel was remembered as buried. Matthew applies Jeremiah's image of Rachel weeping there to the killing of the children of Bethlehem.

senses.name: Rahab
senses.note: A woman of Jericho who sheltered the Israelite spies and was spared when the city fell. Matthew lists her as the mother of Boaz in the family line of Jesus.

senses.name: Rachel
senses.note: Jacob's beloved wife, mother of Joseph and Benjamin, who was buried near Bethlehem. Jeremiah pictured her weeping for her lost children, and Matthew applies this to the killing of Bethlehem's boys.

senses.name: Rebecca
senses.note: Wife of Isaac and mother of the twins Jacob and Esau. Paul uses God's choice between her sons before their birth as an example.

senses.name: Rephan
senses.note: A star god named in Stephen's speech, quoting Amos, as one Israel worshipped in the wilderness. It is probably linked with an Assyrian name for the planet Saturn.

senses.name: Rhegium
senses.note: A port at the toe of Italy on the Strait of Messina (modern Reggio Calabria), where Paul's ship called on its way to Rome.

senses.name: Rhesa
senses.note: Named in Luke's genealogy of Jesus as a son of Zerubbabel; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Rehoboam
senses.note: Son of Solomon and king of Judah in the tenth century BC. Under him the northern tribes broke away, dividing the kingdom; he is listed in Matthew's family line of Jesus.

senses.name: Rhoda
senses.note: A slave girl in the house of Mary, John Mark's mother, in Jerusalem. She was so glad to hear Peter's voice at the gate that she ran to tell the others without opening it.

senses.name: Rhodes
senses.note: An island and city off the south-west coast of Asia Minor, an important stop on sea routes. Paul's ship called there on the way to Jerusalem.

senses.name: the tribe of Reuben
senses.note: The Israelite tribe descended from Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, named among the tribes sealed in Revelation.

senses.name: Ruth
senses.note: A Moabite woman who married Boaz of Bethlehem and became the great-grandmother of King David; her story is told in the book of Ruth.

senses.name: Rufus
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets along with his mother, who had cared for Paul. He may be the son of Simon of Cyrene named in Mark 15:21, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Rufus son of Simon of Cyrene
senses.note: A son of Simon of Cyrene, who carried Jesus' cross, and brother of Alexander; Mark names him as if readers knew him. He may be the Rufus Paul greets in Rome.

senses.name: Anna
senses.note: An elderly widow and prophet of the tribe of Asher, daughter of Phanuel, who served God in the temple and spoke about the infant Jesus.

senses.name: the Romans
senses.note: The people of Rome, whose empire ruled Judea in Jesus' time. The council feared that Rome would take away their temple and nation if Jesus' following grew.

senses.name: Latin
senses.note: The language of the Romans, used in the Roman government; Pilate's notice on the cross was written in it as well as in Hebrew and Greek.

senses.name: Rome
senses.note: The capital of the Roman Empire, in Italy. Paul wrote his letter to the believers there before he had visited them.

senses.name: Annas
senses.note: High priest in Jerusalem from AD 6 to 15 and father-in-law of Caiaphas, he remained powerful afterwards. Jesus was first brought to him after his arrest, and he later questioned Peter and John.

senses.name: the Sadducees
senses.note: A Jewish party linked with the priestly aristocracy that controlled the temple. They denied the resurrection, angels and spirits, and opposed Jesus and the apostles.

senses.name: Zadok
senses.note: A descendant of Zerubbabel listed in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus after the exile. Nothing more is known of him; he is not the priest Zadok of David's time.

senses.name: Sala
senses.note: Luke's form of the name Salmon: son of Nahshon and father of Boaz in the line of David.

senses.name: Shelah
senses.note: Son of Cainan and father of Eber in Luke's genealogy, one of the early descendants of Shem.

senses.name: Shealtiel
senses.note: A son of King Jechoniah born during the exile in Babylon, and father of Zerubbabel in Matthew's family line of Jesus.

senses.name: Salamis
senses.note: The main port city on the east coast of Cyprus, where Barnabas and Paul first preached in the synagogues on their journey.

senses.name: Salim
senses.note: A place near Aenon, where John baptized because there was plenty of water. The location is uncertain; it may have been in the Jordan valley or in Samaria.

senses.name: Salem
senses.note: The city where Melchizedek was king; its name is linked with peace. It is usually identified with Jerusalem.

senses.name: Salmon
senses.note: An ancestor of King David in Matthew's genealogy: son of Nahshon, husband of Rahab and father of Boaz.

senses.name: Salmone
senses.note: A cape at the eastern tip of Crete, which Paul's ship rounded on its way to Rome.

senses.name: Salome
senses.note: One of the women from Galilee who followed Jesus, watched the crucifixion and brought spices to the tomb. She is probably the mother of Zebedee's sons named in Matthew, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Samaria
senses.note: The central region of the land of Israel between Judea and Galilee, home of the Samaritans. Jesus passes through it and talks with a Samaritan woman at Jacob's well near Sychar.

senses.name: the Samaritans
senses.note: The people of Samaria, between Judea and Galilee, who worshipped the God of Israel but centred their worship on Mount Gerizim and accepted only the books of Moses. Jews and Samaritans were long hostile to one another.

senses.name: Samaritan
senses.note: Belonging to Samaria and its people, who worshipped the God of Israel at Mount Gerizim and kept their own form of the law of Moses. Jews and Samaritans were long at odds.

senses.name: Samothrace
senses.note: A mountainous island in the northern Aegean Sea where Paul's ship stopped overnight on the way from Troas to Neapolis.

senses.name: Samos
senses.note: An island in the Aegean Sea off the west coast of Asia Minor, passed by Paul on his voyage to Miletus.

senses.name: Samuel
senses.note: The prophet who led Israel after the judges and anointed its first kings, Saul and David. In the New Testament he marks the start of the line of prophets.

senses.name: Samson
senses.note: A judge of Israel from the tribe of Dan, famous for his great strength and his fights with the Philistines.

senses.name: Saul son of Kish
senses.note: Israel's first king, from the tribe of Benjamin, who reigned before David.

senses.name: Saul (Paul)
senses.note: The Jewish name of the apostle Paul, a Pharisee from Tarsus who persecuted the church until the risen Jesus confronted him near Damascus.

senses.name: Sapphira
senses.note: Wife of Ananias in the Jerusalem church. With him she kept back part of the price of their land while claiming to give it all, and she died after lying to Peter.

senses.name: Sardis
senses.note: A wealthy city in western Asia Minor (modern Turkey), once capital of Lydia. Revelation addresses a church there that had a name for being alive but was dead.

senses.name: Zarephath
senses.note: A Phoenician town on the coast between Tyre and Sidon, where Elijah was sent to a widow during a famine.

senses.name: Serug
senses.note: A descendant of Shem and great-grandfather of Abraham, named in Luke's family line of Jesus.

senses.name: Sarah
senses.note: The wife of Abraham, who in old age bore Isaac as God had promised. Paul cites the promise of her son, and Peter holds her up as an example to wives.

senses.name: Sharon
senses.note: The coastal plain of Israel running north from Joppa, near Lydda.

senses.name: Satan
senses.note: The chief adversary of God and of his people; the name means 'adversary'. Paul promises that God will soon crush him under the believers' feet.

senses.name: Saul
senses.note: The Jewish name of the apostle Paul, a man of Tarsus. Acts calls him Saul while he persecutes the church, at his conversion near Damascus, and in his early work with Barnabas, then switches to Paul.

senses.name: the emperor
senses.note: The Roman emperor, at this time Nero, called by a title meaning 'the revered one' (Augustus). As a Roman citizen Paul appealed to have his case heard by him.

senses.name: the Augustan Cohort
senses.note: A Roman auxiliary unit bearing an honorary imperial title; its centurion Julius guarded Paul on the voyage to Rome. Which unit it was is uncertain.

senses.name: Secundus
senses.note: A believer from Thessalonica who travelled with Paul toward Jerusalem; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Seleucia
senses.note: The port of Syrian Antioch, near the mouth of the Orontes river, from which Paul and Barnabas sailed to Cyprus.

senses.name: Semein
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy, son of Josech and father of Mattathias. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Sergius Paulus
senses.note: The Roman proconsul, or governor, of Cyprus, described as a man of understanding. He came to believe after Paul exposed the magician Bar-Jesus.

senses.name: Seth
senses.note: The son born to Adam and Eve after Abel's death, through whom Luke traces Jesus' line back to Adam.

senses.name: Shem
senses.note: The eldest son of Noah, named in Luke's genealogy as an ancestor of Abraham and of Jesus.

senses.name: Sidon
senses.note: An ancient Phoenician port city on the Mediterranean coast north of Tyre, in modern Lebanon. Jesus named it with Tyre as Gentile cities, and Paul's ship called there on the way to Rome.

senses.name: Sidon
senses.note: An ancient Phoenician port city on the coast of modern Lebanon. Elijah was sent to a widow in its territory, and its people later sought peace with Herod Agrippa I.

senses.name: Silas
senses.note: A leader of the Jerusalem church sent with Paul and Barnabas to Antioch, then Paul's partner on his second journey, imprisoned with him at Philippi. Paul's letters call him Silvanus.

senses.name: Silas
senses.note: A leader of the Jerusalem church and a prophet, sent with the council's letter to Antioch. He then becomes Paul's partner on his second journey and is jailed with him at Philippi.

senses.name: Silvanus
senses.note: A Christian leader who helped carry or write Peter's letter; probably the same as Silas, Paul's companion on his travels in Acts.

senses.name: the pool of Siloam
senses.note: A pool in the south of Jerusalem, fed by Hezekiah's tunnel from the Gihon spring. Jesus sent a man born blind to wash there, and he came back able to see.

senses.name: the tower at Siloam
senses.note: A tower near the pool of Siloam in the south of Jerusalem whose fall killed eighteen people, a disaster Jesus mentions; nothing more is known of it.

senses.name: Simon Peter
senses.note: One of the Twelve and the brother of Andrew, a fisherman from Bethsaida. Jesus gave him the name Cephas, meaning Rock (Peter), and he became a leading apostle.

senses.name: Simon the Zealot
senses.note: One of the twelve apostles, called the Zealot (or Cananaean) to set him apart from Simon Peter. The name may point to zeal for the law or to a link with Jewish nationalists; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Simon Iscariot
senses.note: The father of Judas Iscariot, the disciple who betrayed Jesus. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Simon the magician
senses.note: A man in Samaria who amazed people with magic. He was baptized after Philip's preaching but then tried to buy from the apostles the power to give the Spirit, and Peter rebuked him.

senses.name: Simon the tanner
senses.note: A tanner in the port town of Joppa whose house by the sea Peter stayed in; there Cornelius's messengers found Peter.

senses.name: Simon of Cyrene
senses.note: A man from Cyrene in North Africa, coming in from the countryside, whom the soldiers forced to carry Jesus' cross. Mark names him as the father of Alexander and Rufus.

senses.name: Simon the Pharisee
senses.note: A Pharisee who invited Jesus to a meal, where a sinful woman anointed Jesus' feet; Jesus answered Simon's unspoken objection with a story about two debtors.

senses.name: Simon the leper
senses.note: A man of Bethany, near Jerusalem, who had suffered from a skin disease; Jesus was a guest in his house when a woman poured costly perfumed oil on him.

senses.name: Simon, brother of Jesus
senses.note: One of the brothers of Jesus named by the people of Nazareth, along with James, Joseph (Joses) and Judas. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Sinai
senses.note: The mountain in the wilderness where God spoke to Moses from the bush and gave the law to Israel. Paul uses it as a picture of the covenant of the law. Its location is debated.

senses.name: Zion
senses.note: Originally the hill of David's fortress in Jerusalem, then a name for Jerusalem and its temple mount, and for God's people. The letters quote Isaiah's prophecy of a stone laid in Zion.

senses.name: Sceva
senses.note: A Jewish high priest whose seven sons tried to drive out demons in Ephesus using the name of Jesus and were overpowered. He is otherwise unknown.

senses.name: Scythians
senses.note: Nomadic peoples from the steppes north of the Black Sea, regarded by Greeks and Romans as the most uncivilized of foreigners. Paul names them to show that no background counts in Christ.

senses.name: Smyrna
senses.note: A port city on the west coast of the province of Asia (modern Izmir, Turkey), home of one of the seven churches addressed in Revelation.

senses.name: Smyrna
senses.note: A port city on the west coast of Asia Minor, north of Ephesus (modern Izmir, Turkey). It received one of the seven messages in Revelation.

senses.name: Sodom
senses.note: A city near the Dead Sea that God destroyed with Gomorrah for its wickedness in Abraham's time. It became a standing example of complete judgment.

senses.name: Solomon
senses.note: Son of David and Bathsheba and king of Israel after him, famed for his wisdom and for building the first temple. He appears in Jesus' genealogy, and a colonnade of the temple courts bore his name.

senses.name: Solomon
senses.note: David's son and successor as king of Israel, who built the first temple in Jerusalem.

senses.name: Solomon's Porch
senses.note: A long roofed colonnade on the east side of the temple courts in Jerusalem, named after King Solomon. The first believers gathered there.

senses.name: Susanna
senses.note: One of the women healed by Jesus who travelled with him and the Twelve and supported them from their own means; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Spain
senses.note: The Roman provinces of the Iberian peninsula, at the western edge of the known world. Paul hoped to travel there after visiting Rome; whether he ever did is uncertain.

senses.name: Stachys
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets as his dear friend; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Stephanas
senses.note: A believer in Corinth whose household was the first to believe in Achaia and was baptized by Paul. He visited Paul in Ephesus with Fortunatus and Achaicus.

senses.name: Stephen
senses.note: One of the seven men chosen to care for the widows in the Jerusalem church, a man full of faith who did signs. He was stoned after his speech before the council, the first follower of Jesus killed for his faith.

senses.name: Solomon's Porch
senses.note: A long roofed colonnade along the east side of the temple courts in Jerusalem, where the first believers often gathered.

senses.name: the Stoics
senses.note: Followers of a leading Greek school of philosophy that taught living in line with reason and nature. Some debated with Paul in Athens.

senses.name: Simon Peter
senses.note: The apostle Peter, here called by the Hebrew form of his name, Simeon. He was one of the Twelve and a leader of the early church.

senses.name: Simeon called Niger
senses.note: One of the prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch when Barnabas and Saul were sent out. His nickname means black; nothing more is known of him for certain.

senses.name: Simeon
senses.note: A devout man in Jerusalem who had been promised he would see the Messiah. He took the infant Jesus in his arms in the temple, praised God, and spoke to Mary about her son's future.

senses.name: Simeon, son of Judah
senses.note: Named in Luke's genealogy of Jesus as an ancestor between David and Zerubbabel; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: the tribe of Simeon
senses.note: The Israelite tribe descended from Simeon, second son of Jacob and Leah. In Revelation it is one of the twelve tribes whose members are sealed.

senses.name: Antioch in Syria
senses.note: A large city in Syria on the Orontes River, where believers were first called Christians. Its church sent out Barnabas and Paul and became their home base.

senses.name: Antioch near Pisidia
senses.note: A Roman colony in the interior of Asia Minor, in what is now central Turkey. Paul preached in its synagogue on his first journey, and Jews from there later stirred up opposition against him at Lystra.

senses.name: Antioch
senses.note: Antioch in Syria, the great city on the Orontes river, in modern Turkey. Nicolaus, one of the seven chosen in Jerusalem, came from there.

senses.name: Antipas
senses.note: A believer at Pergamum who was killed for his faithfulness; the risen Jesus calls him his faithful witness. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Antipatris
senses.note: A town built by Herod the Great on the road from Jerusalem to Caesarea, where Paul's escort stopped on the night journey.

senses.name: Syntyche
senses.note: A woman in the church at Philippi who had worked with Paul in spreading the gospel. Paul urges her and Euodia to agree in the Lord; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Syracuse
senses.note: A major port city on the east coast of Sicily, where Paul's ship stayed three days on the way to Rome.

senses.name: Syria
senses.note: The Roman province north of Galilee, with Antioch as its capital. Jesus' fame spreads there, Quirinius governs it, and Paul works in and sails to and from it.

senses.name: Syria
senses.note: The land of Aram, north-east of Israel, with Damascus as its capital. Naaman, the army commander healed by Elisha, came from there.

senses.name: Syrophoenician
senses.note: A Gentile woman born in Phoenicia, the coastal region around Tyre and Sidon then in the province of Syria, who begged Jesus to free her daughter from a demon.

senses.name: Syrtis
senses.note: Dangerous shallows and sandbanks off the coast of Libya, which the sailors feared the storm would drive the ship onto.

senses.name: Sychar
senses.note: A Samaritan town near Jacob's well, where Jesus spoke with a Samaritan woman; probably near ancient Shechem, though the exact site is uncertain.

senses.name: Shechem
senses.note: An ancient town in central Canaan, near modern Nablus, where Stephen says the patriarchs were buried in a tomb bought from the sons of Hamor.

senses.name: Sopater
senses.note: Son of Pyrrhus, a believer from Berea who travelled with Paul toward Jerusalem. He may be the Sosipater who sends greetings in Romans.

senses.name: Sosthenes
senses.note: A leader of the synagogue in Corinth who was beaten in front of Gallio's court. The Sosthenes who joins Paul in writing 1 Corinthians may be the same man.

senses.name: Sosipater
senses.note: A Jewish believer with Paul when he wrote to the Romans, who sends greetings. He may be Sopater of Berea, who travelled with Paul, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Three Taverns
senses.note: A stopping place on the Appian Way about 33 miles south of Rome. Believers from Rome came out there to meet Paul.

senses.name: Tabitha
senses.note: A disciple at Joppa, also called Dorcas, known for her good works and gifts to the poor. Peter raised her from the dead.

senses.name: Tarsus
senses.note: The chief city of Cilicia in south-eastern Asia Minor, a centre of learning, and the home town of Paul.

senses.name: Tarsus
senses.note: A large city of Cilicia, in what is now south-eastern Turkey, and Paul's birthplace. Paul returned there for a time after his conversion.

senses.name: Tertius
senses.note: The scribe who wrote down Paul's letter to the Romans and adds his own greeting; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Tertullus
senses.note: A professional advocate hired by the high priest Ananias and the elders to press their case against Paul before Governor Felix.

senses.name: the Sea of Tiberias
senses.note: Another name for the Sea of Galilee, taken from the city of Tiberias on its western shore.

senses.name: Tiberias
senses.note: A city on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, founded by Herod Antipas around AD 20 and named after the emperor Tiberius. Boats from there came near where the crowd had been fed.

senses.name: Tiberius
senses.note: Roman emperor from AD 14 to 37, successor of Augustus. Luke dates the start of John's preaching to his fifteenth year, about AD 28 or 29.

senses.name: Timaeus
senses.note: Father of Bartimaeus, the blind beggar healed by Jesus near Jericho; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Timothy
senses.note: Paul's close co-worker and travel companion, from Lystra, with a Jewish mother and a Greek father. He is named with Paul as co-sender of several letters, and Paul sent him to churches on his behalf.

senses.name: Timon
senses.note: One of the seven men chosen to oversee the daily distribution of food in the Jerusalem church. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Titus
senses.note: A Greek Christian and trusted co-worker of Paul, who took him to Jerusalem uncircumcised. He carried out delicate work with the church in Corinth, was later left to organize the churches on Crete, and received a letter from Paul.

senses.name: Trachonitis
senses.note: A rugged volcanic region south of Damascus, in what is now southern Syria, ruled by Herod's son Philip at the time of John the Baptist.

senses.name: Three Taverns
senses.note: A stopping place on the Appian Way about 50 kilometres (30 miles) south of Rome, where believers came out to meet Paul.

senses.name: Trophimus
senses.note: A believer from Ephesus who travelled with Paul to Jerusalem; rumors that Paul had brought him into the temple set off Paul's arrest. Paul later left him sick at Miletus.

senses.name: Tryphaena
senses.note: A woman in the church in Rome, greeted with Tryphosa (perhaps her sister) as a hard worker in the Lord; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Tryphosa
senses.note: A woman in Rome, greeted with Tryphena, whom Paul commends for her work in the Lord; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Troas
senses.note: A Roman port city on the north-west coast of Asia Minor, near ancient Troy. Paul sailed from there to Macedonia after a vision and later visited it again.

senses.name: Tyrannus
senses.note: A man in Ephesus whose lecture hall Paul used every day for about two years after leaving the synagogue; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: the people of Tyre
senses.note: The inhabitants of the Phoenician port of Tyre, who with the people of Sidon depended on Herod Agrippa's territory for food and sought peace with him after a quarrel.

senses.name: Tyre
senses.note: An ancient Phoenician port city on the coast north of Galilee, in modern Lebanon, famous for trade. Jesus visits its region and names it as a pagan city that would have repented, and Paul's ship calls there.

senses.name: Tychicus
senses.note: A trusted co-worker of Paul from the province of Asia, who carried Paul's letters to Colossae and Ephesus and brought news of him to the churches.

senses.name: Hymenaeus
senses.note: A man Paul names as having abandoned the faith and taught that the resurrection had already happened. Paul says he handed him over to Satan to learn not to blaspheme.

senses.name: Peleg
senses.note: A descendant of Shem, son of Eber and father of Reu, listed among the ancestors of Abraham and of Jesus.

senses.name: Phanuel
senses.note: A man of the tribe of Asher, father of the prophet Anna who met the infant Jesus in the temple. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Pharaoh
senses.note: The title of the king of Egypt; here the king who refused to let Israel go at the time of the exodus. Paul cites God's words to him to show God's freedom to act.

senses.name: Pharaoh in Joseph's time
senses.note: The king of Egypt who made Joseph governor over Egypt and his household, and welcomed Joseph's family.

senses.name: Pharaoh in Moses' infancy
senses.note: The king of Egypt who oppressed Israel when Moses was born; his daughter took the abandoned baby Moses and raised him as her son.

senses.name: Perez
senses.note: Son of Judah and Tamar, twin brother of Zerah, and an ancestor of David listed in Jesus' genealogy.

senses.name: the Pharisees
senses.note: A Jewish religious movement devoted to careful keeping of the law of Moses and its traditions. In John they question and oppose Jesus and join the chief priests against him; Paul says he was once a Pharisee.

senses.name: Felix
senses.note: Antonius Felix, Roman governor of Judea in the 50s AD. He held Paul at Caesarea for two years, listening to him with his wife Drusilla but leaving the case unresolved.

senses.name: Festus
senses.note: Porcius Festus, Roman governor of Judea from about AD 59 who succeeded Felix. He heard Paul's case with King Agrippa and sent Paul to Rome after he appealed to Caesar.

senses.name: Philadelphia
senses.note: A city in the Roman province of Asia, in western Asia Minor (modern Turkey). The risen Jesus sends a message to its church, praising it for holding to his word.

senses.name: Philemon
senses.note: A believer, probably at Colossae, whose house hosted a church. Paul wrote to him about his slave Onesimus.

senses.name: Philetus
senses.note: A teacher whom Paul names with Hymenaeus as having wandered from the truth by saying the resurrection had already happened; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: the Philippians
senses.note: The believers in Philippi, a Roman colony in Macedonia where Paul founded a church. They supported his work financially from the start.

senses.name: Philippi
senses.note: A Roman colony in Macedonia, in northern Greece, on the main road between east and west. Paul founded a church there, the first he started in Europe, and later wrote it a letter.

senses.name: Philip
senses.note: One of the twelve disciples, from Bethsaida, the hometown of Andrew and Peter. Jesus called him directly; he brought Nathanael to Jesus and was tested by Jesus before the feeding of the crowd.

senses.name: Philip the evangelist
senses.note: One of the seven men chosen to oversee the daily distribution of food in Jerusalem. He preached in Samaria, baptized an Ethiopian official, and later lived in Caesarea.

senses.name: Philip the tetrarch
senses.note: A son of Herod the Great who ruled the territories north-east of the Sea of Galilee, including Ituraea and Trachonitis, from 4 BC to about AD 34.

senses.name: Philip, husband of Herodias
senses.note: A son of Herod the Great and half-brother of Herod Antipas. His wife Herodias left him to marry Antipas, which John the Baptist condemned.

senses.name: Caesarea Philippi
senses.note: A town at the foot of Mount Hermon near the sources of the Jordan, rebuilt by Philip the tetrarch and named in honour of the emperor and himself. There Peter declared Jesus to be the Messiah.

senses.name: Philologus
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets, perhaps the husband of Julia; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Phlegon
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Phoebe
senses.note: A woman serving the church at Cenchreae, the eastern port of Corinth, whom Paul commends to Rome; she had been a benefactor to many, and probably carried the letter.

senses.name: Phoenicia
senses.note: The coastal region north of Galilee, in today's Lebanon, with the port cities of Tyre and Sidon.

senses.name: Phoenix
senses.note: A harbor on the south coast of Crete where the crew of Paul's ship hoped to spend the winter; a storm drove them off course before they reached it.

senses.name: the Forum of Appius
senses.note: A market town on the Appian Way about 40 miles south of Rome, where believers came out to meet Paul.

senses.name: Fortunatus
senses.note: A believer from Corinth who, with Stephanas and Achaicus, visited Paul in Ephesus and refreshed him. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Phrygia
senses.note: A region in the interior of Asia Minor (modern Turkey), divided between Roman provinces. Paul passed through it on his journeys, and Jews from Phrygia were in Jerusalem at Pentecost.

senses.name: Phygelus
senses.note: A believer in the province of Asia who, with Hermogenes, turned away from Paul during his last imprisonment. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: the Chaldeans
senses.note: A people of southern Mesopotamia, later the ruling people of Babylon. Stephen recalls that Abraham left their land before settling in Haran.

senses.name: Canaan
senses.note: The land between the Jordan and the Mediterranean that God promised to Abraham's descendants, settled by Israel after the seven nations living there were overthrown.

senses.name: Canaanites
senses.note: The ancient inhabitants of the land of Canaan. Matthew uses the old name for a non-Jewish woman from the region of Tyre and Sidon who begs Jesus to heal her daughter.

senses.name: Haran
senses.note: A city in northern Mesopotamia, in what is now south-eastern Turkey. Stephen recalls that Abraham settled there for a time on his way from the land of the Chaldeans to Canaan.

senses.name: cherubim
senses.note: Winged heavenly beings. Two golden figures of them stood over the ark of the covenant in the Most Holy Place, their wings covering the mercy seat.

senses.name: Chios
senses.note: A large island in the Aegean Sea off the west coast of Asia Minor, passed on Paul's voyage to Miletus.

senses.name: Chloe
senses.note: A woman, probably at Corinth or Ephesus, whose people told Paul about the quarrels in the Corinthian church; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Chorazin
senses.note: A village in Galilee a little north of Capernaum. Jesus pronounces woe on it for not repenting despite the miracles done there.

senses.name: Chuza
senses.note: The manager of Herod Antipas's household, whose wife Joanna was among the women who followed Jesus and supported him from their means.

senses.name: Christian
senses.note: A name for followers of Christ, first used in Antioch and probably given by outsiders. Peter tells believers not to be ashamed to suffer under this name.

senses.name: Apelles
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets as tested and found true in Christ; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: the Alpha and the Omega
senses.note: Alpha and Omega are the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet. In Revelation the phrase is a title of the Lord God, and later of Jesus, meaning the beginning and the end of all things.

senses.name: Obed
senses.note: Son of Boaz and Ruth and father of Jesse, so the grandfather of King David. He is listed in Jesus' genealogy.

senses.name: Obed
senses.note: The son of Boaz and Ruth, and father of Jesse, David's father; he appears in Luke's genealogy of Jesus.

senses.name: Hosea
senses.note: An Israelite prophet of the eighth century BC. Paul quotes his book to show that God calls people who were not his people to be his own.

senses.name: Abel
senses.note: The second son of Adam and Eve, a shepherd whose offering God accepted; his brother Cain killed him. He is remembered as the first righteous person whose blood was shed.

senses.name: Apollyon
senses.note: The Greek name, meaning destroyer, of the angel of the abyss who rules over the locusts in Revelation. His Hebrew name is Abaddon.

senses.name: Apollonia
senses.note: A town in Macedonia on the Roman road between Amphipolis and Thessalonica, through which Paul and Silas passed.

senses.name: Apollos
senses.note: A Jewish believer from Alexandria, a gifted speaker skilled in the Scriptures, who taught in Ephesus and then in Corinth. Some Corinthians took sides over him and Paul, who called him a fellow worker.

senses.name: Agrippa
senses.note: Herod Agrippa II, great-grandson of Herod the Great, a client king under Rome. With his sister Bernice he heard Paul's defense at Caesarea and judged that Paul could have been released.

senses.name: the Forum of Appius
senses.note: A market town on the Appian Way about 40 miles (65 km) south of Rome, where believers from Rome came to meet Paul.

senses.name: Apphia
senses.note: A believer named in the greeting of Paul's letter to Philemon, probably a member of Philemon's household, perhaps his wife.

senses.name: Arabia
senses.note: The desert lands east and south of Judea, in Paul's day probably the Nabataean kingdom. Paul went there after his conversion, and he places Mount Sinai there.

senses.name: Admin
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy, between Amminadab and Arni; he is not found in the Old Testament lists, and some manuscripts differ here.

senses.name: Ram
senses.note: Son of Hezron and father of Amminadab, an ancestor of David in the line of Judah listed in Jesus' genealogy. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Arabs
senses.note: People from Arabia, probably the Nabatean kingdom east and south of Judea, among the visitors in Jerusalem at Pentecost.

senses.name: the Areopagus
senses.note: The "Hill of Ares" in Athens, and the city council that met there and had oversight of religion and teaching. Paul explained his message before it.

senses.name: the Areopagus
senses.note: The Hill of Ares in Athens, and the city council that took its name from it. Paul was brought before it to explain his teaching.

senses.name: the Areopagus council
senses.note: The ancient governing council of Athens, named after the Hill of Ares where it once met. Dionysius, one of its members, believed after Paul spoke there.

senses.name: Abijah
senses.note: Son of Rehoboam and king of Judah for about three years, listed among the kings in Jesus' genealogy.

senses.name: Abijah (priestly division)
senses.note: A priest of David's time whose name was given to one of the twenty-four divisions of priests; Zechariah, father of John the Baptist, belonged to it.

senses.name: Aretas
senses.note: King Aretas IV of the Nabataeans, whose kingdom lay south and east of Judea; his governor in Damascus tried to arrest Paul, who escaped in a basket.

senses.name: Arimathea
senses.note: A town of Judea, home of Joseph, the council member who buried Jesus. Its location is uncertain; it is often identified with Ramathaim, north-west of Jerusalem.

senses.name: Aristarchus
senses.note: A Jewish believer from Thessalonica who travelled with Paul and shared his imprisonment; he sends greetings in the letter to the Colossians.

senses.name: Aristobulus
senses.note: A man in Rome; Paul greets the members of his household rather than him, and nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Armageddon
senses.note: The gathering place of the kings for the final battle in Revelation. The name is usually explained as Mount Megiddo, after the old battle site in northern Israel.

senses.name: Artemas
senses.note: A co-worker of Paul whom he planned to send to Titus in Crete. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Artemis
senses.note: A Greek goddess whose great temple at Ephesus was one of the wonders of the ancient world. Silversmiths who made her shrines stirred up a riot against Paul's preaching.

senses.name: Arphaxad
senses.note: Son of Shem, born two years after the flood, and an ancestor of Abraham. Luke includes him in Jesus' genealogy.

senses.name: Archelaus
senses.note: A son of Herod the Great who ruled Judea, Samaria and Idumea after him from 4 BC until Rome removed him in AD 6; fear of him led Joseph to settle in Galilee.

senses.name: Archippus
senses.note: A believer at Colossae, probably connected with Philemon's household, whom Paul urges to complete the ministry he has received.

senses.name: Adam
senses.note: The first man, made by God, husband of Eve, and ancestor of all people. Luke traces Jesus' line back to him, and Paul contrasts Adam, through whom death came, with Christ.

senses.name: Asa
senses.note: A king of Judah, son of Abijah and father of Jehoshaphat, remembered in Kings for removing idols. Some Greek manuscripts of Matthew spell his name Asaph.

senses.name: Asher
senses.note: The Israelite tribe descended from Asher, son of Jacob by Zilpah. The prophet Anna belonged to it.

senses.name: Asia
senses.note: The Roman province in the west of what is now Turkey, with Ephesus as its leading city; not the continent.

senses.name: the province of Asia
senses.note: The Roman province in western Asia Minor (modern Turkey), with Ephesus as its chief city; home of Tychicus and Trophimus.

senses.name: Asiarchs
senses.note: Leading men of the Roman province of Asia who held a civic and religious office. Some of them were friends of Paul and warned him away from the riot in the theater at Ephesus.

senses.name: Addi
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's family line, before the exile. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Assos
senses.note: A port on the north-west coast of Asia Minor (modern Turkey), south of Troas. Paul walked there overland and rejoined his companions on the ship.

senses.name: Asyncritus
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets with others and the believers with them; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Abiathar
senses.note: A priest in David's time, later high priest with Zadok. When David ate the sacred bread, the priest was Abiathar's father Ahimelech, but Mark names Abiathar, probably as the better-known high priest of that period.

senses.name: Attalia
senses.note: A port on the south coast of Asia Minor in Pamphylia, today's Antalya, from which Paul and Barnabas sailed back to Antioch.

senses.name: Caesar Augustus
senses.note: The first Roman emperor, who ruled from 27 BC to AD 14. His order for a registration brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem.

senses.name: Ahaz
senses.note: King of Judah in the eighth century BC, son of Jotham and father of Hezekiah, remembered for unfaithfulness. He is listed among the kings in Jesus' genealogy.

senses.name: Achaia
senses.note: The Roman province of southern Greece, with Corinth as its capital; its churches gave to the poor believers in Jerusalem.

senses.name: Achaicus
senses.note: A believer from Corinth who came to Paul in Ephesus with Stephanas and Fortunatus; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Achim
senses.note: A descendant of Zerubbabel listed in Matthew's family line of Jesus, son of Zadok and father of Eliud. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Wormwood
senses.note: The name of a star that falls from the sky in a vision in Revelation, making a third of the waters bitter. Wormwood is a bitter plant.

senses.name: Baal
senses.note: A Canaanite storm and fertility god whose worship spread in Israel in Elijah's day. God told Elijah he had kept 7,000 people who had not worshipped Baal.

senses.name: Babylon
senses.note: The capital of the Babylonian empire on the Euphrates, to which the people of Judah were deported in the sixth century BC; Matthew uses the deportation to divide Jesus' genealogy.

senses.name: Babylon (where Peter writes from)
senses.note: The place Peter sends greetings from at the close of his letter. It is probably a figurative name for Rome, the imperial capital, though some take it literally.

senses.name: Babylon the great
senses.note: In Revelation, a great city pictured as a richly dressed prostitute whose fall is announced. It stands for a power opposed to God, most often taken to be imperial Rome.

senses.name: Abilene
senses.note: A small district north-west of Damascus, in the Anti-Lebanon mountains, ruled by Lysanias when John the Baptist began preaching.

senses.name: Balaam
senses.note: A prophet, son of Beor, hired by the king of Moab to curse Israel in the time of Moses. Peter uses him as an example of a teacher who loved the reward of wrongdoing.

senses.name: Balak
senses.note: A king of Moab who hired Balaam to curse Israel. Revelation recalls how Balaam taught him to lead Israel into idolatry and immorality.

senses.name: Barabbas
senses.note: A prisoner held for rebellion and murder at the time of Jesus' trial. Pilate offers the crowd a choice, and they ask for Barabbas to be released instead of Jesus.

senses.name: Barak
senses.note: An Israelite commander who, urged on by the prophet Deborah, defeated the Canaanite army of Sisera in the time of the judges.

senses.name: Barachiah
senses.note: The father of the Zechariah whose murder in the temple Jesus mentions. He may be the father of the prophet Zechariah, though the account of the killing fits Zechariah son of Jehoiada.

senses.name: Bartholomew
senses.note: One of the twelve apostles, named only in the lists of the Twelve. Many have identified him with Nathanael, but the Bible does not say so.

senses.name: Bar-Jesus
senses.note: A Jewish magician and false prophet at Paphos on Cyprus, also called Elymas, who opposed Barnabas and Saul and was struck blind for a time.

senses.name: Simon son of Jonah
senses.note: The apostle Peter, called here by his father's name. John's Gospel gives his father's name as John; the two forms may be related.

senses.name: Barnabas
senses.note: A Jewish believer from Cyprus, early leader in Jerusalem and Antioch, and Paul's partner on his first mission journey. Mark is his cousin.

senses.name: Joseph Barsabbas
senses.note: A disciple, also called Justus, who had been with Jesus from the beginning. He was one of two men put forward to replace Judas Iscariot, but Matthias was chosen.

senses.name: Judas Barsabbas
senses.note: A leader and prophet in the Jerusalem church, chosen with Silas to carry the council's letter to the believers in Antioch.

senses.name: Bartimaeus
senses.note: A blind beggar near Jericho, son of Timaeus, who called out to Jesus as Son of David and was given his sight.

senses.name: Beelzebul
senses.note: A name, probably from an old Philistine god, used for the ruler of the demons. Jesus' opponents claimed he drove out demons by Beelzebul's power, and Jesus answered that a divided kingdom cannot stand.

senses.name: Belial
senses.note: A name for Satan, from a Hebrew word meaning worthlessness or wickedness. Paul sets him against Christ to show that believers cannot share in what opposes God.

senses.name: Benjamin
senses.note: The tribe descended from Benjamin, Jacob's youngest son; Saul, Israel's first king, came from it. Paul names it as his own tribe.

senses.name: Bernice
senses.note: The sister of King Agrippa II and daughter of Herod Agrippa I, who sat with him and Festus when Paul made his defence in Caesarea.

senses.name: Berea
senses.note: A town in Macedonia, west of Thessalonica, in northern Greece. Paul and Silas preached there after leaving Thessalonica, and the Jews there examined the Scriptures eagerly.

senses.name: Berea
senses.note: A town in Macedonia, west of Thessalonica. Sopater, one of Paul's travelling companions, came from there.

senses.name: Bethany beyond the Jordan
senses.note: The place on the east side of the Jordan where John was baptizing. It is distinct from Bethany near Jerusalem, and its location is uncertain.

senses.name: Bethany
senses.note: A village on the Mount of Olives about two miles from Jerusalem, home of Martha, Mary and Lazarus, whom Jesus raised from the dead.

senses.name: Bethesda
senses.note: A pool in Jerusalem near the Sheep Gate, surrounded by five porticoes, where Jesus healed a man who had been ill for thirty-eight years. Remains of a double pool have been found north of the temple area. Manuscripts vary on the name.

senses.name: Bethlehem
senses.note: A village about 9 kilometres south of Jerusalem in Judea, the hometown of David. The prophet Micah linked it with a coming ruler, so the Christ was expected to come from there.

senses.name: Bethsaida
senses.note: A fishing town at the north end of the Sea of Galilee, near where the Jordan enters it; home town of Philip, Andrew and Peter.

senses.name: Bethsaida
senses.note: A fishing town on the northern shore of the Sea of Galilee, near where the Jordan enters it; home of Philip, Andrew and Peter. Jesus healed a blind man there.

senses.name: Bethphage
senses.note: A village on the Mount of Olives near Bethany, just east of Jerusalem, where Jesus sent two disciples to fetch a donkey before entering the city.

senses.name: Bithynia
senses.note: A Roman province in north-west Asia Minor (modern Turkey) along the Black Sea coast. It is one of the regions where the readers of 1 Peter lived.

senses.name: Adramyttium
senses.note: A port on the north-west coast of Asia Minor (modern Turkey). Paul begins his voyage to Rome on a ship from there.

senses.name: Blastus
senses.note: The chamberlain of King Herod Agrippa I, whom the people of Tyre and Sidon won over to help them make peace with the king.

senses.name: the Adriatic Sea
senses.note: In New Testament times, the name covered the central Mediterranean between Crete, Sicily and Greece, not only the modern Adriatic. Paul's ship drifted there for two weeks before wrecking on Malta.

senses.name: Boanerges
senses.note: A name Jesus gave to the brothers James and John, sons of Zebedee, explained as 'Sons of Thunder', probably because of their fiery temper.

senses.name: Bethel
senses.note: A town about 19 kilometres (12 miles) north of Jerusalem, earlier called Luz. Abraham camped near it, and Jacob named it Bethel, 'house of God', after God appeared to him there in a dream.

senses.name: Bethel
senses.note: A town in the hill country north of Jerusalem, earlier called Luz. Abraham built an altar nearby, and Jacob named it Bethel, meaning house of God, after God appeared to him there.

senses.name: Bethlehem
senses.note: A town in Judah about 9 km south of Jerusalem, also called Ephrath. Rachel died and was buried on the road near it.

senses.name: Becher
senses.note: A son of Benjamin who went down to Egypt with Jacob; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Bel
senses.note: A title, meaning lord, of Marduk, chief god of Babylon. Isaiah pictures his idols being carried off as baggage.

senses.name: Baladan
senses.note: The father of Merodach-baladan, the king of Babylon who sent envoys to Hezekiah. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Bilhah
senses.note: Rachel's slave woman, given to her by Laban. Rachel gave her to Jacob as a wife, and she bore Dan and Naphtali; Reuben later slept with her.

senses.name: Bilhan
senses.note: A son of Ezer, among the Horite clans of Seir in Edom; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Abaddon
senses.note: A Hebrew name meaning Destruction, used in poetry for the realm of the dead, alongside Sheol and the grave.

senses.name: Adbeel
senses.note: The third son of Ishmael, probably ancestor of an Arab tribe; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Bela, king of Edom
senses.note: Son of Beor, the first king of Edom in the list of its kings; his city was Dinhabah.

senses.name: Bela, son of Benjamin
senses.note: The first-named son of Benjamin, listed among Jacob's family who went down to Egypt.

senses.name: Bela
senses.note: The older name of Zoar, a small town of the plain near the Dead Sea whose king fought alongside Sodom and Gomorrah.

senses.name: Ben-oni
senses.note: The name the dying Rachel gave her last son, meaning 'son of my sorrow'; Jacob renamed him Benjamin.

senses.name: Ben-oni
senses.note: The name, "son of my sorrow", that the dying Rachel gave her second son; Jacob named him Benjamin instead.

senses.name: Benjamin (the tribe)
senses.note: The tribe descended from Benjamin, a small tribe whose land lay just north of Jerusalem; Israel's first king, Saul, came from it.

senses.name: Benjamin
senses.note: The youngest of Jacob's twelve sons and the second son of Rachel, who died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him closely after losing Joseph, and Joseph tested his brothers through him in Egypt.

senses.name: Ben-ammi
senses.note: The son of Lot by his younger daughter, ancestor of the Ammonites.

senses.name: Ben-ammi
senses.note: The son born to Lot's younger daughter after the destruction of Sodom, and the ancestor of the Ammonites.

senses.name: Beor
senses.note: Father of Bela, the first king of Edom named in Genesis. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Baal-hanan
senses.note: Son of Achbor, one of the kings who ruled Edom before Israel had a king. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Baal-zephon
senses.note: A place by the sea on the Israelites' route out of Egypt, named after a Canaanite god; they camped opposite it before crossing. Its location is uncertain.

senses.name: Baal-zephon
senses.note: A place near the sea in the eastern Nile delta where the Israelites camped before crossing the sea. The name honors a Canaanite god; its exact location is uncertain.

senses.name: Adam
senses.note: The first man, formed by God and placed in the garden of Eden, husband of Eve and father of Cain, Abel and Seth. The same word also means 'human being' or 'humankind'.

senses.name: Bezalel
senses.note: Son of Uri and grandson of Hur, from the tribe of Judah, whom God gifted with skill to lead the work on the tabernacle and its furnishings, including the ark, with Oholiab.

senses.name: Bozrah
senses.note: A major city of Edom, south-east of the Dead Sea, probably at modern Buseirah in Jordan. Isaiah uses it to stand for Edom under judgment.

senses.name: Edom (Esau)
senses.note: A second name given to Esau, Jacob's twin brother, from the red stew he asked for; the people and land descended from him took the name.

senses.name: Edom
senses.note: The land and people descended from Esau, in the hill country of Seir south-east of the Dead Sea. Edom was often hostile to Israel, and the prophets speak of its judgment.

senses.name: Admah
senses.note: One of the cities of the plain beside Sodom and Gomorrah, near the Dead Sea; its king joined the revolt against Kedorlaomer. Its exact site is unknown.

senses.name: Bered
senses.note: A place in the Negev near the well Beer-lahai-roi, on the other side from Kadesh. Its location is unknown.

senses.name: Beriah
senses.note: A son of Asher and father of Heber and Malkiel, among those who went down to Egypt with Jacob.

senses.name: Bera
senses.note: The king of Sodom in Abraham's time, defeated by the four eastern kings. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Birsha
senses.note: King of Gomorrah, one of the five kings of the Jordan plain who rebelled against Kedorlaomer; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Basemath, daughter of Elon
senses.note: A Hittite woman whom Esau married at forty, to the grief of his parents. She may be the same as one of the wives listed in chapter 36 under other names.

senses.name: Basemath, daughter of Ishmael
senses.note: A wife of Esau, daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth. She bore Esau's son Reuel, whose sons became chiefs in Edom.

senses.name: Bashan
senses.note: A fertile highland east of the Sea of Galilee, famous for its oak forests and strong cattle. Its high mountain appears as a rival to Zion in the Psalms.

senses.name: Bethuel
senses.note: Son of Abraham's brother Nahor and Milcah, and father of Rebekah and Laban. Isaac's and Jacob's wives both come from his household.

senses.name: Bathsheba
senses.note: The wife of Uriah the Hittite, with whom David committed adultery; she later became David's wife and the mother of Solomon.

senses.name: Bathsheba
senses.note: The wife of Uriah the Hittite, with whom David committed adultery before arranging Uriah's death. She later became David's wife and Solomon's mother.

senses.name: Gebim
senses.note: A village north of Jerusalem whose people flee before the invader in Isaiah's poem; its location is unknown.

senses.name: Gebal
senses.note: A place or people among Israel's enemies; perhaps the Phoenician city of Byblos, or a region near Edom. Its identity is uncertain.

senses.name: Geba
senses.note: A town of Benjamin a few miles north of Jerusalem, on the invasion route Isaiah pictures the Assyrians taking.

senses.name: Gibeah
senses.note: A town of Benjamin a few miles north of Jerusalem, Saul's hometown. Isaiah pictures its people fleeing an invader advancing on Jerusalem.

senses.name: Gibeon
senses.note: A town a few miles north-west of Jerusalem; Isaiah recalls the LORD's past victories there as a picture of his coming deed.

senses.name: Gad
senses.note: A god of good fortune whom some in Isaiah's day honoured by setting tables of food. He is paired with Meni, a god of destiny.

senses.name: Gad
senses.note: A son of Jacob by Zilpah, Leah's slave woman; Leah named him for good fortune. He became the ancestor of the tribe of Gad.

senses.name: Gozan
senses.note: A city and district on the Habor river in northern Mesopotamia, conquered by Assyria.

senses.name: Goyim
senses.note: A kingdom ruled by Tidal, one of the four kings who raided the Jordan valley in Abraham's time. The name means 'nations', and where it lay is uncertain.

senses.name: Guni
senses.note: A son of Naphtali, listed among Jacob's family who went down to Egypt.

senses.name: Gaham
senses.note: A son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by his secondary wife Reumah; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: the Valley of Salt
senses.note: A valley where Israel defeated Edom, probably south of the Dead Sea; the exact site is uncertain.

senses.name: Valley of Salt
senses.note: A valley probably south of the Dead Sea where David's forces defeated the Edomites.

senses.name: Gihon
senses.note: The second of the four rivers flowing from Eden, said to wind through the land of Cush. Which river is meant is uncertain.

senses.name: Adrammelech
senses.note: A son of Sennacherib king of Assyria who, with his brother Sharezer, killed his father in the temple of Nisroch and fled to Ararat.

senses.name: Galilee
senses.note: The northern region of Israel around the Sea of Galilee, lands of Zebulun and Naphtali, which Assyria overran early. Isaiah calls it Galilee of the nations.

senses.name: Gallim
senses.note: A village north of Jerusalem in the land of Benjamin, on the route of an invading army in Isaiah's oracle. Its exact site is uncertain.

senses.name: Galeed
senses.note: The name Jacob gave to the heap of stones he and Laban set up in Gilead as a witness to their agreement. Laban gave it an Aramaic name with the same meaning.

senses.name: Gilead
senses.note: A hilly, fertile region east of the Jordan River, known for its balm. Jacob and Laban made their agreement there.

senses.name: Gomer
senses.note: Son of Japheth in the table of nations, and father of Ashkenaz, Riphath and Togarmah. The name probably stands for a people later known as the Cimmerians.

senses.name: Gatam
senses.note: A grandson of Esau through Eliphaz, listed among the clan chiefs of Edom; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Ohad
senses.note: A son of Simeon, son of Jacob, listed among those who went down to Egypt; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Gera
senses.note: A son of Benjamin, listed among Jacob's family who went down to Egypt.

senses.name: Gerar
senses.note: A town in the south-west of Canaan, between Gaza and Beersheba, ruled by Abimelech. Both Abraham and Isaac lived there for a time and passed off their wives as sisters.

senses.name: Gershon
senses.note: The eldest son of Levi and ancestor of the Gershonite clans of Levites; his sons were Libni and Shimei.

senses.name: Gershom
senses.note: The first son of Moses and Zipporah, born in Midian; his name sounds like the Hebrew for 'a foreigner there', recalling Moses' life as an outsider.

senses.name: Goshen
senses.note: A fertile grazing region in the eastern Nile delta of Egypt where Joseph settled Jacob's family. The Israelites lived there until the exodus, and it was spared some of the plagues.

senses.name: Gath
senses.note: One of the five main Philistine cities, Goliath's home town. David fled there from Saul, and the Philistines seized him.

senses.name: Gether
senses.note: A son of Aram in the table of nations; nothing more is known of him or the people named after him.

senses.name: Doeg
senses.note: An Edomite, Saul's chief herdsman, who told Saul that the priest Ahimelech had helped David, and then killed the priests of Nob at Saul's order.

senses.name: Deborah
senses.note: Rebekah's nurse, who came with her from Haran. She died near Bethel and was buried under an oak named for the weeping over her.

senses.name: Dibri
senses.note: A man of the tribe of Dan whose daughter Shelomith was mother of the man stoned for blasphemy; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Oholiab
senses.note: Son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, a skilled engraver, designer and weaver who worked with Bezalel on the tabernacle and its furnishings.

senses.name: Dedan son of Raamah
senses.note: A son of Raamah and descendant of Cush in the table of nations, ancestor of a people in Arabia.

senses.name: Dedan son of Jokshan
senses.note: A grandson of Abraham and Keturah through Jokshan, and ancestor of three Arabian tribes.

senses.name: the Dodanim
senses.note: A people descended from Javan in the table of nations, perhaps the people of Rhodes, as some manuscripts read; the identification is uncertain.

senses.name: Oholibamah
senses.note: A wife of Esau, daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite, and mother of Jeush, Jalam and Korah.

senses.name: Oholibamah (chief)
senses.note: A chief or clan of Edom listed among those descended from Esau, perhaps named after Esau's wife; nothing more is known.

senses.name: David
senses.note: Israel's second king, from Bethlehem in Judah, who made Jerusalem his capital. Many psalms bear his name, and God's promise of a lasting royal line made his family the hope of later kings.

senses.name: Dumah (son of Ishmael)
senses.note: A son of Ishmael, listed among the ancestors of Arabian tribes. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Dumah
senses.note: The subject of a short oracle in Isaiah, probably an oasis in northern Arabia named after Ishmael's son; the mention of Seir suggests a link with Edom.

senses.name: Aaron
senses.note: Elder brother of Moses, from the tribe of Levi, who spoke for him before Pharaoh. He became Israel's first high priest, and his sons served as priests after him; he also made the golden calf.

senses.name: Dibon
senses.note: A town of Moab east of the Dead Sea, north of the Arnon river, whose people go up to their high places to weep in Isaiah's oracle.

senses.name: Dimon
senses.note: A town of Moab, probably a form of Dibon chosen because it sounds like the Hebrew word for blood.

senses.name: Dinah
senses.note: Daughter of Jacob and Leah. After Shechem son of Hamor violated her, her brothers Simeon and Levi took violent revenge on his town.

senses.name: Dishon son of Seir
senses.note: A son of Seir the Horite and one of the Horite chiefs in the land of Edom; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Dishon son of Anah
senses.note: A son of Anah and grandson of Seir the Horite, brother of Oholibamah; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Dishan
senses.note: The youngest son of Seir the Horite and a Horite chief in Edom, father of Uz and Aran. He is known only from these lists.

senses.name: Damascus
senses.note: An ancient city in Syria, north-east of Galilee, capital of the kingdom of Aram in Isaiah's day. It allied with Israel against Judah and fell to Assyria in 732 BC.

senses.name: Dan
senses.note: The son of Jacob by Bilhah, Rachel's slave woman; Rachel named him, saying God had judged her case. He is ancestor of the tribe of Dan.

senses.name: the tribe of Dan
senses.note: The Israelite tribe descended from Dan, son of Jacob. Oholiab, the craftsman of the tabernacle, came from it.

senses.name: Dan (town)
senses.note: A town in the far north of Israel, near the sources of the Jordan; Genesis uses its later name for the place Abram reached chasing the kings.

senses.name: Dinhabah
senses.note: The city of Bela son of Beor, king of Edom. Its location is unknown.

senses.name: Diklah
senses.note: A son of Joktan in the table of nations, ancestor of a people probably in Arabia; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Uzal
senses.note: A son of Joktan, linked with a people or place in southern Arabia, perhaps in Yemen. He is known only from these lists.

senses.name: Dothan
senses.note: A town in the hills north of Shechem, on a trade route, where Joseph's brothers sold him to traders bound for Egypt.

senses.name: Abel
senses.note: The second son of Adam and Eve, a keeper of sheep and goats. The LORD accepted his offering, and his jealous brother Cain killed him; Seth was later born in his place.

senses.name: Hagar
senses.note: An Egyptian slave of Sarah whom Sarah gave to Abraham as a wife; she bore him Ishmael. Twice she ended up in the wilderness, and both times God's angel met her and promised a future for her son.

senses.name: Hadad, son of Bedad
senses.note: A king of Edom, ruling from the city of Avith, who defeated the Midianites in the land of Moab.

senses.name: Hadoram
senses.note: A son of Joktan in the table of nations, probably the ancestor of an Arabian tribe; nothing more is known.

senses.name: Hadar
senses.note: A king of Edom whose city was Pau and whose wife was Mehetabel; he is the last king in the list.

senses.name: Hemam
senses.note: A son of Lotan, among the Horites of Seir. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Heman the Ezrahite
senses.note: A wise man and probably a musician, to whom Psalm 88 is credited. He may be the singer Heman of David's time, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Ham
senses.note: A town east of the Jordan where Kedorlaomer defeated the Zuzites; it is probably modern Ham in northern Jordan.

senses.name: Omar
senses.note: A son of Eliphaz and grandson of Esau who became a clan chief in Edom; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Hena
senses.note: A city whose king the Assyrians boast of having defeated; its location is unknown, perhaps in Syria or Mesopotamia.

senses.name: Haran
senses.note: A son of Terah and brother of Abram and Nahor, father of Lot, Milcah and Iscah. He died young in Ur of the Chaldeans.

senses.name: On
senses.note: An ancient Egyptian city near modern Cairo, a centre of sun worship, later called Heliopolis by the Greeks. Joseph's wife Asenath was the daughter of its priest Potiphera.

senses.name: Zeeb
senses.note: A prince of Midian captured and killed by Gideon's men; the psalm asks God to deal with Israel's enemies as with him.

senses.name: Zebulun
senses.note: The sixth son of Jacob and Leah, and ancestor of the tribe of Zebulun.

senses.name: Zebulun (tribe)
senses.note: The tribe descended from Jacob's son Zebulun, and its land in lower Galilee, between the Sea of Galilee and the Mediterranean coast.

senses.name: Zebah
senses.note: A king of Midian who, with Zalmunna, was captured and killed by Gideon.

senses.name: Onam
senses.note: A son of Shobal, among the descendants of Seir the Horite; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Onan
senses.note: The second son of Judah and his Canaanite wife. He refused to give his dead brother Er an heir by Tamar, and the LORD put him to death.

senses.name: Ophir
senses.note: A son of Joktan in the table of nations; the name was later given to a distant land famous for its gold, probably in Arabia or East Africa.

senses.name: Ophir
senses.note: A distant land famous for fine gold, reached by sea. Its location is uncertain; suggestions include south-west Arabia, East Africa and India.

senses.name: Zikri
senses.note: A son of Izhar and brother of Korah, in the Levite family of Kohath; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Zechariah son of Jeberekiah
senses.note: A man Isaiah called as a reliable witness to his written prophecy, along with Uriah the priest. Nothing more is known of him for certain.

senses.name: Zilpah
senses.note: Leah's slave woman, given to her by Laban. Leah gave her to Jacob as a wife, and she bore Gad and Asher.

senses.name: Zimran
senses.note: The first son of Abraham and Keturah; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Ur of the Chaldeans
senses.note: The city in southern Mesopotamia where Terah's family lived before setting out for Canaan; it is usually identified with the ruins of Ur in southern Iraq.

senses.name: Zaavan
senses.note: A son of Ezer and grandson of Seir the Horite. He is known only from this list.

senses.name: Uri
senses.note: Son of Hur of the tribe of Judah and father of Bezalel, the chief craftsman of the tabernacle; he is known only through his son.

senses.name: Zerah
senses.note: Son of Reuel and grandson of Esau, listed among the clan chiefs of Edom.

senses.name: Zerah
senses.note: Father of Jobab, an early king of Edom from Bozrah; nothing more is known of him. He may be the same as Esau's grandson, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Zerah
senses.note: One of the twin sons of Judah and Tamar, the brother of Perez. A scarlet thread was tied to his hand at birth, but his brother came out first.

senses.name: Uriah the priest
senses.note: A priest whom Isaiah called as a reliable witness. He is probably the priest of King Ahaz's day who built an altar copied from one in Damascus.

senses.name: Heber
senses.note: A son of Beriah and grandson of Asher, who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family. He is known only from the family lists.

senses.name: Hebron
senses.note: An ancient town in the hills of Judah, about 19 miles south of Jerusalem, earlier called Kiriath-arba. Abraham, Isaac and Jacob lived nearby at Mamre, and the family burial cave of Machpelah was there.

senses.name: Hebron
senses.note: A son of Kohath and grandson of Levi, ancestor of a Levite clan. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Haggi
senses.note: A son of Gad, among those who went down to Egypt with Jacob; ancestor of a Gadite clan.

senses.name: Abiasaph
senses.note: A son of Korah, of the tribe of Levi, and head of one of the Korahite clans. He is known only from these lists.

senses.name: Hadad
senses.note: One of the twelve sons of Ishmael, Abraham's son; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Tigris
senses.note: One of the four rivers flowing out of Eden, the great river of Mesopotamia that runs east of Assyria and joins the Euphrates near the Persian Gulf.

senses.name: Hobah
senses.note: A place north of Damascus to which Abram chased the four kings when he rescued Lot; its exact site is unknown.

senses.name: Eve
senses.note: The first woman, wife of the man (Adam). He named her Eve because she would be the mother of all the living; she bore Cain, Abel and Seth.

senses.name: Havilah
senses.note: A land around which the river Pishon flows, known for gold. Its location is uncertain; it is often placed in Arabia.

senses.name: Havilah, son of Cush
senses.note: A descendant of Ham through Cush in the table of nations, probably standing for a people of Arabia.

senses.name: Havilah, son of Joktan
senses.note: A descendant of Shem through Joktan in the table of nations, probably standing for a people of Arabia.

senses.name: Hul
senses.note: A son of Aram, named in the list of the nations descended from Shem. He is known only from this list.

senses.name: Hur
senses.note: A leader who helped Aaron hold up Moses' hands during the battle against Amalek and shared charge of the people while Moses was on the mountain. He may be the same man as Bezalel's grandfather.

senses.name: Hur, grandfather of Bezalel
senses.note: A man of the tribe of Judah, father of Uri and grandfather of the craftsman Bezalel. He may be the same man as Moses' helper Hur.

senses.name: Hushim
senses.note: The son of Dan who went down to Egypt with Jacob; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Husham
senses.note: An early king of Edom from the land of the Temanites, who succeeded Jobab and was followed by Hadad.

senses.name: Hazo
senses.note: A son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, and Milcah; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Hezekiah
senses.note: Hezekiah, king of Judah from about 715 to 686 BC, whose officials copied and collected further proverbs of Solomon.

senses.name: Hezekiah
senses.note: King of Judah in Isaiah's time (about 715 to 686 BC). He trusted the LORD when the Assyrian king Sennacherib threatened Jerusalem, recovered from a serious illness, and unwisely showed his treasures to envoys from Babylon.

senses.name: Hirah
senses.note: A man from the town of Adullam in the lowlands of Judah, a friend of Judah. He went with Judah to Timnah and was sent back to find Tamar.

senses.name: Hilkiah
senses.note: The father of Eliakim, King Hezekiah's palace administrator; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Ham
senses.note: One of the three sons of Noah, with Shem and Japheth, and ancestor of several peoples listed in Genesis 10.

senses.name: Ham (Egypt)
senses.note: A poetic name for Egypt, whose people Genesis 10 traces to Ham, son of Noah.

senses.name: Hemdan
senses.note: A son of Dishon, a Horite chief in Seir. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Hamul
senses.note: A son of Perez and grandson of Judah, among those who went down to Egypt with Jacob.

senses.name: Hamor
senses.note: A Hivite ruler of the region of Shechem and father of Shechem. After his son violated Dinah, he negotiated with Jacob's family, and Simeon and Levi killed him and his son.

senses.name: Hamath
senses.note: A city and kingdom on the Orontes River in Syria, modern Hama. Assyria conquered it, and its envoys boasted of this to Jerusalem.

senses.name: Enoch son of Cain
senses.note: Cain's son, after whom Cain named the city he was building; his line leads to Lamech. He is a different man from Enoch the son of Jared in Genesis 5.

senses.name: Enoch son of Jared
senses.note: A descendant of Seth through Jared and the father of Methuselah. Genesis says he walked with God and did not die in the usual way: God took him away after 365 years.

senses.name: Hanoch son of Reuben
senses.note: Reuben's eldest son, ancestor of one of the Reubenite clans.

senses.name: Hanoch son of Midian
senses.note: A son of Midian and grandson of Abraham through Keturah; he is named only in this list.

senses.name: Enoch, son of Cain
senses.note: Cain's first son, after whom Cain named the city he was building; a different man from Enoch the descendant of Seth in chapter 5.

senses.name: Hanes
senses.note: An Egyptian town to which Judah's envoys went seeking help; it is probably Heracleopolis, south of Memphis, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Huppim
senses.note: A son, or perhaps descendant, of Benjamin, named among those who went down to Egypt with Jacob. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: She Is My Delight
senses.note: A new name Isaiah gives to Jerusalem (Hephzibah), showing that the LORD delights in the city in place of its old name, Abandoned.

senses.name: Hephzibah
senses.note: A new name, meaning my delight is in her, that Isaiah says God will give to Zion, the restored Jerusalem.

senses.name: Hazazon-tamar
senses.note: A place where Amorites lived, conquered by Kedorlaomer's allies; later identified with En-gedi on the west shore of the Dead Sea.

senses.name: Hezron son of Reuben
senses.note: A son of Reuben and ancestor of one of the Reubenite clans.

senses.name: Hezron son of Perez
senses.note: A grandson of Judah through Perez. Later genealogies trace the line of David through him.

senses.name: Hazarmaveth
senses.note: A son of Joktan in the table of nations; the name probably survives in Hadramaut in southern Arabia.

senses.name: Ahaz
senses.note: King of Judah, son of Jotham, in Isaiah's time. When Aram and Israel threatened him, Isaiah urged him to trust the LORD and ask for a sign, which he refused.

senses.name: Horeb
senses.note: Another name for Mount Sinai, the mountain of God, where Moses met God at the burning bush and where Israel received the law.

senses.name: Hori
senses.note: A son of Lotan among the Horites, the earlier inhabitants of Seir; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Ahuzzath
senses.note: A counsellor of Abimelech king of Gerar, who came with him to make a treaty with Isaac.

senses.name: Hermon
senses.note: A high mountain range on the northern edge of Israel, between modern Lebanon and Syria, often snow-capped.

senses.name: Mount Hermon
senses.note: The highest mountain of the region, on Israel's northern border, near the sources of the Jordan. Its peaks are named in a psalm of longing for God far from the temple.

senses.name: Haran
senses.note: A city in northern Mesopotamia, in what is now south-eastern Turkey. Terah's family settled there on the way to Canaan, and Abraham's relatives, including Laban, lived there; it was later taken by Assyria.

senses.name: Horonaim
senses.note: A town of Moab on a road where refugees flee in Isaiah's lament. Its location is uncertain.

senses.name: Ehi
senses.note: A son of Benjamin, named in the family that went down to Egypt with Jacob. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Abida
senses.note: A son of Midian and grandson of Abraham and Keturah; known only from these lists.

senses.name: Heshbon
senses.note: A city east of the Jordan, north of the Dead Sea, once a royal city of the Amorites and later held by Moab. Isaiah mourns its ruined vineyards.

senses.name: Heth
senses.note: A son of Canaan in the table of nations, named as ancestor of the Hittites.

senses.name: the Hittites
senses.note: A people living in Canaan in the time of the patriarchs, around Hebron. Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah from them as a family grave, and Esau's Hittite wives grieve Rebekah.

senses.name: Tabeel
senses.note: The father of the man whom the kings of Aram and Israel planned to put on Judah's throne instead of Ahaz; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Tebah
senses.note: A son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by his secondary wife Reumah. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Ahimelech
senses.note: The priest at Nob who gave David bread and Goliath's sword when he fled from Saul. Doeg the Edomite reported it to Saul.

senses.name: Ahisamach
senses.note: Of the tribe of Dan, father of Oholiab, the craftsman who helped Bezalel build the tabernacle. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: the Nile
senses.note: The great river of Egypt, whose yearly flood watered the land and fed its farming and fishing. In Exodus Moses struck its water and it became blood; in Isaiah its drying up spells ruin for Egypt.

senses.name: Jabin
senses.note: A Canaanite king of Hazor whose army, led by Sisera, was defeated by Israel under Deborah and Barak at the Kishon river.

senses.name: Jabal
senses.note: A son of Lamech and Adah, Cain's descendants. Genesis names him as the forerunner of those who live in tents and raise livestock.

senses.name: the Jabbok
senses.note: A river east of the Jordan, in what is now Jordan, flowing west into the Jordan. Jacob crossed its ford on his way home and wrestled there through the night.

senses.name: Abihu
senses.note: The second son of Aaron, who went up Mount Sinai with the elders and was made a priest. He and his brother Nadab died when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD.

senses.name: Jeberekiah
senses.note: Father of Zechariah, one of the two reliable witnesses Isaiah chose; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Jegar-sahadutha
senses.note: The Aramaic name Laban gave to the heap of stones marking his pact with Jacob in Gilead; Jacob called it Galeed. Both names mean heap of witness.

senses.name: Jegar-sahadutha
senses.note: Laban's Aramaic name for the heap of stones set up as a witness to his covenant with Jacob; Jacob called the same heap Galeed in Hebrew.

senses.name: Jeduthun
senses.note: A Levite musician of David's time, named in some psalm headings. Whether the heading names him or a musical style linked to him is uncertain.

senses.name: Jidlaph
senses.note: A son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by Milcah. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Yah
senses.note: A short form of God's personal name, the LORD, used mostly in songs and prayers, and in the cry hallelujah, meaning 'praise Yah'.

senses.name: Judah
senses.note: The fourth son of Jacob and Leah. He suggested selling Joseph, had sons by Tamar, and later offered himself in Benjamin's place; Jacob's blessing gives his line the royal scepter.

senses.name: Judah (tribe and kingdom)
senses.note: The tribe descended from Judah, and the southern kingdom named after it, with Jerusalem as its capital and kings of David's line. Isaiah's prophecies are addressed mainly to Judah and Jerusalem.

senses.name: Judith
senses.note: A Hittite woman, daughter of Beeri, whom Esau married at forty; his marriages grieved Isaac and Rebekah.

senses.name: GOD
