senses.note: In capitals, GOD stands for the personal name of Israel's God (often written YHWH), used here together with the word Lord. Where the name stands alone it appears as the LORD.

senses.name: GOD (the LORD)
senses.note: The personal name of Israel's God, usually shown as LORD; where it follows "Lord" it is shown as GOD to avoid repeating the word.

senses.name: Joseph
senses.note: Jacob's son Joseph, whose name here stands for the people of Israel at the time of the exodus from Egypt.

senses.name: Joshua
senses.note: Joshua son of Nun, Moses' young assistant. He leads Israel in battle against Amalek, goes partway up the mountain with Moses, and stays at the tent of meeting; later he succeeds Moses as leader.

senses.name: Jahaz
senses.note: A town of Moab, north of the Arnon river, mentioned in Isaiah's lament over Moab.

senses.name: Joab
senses.note: David's nephew and army commander, here credited with a great victory over Edom in the Valley of Salt.

senses.name: Joah
senses.note: Son of Asaph and the royal recorder under King Hezekiah. He went out with Eliakim and Shebna to hear the Assyrian commander's demands outside Jerusalem.

senses.name: Iob
senses.note: A son of Issachar who went down to Egypt with Jacob; elsewhere he is called Jashub.

senses.name: Jobab son of Joktan
senses.note: A son of Joktan in the table of nations, ancestor of a people in Arabia; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Jobab son of Zerah
senses.note: An early king of Edom from Bozrah, who succeeded Bela; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Jubal
senses.note: A son of Lamech and Adah, a descendant of Cain, named as the first of those who play the lyre and flute.

senses.name: Jochebed
senses.note: A woman of the tribe of Levi, wife of Amram and mother of Aaron and Moses. She was also Amram's aunt.

senses.name: Javan
senses.note: A son of Japheth in the table of nations, whose descendants include Elishah, Tarshish and the Kittim; his name is linked with the Greeks of Ionia.

senses.name: Javan
senses.note: The Hebrew name for Greece, or the Greek lands of Ionia; Isaiah lists it among distant nations that would hear of the LORD's glory.

senses.name: Joseph
senses.note: Jacob's son by Rachel, sold into slavery in Egypt by his jealous brothers, who rose to govern Egypt under Pharaoh and saved his family from famine. Before he died he made Israel promise to carry his bones back to Canaan.

senses.name: Joseph (the tribes)
senses.note: In the Psalms Joseph's name stands for the tribes descended from him, Ephraim and Manasseh, and sometimes for the northern tribes of Israel as a whole.

senses.name: Jotham
senses.note: King of Judah in the eighth century BC, son of Uzziah and father of Ahaz. Isaiah began to prophesy during the reigns that included his.

senses.name: Hezekiah
senses.note: Hezekiah, king of Judah from about 715 to 686 BC, son of Ahaz. He trusted the LORD when Assyria besieged Jerusalem and is remembered as a reforming king.

senses.name: Jahleel
senses.note: A son of Zebulun who went down to Egypt with Jacob and became ancestor of a clan.

senses.name: Jahzeel
senses.note: A son of Naphtali who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family; ancestor of a Naphtalite clan.

senses.name: Jetur
senses.note: A son of Ishmael, probably the ancestor of the Itureans, a people north-east of Galilee.

senses.name: Jachin
senses.note: A son of Simeon and founder of a Simeonite clan, also spelled Jakin; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Jemuel
senses.note: The eldest son of Simeon and head of a Simeonite clan; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Jamin
senses.note: The second son of Simeon, son of Jacob, and head of a Simeonite clan. He is known only from the family lists.

senses.name: Imnah
senses.note: The first-named son of Asher, listed among Jacob's family who went down to Egypt.

senses.name: Iscah
senses.note: Daughter of Haran and sister of Milcah and Lot; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Jeush
senses.note: A son of Esau and Oholibamah, born in Canaan, who became a chief of Edom.

senses.name: Jazer
senses.note: A town east of the Jordan, in vine country north of Heshbon; Isaiah mourns its vineyards in his oracle against Moab. Its exact site is uncertain.

senses.name: Jalam
senses.note: A son of Esau by Oholibamah who became a clan chief in Edom; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Jacob
senses.note: Son of Isaac and Rebekah and twin brother of Esau, also named Israel. His twelve sons became the ancestors of the tribes of Israel, and God is often called the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

senses.name: Jacob (the people of Israel)
senses.note: The nation descended from Jacob, called by his name, especially in poetry and prophecy where Jacob stands in parallel with Israel. Phrases like "the house of Jacob" and "the God of Jacob" refer to this people.

senses.name: Atad's threshing floor
senses.note: A place beyond the Jordan where Joseph and the Egyptians mourned Jacob for seven days; it was renamed Abel-mizraim. The location is uncertain.

senses.name: Japheth
senses.note: One of Noah's three sons, with Shem and Ham, who survived the flood; later chapters trace many peoples back to him.

senses.name: Izhar
senses.note: A son of Kohath and grandson of Levi, and father of Korah, who later rebelled against Moses.

senses.name: Isaac
senses.note: Son of Abraham and Sarah, born in their old age and heir to God's promises. He married Rebekah and was father of the twins Esau and Jacob.

senses.name: Jezer
senses.note: A son of Naphtali who went down to Egypt with Jacob and became ancestor of a clan.

senses.name: Jakeh
senses.note: The father of Agur, whose sayings are collected in Proverbs 30. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Joktan
senses.note: A son of Eber and brother of Peleg, in the line of Shem. His thirteen sons are linked with peoples of southern Arabia.

senses.name: Jokshan
senses.note: A son of Abraham by Keturah, and father of Sheba and Dedan.

senses.name: Jared
senses.note: A descendant of Seth through Mahalalel and the father of Enoch, who in turn fathered Methuselah. Genesis gives him a lifespan of 962 years.

senses.name: Jordan
senses.note: The main river of the land, flowing south from near Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee into the Dead Sea. Its valley and the land beyond it to the east are often named after it.

senses.name: Jerusalem
senses.note: The city in the hills of Judah that David made his capital, where Solomon built the temple on Mount Zion. In Isaiah and the Psalms it stands for the people of Judah and for God's dwelling among them.

senses.name: Jerah
senses.note: A son of Joktan, descended from Shem, probably standing for a tribe of southern Arabia; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Ishbak
senses.note: A son of Abraham by Keturah. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Ishvah
senses.note: A son of Asher who went down to Egypt with Jacob; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Ishvi
senses.note: A son of Asher who went down to Egypt with Jacob. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Jesse
senses.note: A man of Bethlehem, grandson of Ruth and Boaz, and father of King David. Isaiah speaks of a new shoot rising from his line.

senses.name: Aiah
senses.note: A son of Zibeon among the Horite clans of Seir in Edom; named only in this list.

senses.name: Ishmael
senses.note: Son of Abraham by Hagar, Sarah's Egyptian slave. God promised to make him a great nation, and he became father of twelve tribal chiefs.

senses.name: Isaiah son of Amoz
senses.note: A prophet in Jerusalem in the eighth century BC, during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah. He advised Hezekiah during the Assyrian siege, and the book of Isaiah carries his visions and oracles.

senses.name: Israel (Jacob)
senses.note: The name God gave to Jacob, son of Isaac and grandson of Abraham, after he wrestled at the Jabbok. His twelve sons became the ancestors of the tribes of Israel.

senses.name: Israel (the northern kingdom)
senses.note: The northern kingdom of the ten tribes, with Samaria as its capital, in Isaiah's day allied with Aram against Judah; it fell to Assyria in 722 BC.

senses.name: Israel
senses.note: The people descended from Jacob, also called Israel: the twelve tribes God brought out of Egypt and bound to himself by covenant. Prophets and psalms often pair the name with Jacob for the whole nation.

senses.name: Jeshurun
senses.note: A poetic, affectionate name for Israel, probably meaning upright one.

senses.name: Issachar
senses.note: Jacob's fifth son by Leah and ancestor of the tribe named after him. Jacob's blessing compares him to a strong donkey.

senses.name: Jethro
senses.note: A priest of Midian and the father-in-law of Moses, called Jether in this verse; Moses asked his leave before returning to Egypt.

senses.name: Jethro
senses.note: A priest of Midian and the father-in-law of Moses, who sheltered Moses for years. He later brought Zipporah and her sons to Moses, praised the LORD for the rescue from Egypt, and advised Moses on judging.

senses.name: Ithran
senses.note: A son of Dishon, among the Horites of Seir. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Jetheth
senses.note: A chief or clan of Edom listed among those descended from Esau. Nothing more is known.

senses.name: Kedorlaomer
senses.note: A king of Elam who led four eastern kings against the cities of the Jordan plain, including Sodom. Abram defeated him and rescued Lot.

senses.name: Elon
senses.note: A Hittite of Canaan, father of a wife of Esau. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Elon
senses.note: A son of Zebulun, listed among Jacob's family who went down to Egypt.

senses.name: Cyrus
senses.note: Cyrus the Great, king of Persia, who conquered Babylon in 539 BC and let exiled peoples, including the Jews, return home. Isaiah calls him the LORD's shepherd and anointed.

senses.name: Cush, son of Ham
senses.note: A son of Ham in the table of nations, father of Nimrod and ancestor of peoples of the Nile region south of Egypt and of Arabia.

senses.name: Cush the Benjaminite
senses.note: A man of the tribe of Benjamin named in the heading of Psalm 7, apparently an enemy of David. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Cush
senses.note: A land around which the river Gihon is said to wind. Elsewhere Cush is the region south of Egypt (ancient Nubia), but its meaning here is uncertain.

senses.name: Cush
senses.note: The land south of Egypt along the upper Nile, roughly ancient Nubia in today's Sudan. In Isaiah's time its kings also ruled Egypt, and Tirhakah was one of them.

senses.name: Kezib
senses.note: A place in Judah where Judah was when his son Shelah was born; probably the same as Achzib in the lowlands.

senses.name: Elim
senses.note: An oasis with twelve springs and seventy palm trees where the Israelites camped after Marah, on the way to the wilderness of Sin. The site is uncertain.

senses.name: Calah
senses.note: An Assyrian city on the Tigris built by Nimrod, later known as Nimrud, south of Nineveh in modern Iraq.

senses.name: El-paran
senses.note: A place on the edge of the wilderness south of Seir, the farthest point reached by the eastern kings; possibly Elath on the Gulf of Aqaba.

senses.name: Calneh
senses.note: One of the first cities of Nimrod's kingdom in Shinar (Babylonia); its location is uncertain.

senses.name: Calno
senses.note: A city in northern Syria conquered by Assyria, named in Isaiah as a warning that no city can stand against Assyria. Its location is uncertain.

senses.name: Canaan son of Ham
senses.note: A son of Ham and grandson of Noah, whom Noah cursed after Ham's offense. Genesis names him as the ancestor of Sidon, Heth and the peoples of the land later called Canaan.

senses.name: Canaan
senses.note: The land between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean, named after its earlier peoples, which God promised to Abraham's descendants. In Isaiah 23 the name points to the Phoenician coast of Tyre and Sidon.

senses.name: Carchemish
senses.note: A fortified city on the upper Euphrates, now on the Turkey-Syria border, which fell to Assyria in 717 BC.

senses.name: Carmi
senses.note: A son of Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, and head of one of the Reubenite clans.

senses.name: Carmel
senses.note: The wooded mountain ridge running to the Mediterranean coast near modern Haifa, famous for its fertility. Isaiah uses it as a picture of lush beauty that withers or is restored.

senses.name: Cheran
senses.note: A son of Dishon among the Horite clans of Seir; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Chesed
senses.note: A son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by Milcah; his name may be linked with the Chaldeans, but nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: the Chaldeans
senses.note: A people of southern Mesopotamia who later ruled Babylon; the name often stands for the Babylonians. Abraham's family came from Ur of the Chaldeans, and Isaiah foretells Babylon's fall.

senses.name: the Kittim
senses.note: A people descended from Javan in the table of nations, generally linked with Cyprus.

senses.name: Kittim
senses.note: Cyprus, named from its town of Kition, a trading partner of Tyre and Sidon; Isaiah pictures the Phoenicians hearing of Tyre's fall from there.

senses.name: Leah
senses.note: Elder daughter of Laban and the first wife of Jacob, given to him in place of her sister Rachel. She bore six of his sons, among them Levi and Judah, and a daughter, Dinah.

senses.name: the Leummites
senses.note: An Arabian people descended from Dedan, a grandson of Abraham and Keturah; nothing more is known of them.

senses.name: Laban
senses.note: Rebekah's brother, son of Bethuel, living in Paddan-aram. He becomes Jacob's uncle and father-in-law, giving him Leah and Rachel, and the two men deal shrewdly with each other over wages and flocks.

senses.name: Ithiel
senses.note: A person to whom Agur addresses his sayings, along with Ucal; nothing more is known of him, and some read the words differently.

senses.name: Libnah
senses.note: A town in the lowlands of Judah, near Lachish, which the Assyrian king Sennacherib attacked.

senses.name: Lebanon
senses.note: The mountain range north of Israel, famous for its tall cedars and forests. The poets use it as a picture of height, pride, beauty and abundance.

senses.name: Libni
senses.note: A son of Gershon and grandson of Levi, ancestor of a Levite clan.

senses.name: Ithamar
senses.note: The youngest of Aaron's four sons, made a priest with his father. He oversaw the Levites' record of the tabernacle and remained a priest after his brothers Nadab and Abihu died.

senses.name: Lud, son of Shem
senses.note: A son of Shem in the table of nations, probably standing for a people; their identity is uncertain.

senses.name: Lud
senses.note: A distant people famous as archers, named among nations far off. They may be the Lydians of western Asia Minor, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Ethan the Ezrahite
senses.note: A wise man named in a psalm heading; 1 Kings counts him among famous sages, and he may be the same as a Levite singer of David's time.

senses.name: Luz
senses.note: The older name of the town Jacob renamed Bethel, about ten miles north of Jerusalem, where God appeared to him in a dream.

senses.name: Luhith
senses.note: A place in Moab reached by an ascent on the refugees' route; its location is uncertain.

senses.name: Lot
senses.note: Son of Haran and nephew of Abram, who travelled with him to Canaan, then settled near Sodom. Rescued before Sodom was destroyed, he became through his daughters the ancestor of Moab and Ammon.

senses.name: Lotan
senses.note: The eldest son of Seir the Horite and a Horite chief in the land of Edom; his sister was Timna. He is known only from these lists.

senses.name: Levi
senses.note: The third son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the tribe of Levi, from which Moses, Aaron and the priests came. With Simeon he took violent revenge on Shechem for their sister Dinah.

senses.name: Abimael
senses.note: A son of Joktan, descended from Shem, named in the table of nations; probably ancestor of a tribe in Arabia. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Akkad
senses.note: An ancient city in Mesopotamia, north of Babylon, capital of a powerful early empire. It gave its name to the region and to the Akkadian language; its exact site has not been found.

senses.name: the Letushites
senses.note: An Arabian tribe descended from Dedan, grandson of Abraham and Keturah; nothing more is known of them.

senses.name: Laishah
senses.note: A village just north of Jerusalem in the land of Benjamin, on the route of the Assyrian advance in Isaiah's vision. Its exact site is uncertain.

senses.name: Lachish
senses.note: A strongly fortified city of Judah south-west of Jerusalem. The Assyrian king Sennacherib besieged it and sent his officer from there to demand Jerusalem's surrender.

senses.name: Lemuel
senses.note: A king named only in Proverbs 31, whose mother taught him the sayings recorded there. Who he was is unknown.

senses.name: Lamech, descendant of Cain
senses.note: A descendant of Cain in the fifth generation, husband of Adah and Zillah and father of Jabal, Jubal, Tubal-Cain and Naamah. He boasts of killing a man and claims far greater vengeance than Cain.

senses.name: Lamech, father of Noah
senses.note: A descendant of Seth, son of Methuselah and father of Noah; a different man from Cain's descendant Lamech in chapter 4. He lived 777 years.

senses.name: Lasha
senses.note: A place at the edge of Canaan's territory, near Sodom and Gomorrah. Its location is unknown.

senses.name: Abimelech king of Gerar
senses.note: A Philistine king at Gerar in the western Negev who took Sarah into his household and later made a treaty with Abraham. The Abimelech of Isaac's day may be the same man or a later king of that name.

senses.name: Abimelech (in a psalm title)
senses.note: The name the psalm heading gives to the king before whom David pretended to be insane; the account in 1 Samuel calls this king Achish of Gath. Abimelech may have been a royal title.

senses.name: Ucal
senses.note: A person to whom Agur addresses his sayings, along with Ithiel. Some read the words differently, as a lament rather than names.

senses.name: Mibzar
senses.note: Named among the clan chiefs of Edom descended from Esau; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Mibsam
senses.note: The fourth son of Ishmael. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Migdol
senses.note: A place near the sea on Egypt's eastern border, named with Pi-hahiroth where Israel camped before crossing; the name means "tower". Its location is uncertain.

senses.name: Magdiel
senses.note: One of the chiefs of Edom descended from Esau; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Migdal-eder
senses.note: A place between Bethlehem and Hebron where Jacob camped after Rachel's death; the name means tower of the flock. Its exact site is unknown.

senses.name: Magog
senses.note: A son of Japheth in the table of nations, probably standing for a people in the far north; Ezekiel later uses the name for a distant hostile land.

senses.name: Migron
senses.note: A place in Benjamin north of Jerusalem, on the route of an invading army in Isaiah's poem; its exact site is uncertain.

senses.name: Madai
senses.note: A son of Japheth in the table of nations, regarded as the ancestor of the Medes.

senses.name: the Medes
senses.note: A people of the Iranian plateau, east of Assyria. With the Persians they captured Babylon in 539 BC, as Isaiah foresaw.

senses.name: Midian, son of Abraham
senses.note: A son of Abraham by Keturah, and ancestor of the Midianites.

senses.name: Midian
senses.note: A desert region east of the Gulf of Aqaba and the people who lived there, the Midianites. Moses fled there and married the daughter of its priest Jethro; later Gideon's defeat of Midian became a byword for God's rescue.

senses.name: Madmenah
senses.note: A village north of Jerusalem on the invader's route in Isaiah's vision. Its location is uncertain.

senses.name: Medan
senses.note: A son of Abraham by Keturah; named only in family lists.

senses.name: God Almighty
senses.note: A title of God (in Hebrew, El Shaddai) by which he makes himself known to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, especially when promising them descendants.

senses.name: Mehetabel
senses.note: Wife of Hadar, an early king of Edom, and daughter of Matred; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Mahalalel
senses.note: A descendant of Seth in the line from Adam to Noah: son of Kenan and father of Jared. He lived 895 years; nothing else is told of him.

senses.name: Maher-shalal-hash-baz
senses.note: A son of Isaiah and the prophetess; his name, roughly "quick to the plunder, swift to the spoil", signalled that Assyria would soon plunder Damascus and Samaria.

senses.name: Moab
senses.note: Son of Lot by his older daughter, born after the destruction of Sodom; Genesis names him as ancestor of the Moabites.

senses.name: Moab
senses.note: The land and people east of the Dead Sea, descended from Lot and often hostile to Israel. Isaiah 15–16 is a lament and oracle over its towns.

senses.name: Moreh
senses.note: A great tree near Shechem, probably a sacred oak or terebinth, where God appeared to Abram on his arrival in Canaan.

senses.name: Moriah
senses.note: The land with the mountain where God told Abraham to offer Isaac. Later tradition links it with the temple hill in Jerusalem.

senses.name: Mushi
senses.note: A son of Merari and grandson of Levi, ancestor of a clan of Levites.

senses.name: Mizzah
senses.note: A son of Reuel and grandson of Esau and Basemath, and a chief in Edom; known only from these lists.

senses.name: Eldaah
senses.note: A son of Midian and grandson of Abraham and Keturah; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Mehujael
senses.note: A descendant of Cain, son of Irad and father of Methushael, in the line leading to Lamech in Genesis 4.

senses.name: Mehujael
senses.note: A descendant of Cain, son of Irad and grandfather of Lamech. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Mahli
senses.note: A son of Merari and grandson of Levi, ancestor of a Levite clan.

senses.name: Elah
senses.note: Named among the clan chiefs of Edom descended from Esau; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Mahalath
senses.note: Daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth, whom Esau married after seeing that his parents disliked Canaanite wives.

senses.name: Mahanaim
senses.note: A place east of the Jordan, near the Jabbok, named by Jacob after he met angels there; the name means two camps.

senses.name: Matred
senses.note: The mother of Mehetabel, wife of the Edomite king Hadar; she is known only from this family note.

senses.name: Medeba
senses.note: A town of Moab on the plateau east of the Dead Sea, today's Madaba in Jordan.

senses.name: Mishael
senses.note: A Levite, son of Uzziel and cousin of Aaron. With his brother Elzaphan he carried out the bodies of Nadab and Abihu.

senses.name: Machir
senses.note: A son of Manasseh and grandson of Joseph, whose children were born while Joseph lived; his descendants became a leading clan of Manasseh.

senses.name: Michmash
senses.note: A town of Benjamin north of Jerusalem, on the route of the invading Assyrian army in Isaiah's vision.

senses.name: Machpelah
senses.note: A field with a cave east of Mamre, at Hebron, which Abraham bought from Ephron the Hittite as a family tomb. Sarah, Abraham, Isaac, Rebekah, Leah and Jacob were buried there.

senses.name: Allon-bacuth
senses.note: The oak below Bethel where Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, was buried. The name means oak of weeping.

senses.name: Allon-bacuth
senses.note: The oak below Bethel where Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, was buried; the name means oak of weeping.

senses.name: Molech
senses.note: A god of the peoples around Israel worshipped by passing children through fire, probably as child sacrifice. The law of Moses forbids it under penalty of death.

senses.name: Milcah
senses.note: Daughter of Haran and wife of Abraham's brother Nahor. She bears him eight sons, among them Bethuel, so she is Rebekah's grandmother.

senses.name: Malkiel
senses.note: A son of Beriah and grandson of Asher, who went down to Egypt with Jacob; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Melchizedek
senses.note: King of Salem and priest of God Most High, who brought bread and wine to Abram and blessed him. Salem is usually taken to be Jerusalem.

senses.name: Melchizedek
senses.note: King of Salem and priest of God Most High, who met Abram with bread and wine after his victory and blessed him; Abram gave him a tenth of the spoil.

senses.name: Mamre the Amorite
senses.note: An Amorite, brother of Eshcol and Aner, who was allied with Abram and joined him in rescuing Lot. The oaks where Abram camped bore his name.

senses.name: Mamre
senses.note: A place of great trees near Hebron where Abraham camped and built an altar. The cave of Machpelah, the family burial place, lay to the east of it.

senses.name: Manahath
senses.note: A son of Shobal, among the Horite clans of Seir in Edom; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Meni
senses.note: A god of fate or fortune, honoured with offerings alongside Gad; his worship is condemned in Isaiah.

senses.name: Massah
senses.note: A place in the wilderness near Rephidim where Israel tested the LORD by demanding water; its name means testing. It is also called Meribah.

senses.name: Maacah
senses.note: A child of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by his secondary wife Reumah. The name was later linked with a small Aramean kingdom north-east of Galilee.

senses.name: Eliezer of Damascus
senses.note: A member of Abram's household who, Abram complained, would inherit from him since he had no child.

senses.name: Eliezer, son of Moses
senses.note: The second son of Moses and Zipporah, named to recall that God had helped Moses and rescued him from Pharaoh.

senses.name: Eliphaz
senses.note: Esau's firstborn son, by his wife Adah. His sons, including Teman and Amalek, became clan chiefs in Edom.

senses.name: Muppim
senses.note: A son of Benjamin who went down to Egypt with Jacob; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Egypt
senses.note: A poetic name for Egypt, used here in Isaiah's oracles about its rivers and canals drying up.

senses.name: Elzaphan
senses.note: A Levite, son of Uzziel and cousin of Aaron. With his brother Mishael he carried the bodies of Nadab and Abihu out of the camp.

senses.name: Mizpah
senses.note: A name, meaning "watchtower", given to the stone heap in Gilead where Jacob and Laban made their agreement and asked the LORD to watch between them.

senses.name: Eliakim
senses.note: Son of Hilkiah, palace administrator under King Hezekiah of Judah, chosen to replace Shebna. He was one of the officials who met the Assyrian commander during the siege of Jerusalem.

senses.name: Egypt
senses.note: A son of Ham in the table of nations, presented as the ancestor of the Egyptians and of several peoples linked with them.

senses.name: Egypt
senses.note: The land of the Nile valley in north-east Africa and its people, the Egyptians. Joseph rose to power there, Jacob's family settled there, and Israel was later enslaved there until God brought them out under Moses.

senses.name: Elisheba
senses.note: The wife of Aaron, daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshon of Judah, and mother of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

senses.name: Elishah
senses.note: A son of Javan in the table of nations, ancestor of a seafaring people, perhaps on Cyprus; the identification is uncertain.

senses.name: Merodach-baladan
senses.note: A Chaldean king of Babylon who fought Assyria. He sent envoys and a gift to Hezekiah after his illness, and Hezekiah showed them all his treasures.

senses.name: Marah
senses.note: A place in the wilderness three days from the sea crossing, named for its bitter water, which the LORD made sweet.

senses.name: Meribah
senses.note: A place near Rephidim in the wilderness where the Israelites quarrelled with Moses over water and tested the LORD. Its name means quarrelling, and the Psalms recall it as a warning.

senses.name: Miriam
senses.note: Sister of Aaron and Moses and a prophetess. After the crossing of the sea she leads the women with tambourines and dancing in a song to the LORD.

senses.name: Merari
senses.note: The third son of Levi and ancestor of the Merarite clans of Levites, through his sons Mahli and Mushi.

senses.name: Mash
senses.note: A son of Aram listed in the table of nations, probably standing for an Aramean people; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Mesha
senses.note: One end of the region where Joktan's descendants lived, probably in Arabia; its location is uncertain.

senses.name: Massa
senses.note: A son of Ishmael, probably the ancestor of an Arabian tribe. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Almodad
senses.note: The first-named son of Joktan in the table of nations, probably standing for a people of Arabia. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Moses
senses.note: The Israelite leader through whom the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt and gave the law at Sinai. Brother of Aaron and Miriam, he speaks with Pharaoh, leads the people through the wilderness, and receives God's instructions for worship.

senses.name: Meshech
senses.note: A son of Japheth and ancestor of a people of the same name, probably living in central or eastern Asia Minor.

senses.name: Mishma
senses.note: A son of Ishmael and ancestor of an Arabian tribe; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Ellasar
senses.note: The kingdom of Arioch, one of the four eastern kings who invaded the Jordan valley in Abraham's time. Its location is uncertain; it was somewhere in Mesopotamia or Asia Minor.

senses.name: Masrekah
senses.note: The home town of Samlah, an early king of Edom. Its location is unknown.

senses.name: Methushael
senses.note: A descendant of Cain, son of Mehujael and father of Lamech; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Methuselah
senses.note: The son of Enoch and father of Lamech in the line from Seth to Noah. At 969 years he is the longest-lived person recorded in the Bible.

senses.name: Eleazar
senses.note: The third son of Aaron, who served with his father as a priest. After his brothers Nadab and Abihu died he and Ithamar remained, and he later succeeded Aaron as high priest; Phinehas was his son.

senses.name: Elealeh
senses.note: A town in Moab, east of the Jordan, close to Heshbon. Isaiah mourns it in his oracle against Moab.

senses.name: Nob
senses.note: A priestly town of Benjamin just north of Jerusalem, within sight of the city, where Isaiah pictures the Assyrian invader halting.

senses.name: Nebo
senses.note: A Babylonian god, Nabu, god of writing and wisdom and son of Marduk (Bel). Isaiah pictures his images carted off like baggage.

senses.name: Nebo
senses.note: A town in Moab east of the Jordan, near the mountain of the same name. Isaiah lists it among the places of Moab that mourn.

senses.name: Nebaioth
senses.note: The firstborn son of Ishmael and brother of Mahalath and Basemath, whom Esau married.

senses.name: Nebaioth
senses.note: An Arabian tribe descended from Ishmael's son Nebaioth, known for its flocks. Isaiah pictures its rams offered on God's altar.

senses.name: Nadab
senses.note: The eldest son of Aaron and Elisheba, who went up Mount Sinai with Moses. He and his brother Abihu died after offering unauthorized fire before the LORD.

senses.name: Elkanah
senses.note: A son of Korah the Levite and head of a Korahite clan; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Nod
senses.note: The land east of Eden where Cain settled after leaving the presence of the LORD. Its location is unknown.

senses.name: Nun
senses.note: Father of Joshua, Moses' assistant and successor; known only as Joshua's father.

senses.name: Noah
senses.note: Son of Lamech and father of Shem, Ham and Japheth. His father named him in hope of relief from the toil caused by the cursed ground; he is later the one saved through the flood.

senses.name: Nahor, grandfather of Abraham
senses.note: Son of Serug and father of Terah, named in the family line from Shem to Abraham.

senses.name: Nahor, brother of Abraham
senses.note: Son of Terah and brother of Abraham, named after his grandfather. He married Milcah and settled in northern Mesopotamia; Rebekah and Laban were his grandchildren.

senses.name: Nahshon
senses.note: Son of Amminadab and brother of Elisheba, Aaron's wife. He led the tribe of Judah in the wilderness and was an ancestor of David.

senses.name: Nahath
senses.note: A grandson of Esau through Reuel and Basemath, and a chief of an Edomite clan.

senses.name: Nineveh
senses.note: An ancient city on the Tigris River, across from modern Mosul in Iraq, which became the capital of the Assyrian empire. Sennacherib returned there after failing to take Jerusalem.

senses.name: Nimrod
senses.note: A son of Cush remembered as the first mighty warrior and a famous hunter, who founded kingdoms in Babylonia and Assyria.

senses.name: Nimrim
senses.note: A stream in Moab whose waters dry up in Isaiah's oracle; probably a wadi near the south-east end of the Dead Sea.

senses.name: Nisroch
senses.note: The god of the Assyrian king Sennacherib, in whose temple his sons killed him. The god is otherwise unknown.

senses.name: Naamah
senses.note: The daughter of Lamech and Zillah and sister of Tubal-cain, in Cain's line. Nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Naaman son of Benjamin
senses.note: Listed among Benjamin's sons who went down to Egypt with Jacob; elsewhere he appears as a grandson. He is not the Syrian commander healed by Elisha.

senses.name: Memphis
senses.note: An ancient capital of Egypt on the Nile, south of modern Cairo; Isaiah mocks the folly of its officials.

senses.name: Nepheg
senses.note: A son of Izhar and brother of Korah, among the Levites listed in Exodus; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Absalom
senses.note: A son of King David who rebelled against him and drove him from Jerusalem; the heading links Psalm 3 with that flight.

senses.name: Naphish
senses.note: A son of Ishmael and head of one of the twelve Ishmaelite tribes. He is known only from these lists.

senses.name: Amoz
senses.note: The father of the prophet Isaiah; he is known only through his son's name.

senses.name: Naphtali
senses.note: Jacob's son by Bilhah, Rachel's slave woman, and ancestor of the tribe named after him.

senses.name: the tribe of Naphtali
senses.note: The Israelite tribe descended from Naphtali, whose land lay west and north of the Sea of Galilee. Assyria overran it early, and Isaiah promises honor to that region.

senses.name: Nathan
senses.note: A prophet at David's court who confronted David over Bathsheba and Uriah; the heading of Psalm 51 links the psalm with that moment.

senses.name: Seba, son of Cush
senses.note: A descendant of Ham through Cush in the table of nations.

senses.name: Seba
senses.note: A distant land, probably in north-east Africa or southern Arabia, named with Cush and Sheba as a source of wealth and tribute.

senses.name: the Sabeans
senses.note: A tall people of Seba, probably in the upper Nile region or southern Arabia; Isaiah lists them with Egypt and Cush as nations that would submit to Israel.

senses.name: Sabtah
senses.note: A son of Cush, probably the ancestor of a people in Arabia; his name is known only from the table of nations.

senses.name: Sabteca
senses.note: A son of Cush in the table of nations, probably standing for a people of Arabia or Africa; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Sodom
senses.note: A city of the Jordan plain, probably near the south end of the Dead Sea, where Lot settled. Destroyed with Gomorrah for its wickedness, it became a byword for sin and judgment.

senses.name: the wilderness of Sin
senses.note: A desert region between Elim and Mount Sinai, probably in the south-west of the Sinai peninsula. There the Israelites complained of hunger and God gave them manna and quail.

senses.name: Sinai
senses.note: The mountain in the wilderness where God gave Israel the law through Moses, and the desert around it. Its exact location is uncertain; a traditional site is in the south of the Sinai peninsula.

senses.name: Sinim
senses.note: A distant land from which God's scattered people return. It is probably Syene, modern Aswan in southern Egypt.

senses.name: Sisera
senses.note: The commander of the army of Jabin, a Canaanite king, defeated by Barak and Deborah near the Kishon and killed by Jael.

senses.name: Succoth in Egypt
senses.note: The Israelites' first stopping place after leaving Rameses in the exodus, in the eastern Nile delta; the exact site is uncertain.

senses.name: Succoth
senses.note: A town east of the Jordan, near the Jabbok river, where Jacob built shelters for his livestock and gave the place its name, meaning 'booths'.

senses.name: Sela
senses.note: A rocky place in the region of Edom, south-east of the Dead Sea; its name means rock, and the exact site is uncertain.

senses.name: Sennacherib
senses.note: King of Assyria from 705 to 681 BC. He invaded Judah in 701 BC and threatened Jerusalem under Hezekiah, but withdrew to Nineveh, where he was later murdered by his own sons.

senses.name: Sephar
senses.note: A place marking one limit of the land of Joktan's descendants, in the eastern hill country, probably in southern Arabia. Its location is uncertain.

senses.name: Sepharvaim
senses.note: A city conquered by Assyria, whose gods and king the Assyrian envoys cited as unable to resist them. Its location is uncertain, probably in Syria.

senses.name: Sargon
senses.note: Sargon II, king of Assyria from 722 to 705 BC, whose commander captured the Philistine city of Ashdod around 711 BC.

senses.name: Sered
senses.note: A son of Zebulun who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family; ancestor of a Zebulunite clan.

senses.name: Sithri
senses.note: A Levite, son of Uzziel and grandson of Kohath, named in a family list; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Eber
senses.note: A descendant of Shem, son of Shelah and father of Peleg and Joktan. Many peoples are traced to him, and his name may be linked with the word Hebrew.

senses.name: Amraphel
senses.note: King of Shinar (Babylonia) and one of the four eastern kings who raided Canaan and carried off Lot. He has not been identified in other records.

senses.name: Eglath-shelishiyah
senses.note: A place in Moab, named with Zoar as a refuge of fleeing Moabites. Its location is unknown.

senses.name: Eglath-shelishiyah
senses.note: A place in Moab to which refugees flee in Isaiah's lament. Its location is unknown.

senses.name: Adah
senses.note: One of the two wives of Lamech, Cain's descendant, and mother of Jabal and Jubal. Lamech addresses his boastful song to her and Zillah.

senses.name: Adah, wife of Esau
senses.note: A wife of Esau, daughter of Elon the Hittite, and mother of Eliphaz, from whom several chiefs of Edom descended.

senses.name: the people of Eden
senses.note: The people of Beth-eden, an Aramean state on the upper Euphrates conquered by Assyria; it is not the garden of Eden.

senses.name: Eden
senses.note: The region where God planted the garden in which he placed the first man, with a river flowing out of it. The man was later sent out of the garden. Its location is unknown.

senses.name: Obal
senses.note: A son of Joktan in the table of nations, standing for an Arabian tribe; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Ivvah
senses.note: A city conquered by Assyria, perhaps in Syria. Its location is unknown.

senses.name: Avith
senses.note: The city of Hadad son of Bedad, an early king of Edom. Its location is unknown.

senses.name: Uz son of Aram
senses.note: A son of Aram in the table of nations, probably the ancestor of a people in Syria or Arabia.

senses.name: Uz son of Nahor
senses.note: The firstborn son of Abraham's brother Nahor and Milcah; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Uz son of Dishan
senses.note: A son of Dishan, among the Horite clans of Seir in Edom; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Azazel
senses.note: The destination of the second goat on the Day of Atonement, which carried the people's sins into the wilderness. The meaning is uncertain: probably a wilderness demon, though some take it as a place or as 'the goat that goes away'.

senses.name: Gaza
senses.note: A city on the southern coast of Canaan, marking a limit of Canaanite territory; later one of the chief Philistine cities.

senses.name: Uzziel
senses.note: A son of Kohath and grandson of Levi, making him an uncle of Aaron and Moses. His sons Mishael and Elzaphan carried out the bodies of Nadab and Abihu.

senses.name: Uzziah
senses.note: King of Judah for a long reign in the eighth century BC, grandfather of Ahaz. Isaiah saw his vision of the Lord in the year Uzziah died.

senses.name: Enosh
senses.note: The son of Seth and grandson of Adam, father of Kenan. Genesis links his time with people beginning to call on the name of the LORD.

senses.name: Ai
senses.note: A Canaanite town just east of Bethel in the central hill country; Abram camped and built an altar between the two.

senses.name: Aiath
senses.note: A form of the name Ai, a town north of Jerusalem near Bethel. Isaiah names it first on an invader's imagined march toward Jerusalem.

senses.name: Ebal
senses.note: A son of Shobal and grandson of Seir the Horite. He is known only from this list.

senses.name: Elam
senses.note: An ancient kingdom east of Babylonia, in what is now south-west Iran, with Susa as its capital. Its king Kedorlaomer led a raid in Abraham's time, and Isaiah names it among powers that would attack Babylon.

senses.name: Elam
senses.note: A son of Shem in the table of nations, ancestor of the Elamites, who lived east of Babylonia in what is now south-west Iran.

senses.name: Endor
senses.note: A town in the Jezreel valley area, south of Mount Tabor. The psalm recalls that Israel's enemies were destroyed there in the time of the judges.

senses.name: Endor
senses.note: A town in the Jezreel valley near Mount Tabor, linked here with the defeat of Sisera and Jabin.

senses.name: Enaim
senses.note: A place on the road to Timnah where Tamar sat veiled and Judah met her; the exact site is unknown.

senses.name: En-mishpat
senses.note: An older name for Kadesh, an oasis in the desert south of Canaan. The four eastern kings passed through it on their campaign.

senses.name: Ephah son of Midian
senses.note: A son of Midian and grandson of Abraham through Keturah.

senses.name: Ephah
senses.note: A Midianite tribe descended from Ephah son of Midian, living in north-west Arabia and known for camel caravans.

senses.name: Irad
senses.note: A son of Enoch and grandson of Cain, father of Mehujael. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Iram
senses.note: One of the chiefs of Edom descended from Esau. He is known only from this list.

senses.name: Achbor
senses.note: Father of Baal-hanan, one of the early kings of Edom; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Achor
senses.note: A valley near Jericho, remembered as the place where Achan was stoned; Isaiah pictures it becoming a peaceful pasture.

senses.name: Alvah
senses.note: One of the chiefs descended from Esau in Edom, probably also the name of his clan or district. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Alvan
senses.note: A son of Shobal among the Horite clans of Seir, the earlier inhabitants of Edom; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: the Ammonites
senses.note: A people east of the Jordan, traced back to Ben-ammi, son of Lot by his younger daughter. They were often enemies of Israel.

senses.name: Amminadab
senses.note: A man of Judah, father of Nahshon and of Elisheba, Aaron's wife. He is also listed in David's ancestry.

senses.name: Amalek
senses.note: A grandson of Esau through Eliphaz and his concubine Timna, and an Edomite chief. He was regarded as the ancestor of the Amalekites.

senses.name: the Amalekites
senses.note: A nomadic people of the desert south of Canaan, descended from Amalek. They attacked Israel at Rephidim after the exodus and remained bitter enemies of Israel.

senses.name: Immanuel
senses.note: A name meaning God is with us, given to the child promised as a sign to Ahaz in Isaiah 7. Here the land of Judah is called his land.

senses.name: Immanuel
senses.note: "God with us", the name Isaiah gave to the child promised as a sign to Ahaz; here the land of Judah is called his land.

senses.name: Immanuel
senses.note: The name, meaning God is with us, of a child whose birth Isaiah gives King Ahaz as a sign. Matthew later applies it to Jesus.

senses.name: Immanuel
senses.note: The name, meaning God is with us, given to a child whose birth Isaiah announces to King Ahaz as a sign. Matthew applies the prophecy to Jesus.

senses.name: Gomorrah
senses.note: One of the cities of the plain near the Dead Sea, destroyed with Sodom by fire from the sky; its site is unknown. Later prophets use its fate as a byword for complete judgment.

senses.name: Amram
senses.note: A Levite, son of Kohath, who married Jochebed and was the father of Aaron, Moses and Miriam.

senses.name: Anah, son of Zibeon
senses.note: A Horite, son of Zibeon, who found hot springs in the wilderness while grazing donkeys. His daughter Oholibamah became one of Esau's wives.

senses.name: Anah, son of Seir
senses.note: One of the sons of Seir the Horite and a Horite chief in Edom. How he relates to Anah son of Zibeon in the same chapter is unclear.

senses.name: Aner
senses.note: An Amorite, brother of Mamre and Eshcol, who was in alliance with Abram and went with him to rescue Lot.

senses.name: Anathoth
senses.note: A town of priests in Benjamin, about 5 kilometres (3 miles) north-east of Jerusalem, on the line of the Assyrian advance in Isaiah's vision; later Jeremiah's home.

senses.name: Epher
senses.note: A son of Midian and grandson of Abraham and Keturah. He is known only from this list.

senses.name: Ephron
senses.note: A Hittite, son of Zohar, who sold Abraham the field and cave of Machpelah near Mamre as a family burial place. Sarah, Abraham, Isaac, Rebekah, Leah and Jacob were buried there.

senses.name: Akan
senses.note: A son of Ezer, of the Horites of Seir; known only from this list.

senses.name: Ar
senses.note: A chief city or district of Moab, east of the Dead Sea; its exact site is uncertain.

senses.name: Er
senses.note: Judah's firstborn son, Tamar's first husband. He was wicked, and the LORD ended his life.

senses.name: Arabia
senses.note: The desert lands south-east of Israel, home to caravan peoples such as Dedan, Tema and Kedar.

senses.name: the rock of Oreb
senses.note: The place where the Midianite prince Oreb was killed after Gideon's victory, recalled by Isaiah as a picture of the LORD striking down an enemy.

senses.name: Oreb
senses.note: A prince of Midian captured and killed by the men of Ephraim after Gideon's victory. The psalmist asks God to deal with Israel's enemies as he dealt with him.

senses.name: Assir
senses.note: A son of Korah, of the tribe of Levi, named among the Korahite clans; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Aroer
senses.note: A town whose name several places share; in Isaiah's oracle against Damascus it is probably one east of the Jordan. Its identity here is uncertain.

senses.name: Eri
senses.note: A son of Gad who went down to Egypt with Jacob; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Asenath
senses.note: An Egyptian woman, daughter of Potiphera priest of On, whom Pharaoh gave to Joseph as his wife. She was the mother of Manasseh and Ephraim.

senses.name: Esau
senses.note: Elder twin son of Isaac and Rebekah, a hunter who sold his birthright to his brother Jacob and lost his father's blessing. He settled in Seir and became ancestor of the Edomites.

senses.name: Asaph
senses.note: A Levite musician whom David put in charge of temple singing; Psalms 50 and 73–83 are linked with him or with the singers named after him.

senses.name: Asaph
senses.note: Father of Joah, the royal recorder under King Hezekiah; nothing more is known of him. He may or may not be connected with the family of temple singers.

senses.name: Esek
senses.note: A well dug by Isaac's servants in the valley of Gerar and claimed by the local herdsmen; Isaac named it for that dispute.

senses.name: Ashteroth-karnaim
senses.note: A town in Bashan, east of the Sea of Galilee, where Kedorlaomer's army defeated the Rephaites.

senses.name: Paran
senses.note: A wilderness in the north-east of the Sinai peninsula, south of Canaan, where Ishmael grew up.

senses.name: Paddan-aram
senses.note: The region of the Arameans in upper Mesopotamia around Haran, where Abraham's relatives settled. Isaac and Jacob both find wives there, and most of Jacob's sons are born there.

senses.name: Paddan-aram
senses.note: The region of upper Mesopotamia around Haran where Abraham's relatives lived. Isaac's wife Rebekah came from there, and Jacob spent twenty years there with Laban and had most of his children there.

senses.name: Puvah
senses.note: The second son of Issachar, son of Jacob, who went down to Egypt with the family. He is known only from the family lists.

senses.name: Put
senses.note: A son of Ham in the table of nations, standing for a people of Africa, probably in Libya.

senses.name: Putiel
senses.note: The father-in-law of Eleazar son of Aaron, and so grandfather of Phinehas; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Potiphar
senses.note: An Egyptian official of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, who bought Joseph as a slave.

senses.name: Pul
senses.note: A distant nation that Isaiah lists with Tarshish and Lud; many think the name should read Put, a people of north Africa, probably in Libya.

senses.name: Puah
senses.note: One of two Hebrew midwives in Egypt who feared God and refused Pharaoh's order to kill newborn Hebrew boys.

senses.name: Esarhaddon
senses.note: King of Assyria from 681 to 669 BC, a son of Sennacherib who succeeded him after his murder.

senses.name: Esarhaddon
senses.note: King of Assyria from 681 to 669 BC, a son of Sennacherib who succeeded him after his murder.

senses.name: Pi-hahiroth
senses.note: A place by the sea, near Migdol and Baal-zephon, where Israel camped before crossing the sea and where Pharaoh's army caught up with them. Its location is uncertain.

senses.name: Pi-hahiroth
senses.note: A place by the sea where Israel camped just before crossing, between Migdol and the sea, facing Baal-zephon. Its location is uncertain.

senses.name: Phicol
senses.note: The commander of the army of Abimelech, king of Gerar. He was present when Abimelech made treaties first with Abraham and later with Isaac.

senses.name: Phinehas
senses.note: Son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron, later a priest known for his zeal for the LORD at Peor.

senses.name: Pinon
senses.note: A clan chief of Edom descended from Esau. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Pishon
senses.note: One of the four rivers flowing out of Eden, said to wind through the land of Havilah; it cannot be identified with certainty.

senses.name: Peleg
senses.note: Son of Eber and ancestor of Abraham. Genesis connects his name, which sounds like the word for divide, with a dividing of the earth in his time.

senses.name: Pildash
senses.note: A son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by Milcah; named only in this family list.

senses.name: Pallu
senses.note: The second son of Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, and head of a Reubenite clan. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Philistia
senses.note: The coastal plain south-west of Judah, land of the Philistines and their cities such as Gaza and Ashdod. It appears among the nations that fear, oppose or will come to know Israel's God.

senses.name: Penuel
senses.note: The place by the Jabbok river, east of the Jordan, where Jacob wrestled through the night; the name means face of God. Also spelled Peniel.

senses.name: Peniel
senses.note: The place by the Jabbok river, east of the Jordan, where Jacob wrestled through the night and said he had seen God face to face.

senses.name: Pau
senses.note: The city of Hadar, one of the kings of Edom before Israel had kings. Its location is unknown.

senses.name: Pekah
senses.note: Son of Remaliah and king of Israel, who allied with Rezin of Aram to attack Ahaz of Judah.

senses.name: Pharaoh (in Abram's time)
senses.note: The king of Egypt when Abram went there during a famine. He took Sarai into his palace, was struck with plagues, and sent Abram away. He is not named.

senses.name: Pharaoh (in Joseph's time)
senses.note: The king of Egypt who raised Joseph from prison to govern the land after Joseph explained his dreams, and who welcomed Jacob's family to settle in Goshen. He is not named, and his identity is uncertain.

senses.name: Pharaoh (the oppressor)
senses.note: The new king of Egypt who forced the Israelites into hard labour and ordered their baby boys to be killed; he later tried to kill Moses. He is not named, and his identity is debated.

senses.name: Pharaoh (of the exodus)
senses.note: The king of Egypt whom Moses and Aaron confronted, who refused to let Israel go through the plagues and whose army was lost in the sea. He is not named, and his identity is debated.

senses.name: Pharaoh
senses.note: The title of the kings of Egypt. In Isaiah it stands for the Egyptian king of the prophet's day, whose help Judah sought against Assyria; Isaiah warns that relying on him will end in shame.

senses.name: Perez
senses.note: Son of Judah by Tamar and twin of Zerah, named for "breaking out" first at birth. He is the ancestor of the Perezite clan and of David.

senses.name: Mount Perazim
senses.note: The place where David defeated the Philistines, describing the LORD as breaking through his enemies; Isaiah recalls it.

senses.name: Euphrates
senses.note: The fourth river flowing from Eden, the great river of Mesopotamia running from eastern Turkey through Syria and Iraq to the Persian Gulf.

senses.name: Pithom
senses.note: A store city in the eastern Nile delta that the Israelites were forced to build for Pharaoh. Its exact site is debated.

senses.name: Pathros
senses.note: Upper Egypt, the southern part of the Nile valley; Isaiah names it among the places from which God will bring back his scattered people.

senses.name: Zeboiim
senses.note: One of the cities of the plain near Sodom and Gomorrah, whose king joined the revolt against Kedorlaomer. Its location is unknown.

senses.name: Zibeon
senses.note: A Horite chief, son of Seir, living in Edom's land before Esau's descendants; his granddaughter Oholibamah married Esau. Genesis also calls him a Hivite, perhaps through a scribal slip or a wider label.

senses.name: Ephraim
senses.note: The younger son of Joseph and his Egyptian wife Asenath. Jacob adopted him and his brother Manasseh as his own sons and blessed Ephraim ahead of the firstborn.

senses.name: Ephraim (the tribe and kingdom)
senses.note: The tribe descended from Joseph's son Ephraim, which held the central hill country. In the prophets the name often stands for the whole northern kingdom of Israel, with its capital at Samaria.

senses.name: Abel-mizraim
senses.note: The name given to the threshing floor of Atad, beyond the Jordan, where Joseph and the Egyptians mourned Jacob. The name means mourning of Egypt; the site is uncertain.

senses.name: Zohar son of Simeon
senses.note: A son of Simeon, listed among the families who went down to Egypt with Jacob; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Zohar the Hittite
senses.note: The father of Ephron the Hittite, from whom Abraham bought the cave of Machpelah; he is known only by his son.

senses.name: Ephrath
senses.note: An older name for Bethlehem or its district in Judah. Rachel died giving birth to Benjamin on the road there and was buried beside it.

senses.name: Sidon son of Canaan
senses.note: Canaan's firstborn son, named as ancestor of the people of the city of Sidon.

senses.name: Sidon
senses.note: An old Phoenician port city on the coast of what is now Lebanon, north of Tyre. Its sea traders grew rich, and Isaiah foretells its humbling along with Tyre.

senses.name: Zion
senses.note: The hill of Jerusalem that David captured, where the temple stood; the name is often used for Jerusalem and its people as a whole, the city where God is said to live among his people.

senses.name: Zillah
senses.note: One of the two wives of Lamech, a descendant of Cain. She was the mother of Tubal-cain, the metalworker, and of a daughter, Naamah.

senses.name: Ezbon
senses.note: A son of Gad, son of Jacob, who went down to Egypt with the family. He is known only from this list.

senses.name: Zalmon
senses.note: A mountain mentioned in a psalm of victory, probably in Bashan, though its location is uncertain.

senses.name: Zalmunna
senses.note: A king of Midian, with Zebah, who was captured and killed by Gideon.

senses.name: Zoan
senses.note: An Egyptian city in the north-eastern Nile delta, known in Greek as Tanis, which at times served as a royal capital. The Psalms link the plagues with the fields around it.

senses.name: Zoar
senses.note: A small town near the south end of the Dead Sea, earlier called Bela, where Lot fled when Sodom was destroyed. Its exact site is uncertain; in Isaiah it lies on the refugees' route out of Moab.

senses.name: Zepho
senses.note: A grandson of Esau through Eliphaz, and a clan chief in Edom. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Ziphion
senses.note: A son of Gad who went down to Egypt with Jacob. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Zaphenath-paneah
senses.note: The Egyptian name Pharaoh gave Joseph when he put him in charge of Egypt. Its meaning is uncertain.

senses.name: Zipporah
senses.note: Daughter of Jethro, the priest of Midian, and wife of Moses. She circumcised their son on the way to Egypt and later stayed with her father until Moses' return.

senses.name: Tyre
senses.note: A wealthy Phoenician port city on the coast of what is now Lebanon, partly built on an island. Its merchants traded across the Mediterranean, and Isaiah foretells its downfall.

senses.name: Ezer
senses.note: A son of Seir and one of the Horite chiefs in the land of Edom, father of Bilhan, Zaavan and Akan.

senses.name: Areli
senses.note: A son of Gad who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family; ancestor of a Gadite clan.

senses.name: Kedemah
senses.note: The youngest of Ishmael's twelve sons, each the chief of a tribe; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Kedar, son of Ishmael
senses.note: The second son of Ishmael, ancestor of the Arab tribe of Kedar.

senses.name: Kedar
senses.note: An Arab tribe of the Syrian-Arabian desert, descended from Ishmael's son Kedar, known for flocks and skilled archers. Isaiah foretells its decline and its later tribute to Zion.

senses.name: Kadesh
senses.note: An oasis in the desert south of Canaan, also called En-mishpat and later Kadesh-barnea. Abraham and Hagar's stories are set nearby.

senses.name: the Kadesh desert
senses.note: A wilderness named in a psalm about the LORD's voice in the storm. It is probably the desert around Kadesh south of Canaan, though some think of a Kadesh in Syria.

senses.name: Kohath
senses.note: Second son of Levi and grandfather of Moses and Aaron through his son Amram. His descendants formed one of the main Levite clans.

senses.name: Keturah
senses.note: A wife Abraham married after Sarah's death, mother of six sons including Midian, ancestors of tribes in Arabia.

senses.name: Cain
senses.note: The first son of Adam and Eve, who worked the land. He killed his brother Abel, was sent away to the land of Nod, and became the ancestor of a line that included Enoch and Lamech.

senses.name: Kenan
senses.note: Son of Enosh and father of Mahalalel in the line from Adam to Noah in Genesis 5; he is said to have lived 910 years.

senses.name: Kir
senses.note: A distant land, probably in or near Mesopotamia, from which the Arameans came and to which Assyria deported them. Here its warriors serve with the Assyrian forces.

senses.name: Kir of Moab
senses.note: A fortified city of Moab, probably the same as Kir-hareseth, usually identified with modern Kerak east of the Dead Sea.

senses.name: Kir of Moab
senses.note: A fortified city of Moab, probably Kir-hareseth at modern Kerak, east of the Dead Sea.

senses.name: Kir-heres
senses.note: A strongly fortified city of Moab, probably modern Kerak in Jordan.

senses.name: Kir-hareseth
senses.note: A chief fortified city of Moab, probably modern Kerak east of the Dead Sea, known for its raisin cakes.

senses.name: Kishon
senses.note: A stream flowing through the Jezreel valley to the Mediterranean, where Deborah and Barak defeated Sisera's army.

senses.name: Kemuel
senses.note: A son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, and father of Aram. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Kenaz
senses.note: A grandson of Esau through Eliphaz, listed among the clan chiefs of Edom; the name also stands for an Edomite clan.

senses.name: Ard
senses.note: Listed as a son of Benjamin among those who went down to Egypt; elsewhere he appears as a grandson. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Korah son of Esau
senses.note: A son of Esau by his wife Oholibamah, born in Canaan; he became the head of an Edomite clan.

senses.name: Korah, an Edomite chief
senses.note: A chief listed among the descendants of Esau's son Eliphaz. The name is missing here in some ancient witnesses and may have been copied in from the nearby list of Oholibamah's sons.

senses.name: Korah son of Izhar
senses.note: A Levite of the clan of Kohath, cousin of Moses and Aaron, whose sons headed the Korahite clans.

senses.name: the sons of Korah
senses.note: A guild of Levite temple singers descended from Korah son of Izhar. Several psalms, including 42 to 49 and 84 to 88, carry their name in the heading.

senses.name: Kiriath-arba
senses.note: The older name of Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, where Sarah died and Abraham and Isaac lived.

senses.name: Shaveh-kiriathaim
senses.note: A plain near the town of Kiriathaim east of the Dead Sea, where Kedorlaomer defeated the Emites.

senses.name: Reuben
senses.note: Jacob's firstborn son, by Leah. He tried to save Joseph from his brothers, but lost the firstborn's place after sleeping with his father's concubine Bilhah; his descendants became the tribe of Reuben.

senses.name: Reumah
senses.note: A secondary wife of Abraham's brother Nahor, who bore him four sons; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Arodi
senses.note: A son of Gad who went down to Egypt with Jacob, founder of a clan; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Rosh
senses.note: A son of Benjamin, among those who went down to Egypt with Jacob; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Rebekah
senses.note: Daughter of Bethuel and sister of Laban, from Abraham's relatives in Paddan-aram. She became Isaac's wife and the mother of the twins Esau and Jacob, and helped Jacob take his father's blessing.

senses.name: the chief officer
senses.note: A high Assyrian official, known by the title Rabshakeh, whom Sennacherib sent with an army to Jerusalem. He called on Hezekiah's people from outside the wall to surrender.

senses.name: the chief officer
senses.note: A high-ranking Assyrian official (in Hebrew, the Rabshakeh) sent by Sennacherib to Jerusalem. He tries to talk Hezekiah's people into surrendering, mocking their trust in the LORD.

senses.name: Rahab
senses.note: A poetic name for Egypt, taken from the name of a sea monster; Isaiah uses it to mock Egypt as useless help.

senses.name: Rahab
senses.note: A mythical sea monster standing for chaos, which the LORD is pictured as crushing. The image probably also looks back to Egypt's defeat at the sea.

senses.name: Rehoboth
senses.note: A well dug by Isaac near Gerar that no one disputed, so he named it 'Open Spaces'.

senses.name: Rehoboth on the River
senses.note: The home town of Shaul, a king of Edom. The location is uncertain; the river may be the Euphrates or a stream in Edom.

senses.name: Rehoboth-Ir
senses.note: One of the cities in Assyria built by Nimrod; the name means "city squares". Its location is unknown.

senses.name: Rehoboth-Ir
senses.note: A city in Assyria built along with Nineveh and Calah; its location is unknown, and the name may mean 'the broad places of the city'.

senses.name: Rachel
senses.note: The younger daughter of Laban and the wife Jacob loved most, sister of Leah. After years without children she bore Joseph, and she died giving birth to Benjamin near Bethlehem.

senses.name: Riphath
senses.note: A son of Gomer in the table of nations, probably the ancestor of a people of Asia Minor; nothing more is known.

senses.name: Ariel
senses.note: A poetic name Isaiah gives to Jerusalem, the city where David camped. The word can mean altar hearth, and Isaiah plays on that sense.

senses.name: Ariel
senses.note: A name for Jerusalem in Isaiah, probably meaning altar hearth, the place where David camped.

senses.name: Ramah
senses.note: A town of Benjamin about 8 km north of Jerusalem, on the route of the Assyrian advance Isaiah describes.

senses.name: Remaliah
senses.note: Father of Pekah, king of Israel, who allied with Rezin of Aram against Ahaz of Judah. Isaiah scornfully calls Pekah only the son of Remaliah.

senses.name: Resen
senses.note: A city in Assyria between Nineveh and Calah, said to be founded by Nimrod. Its site is unknown.

senses.name: Arioch
senses.note: King of Ellasar, one of the four eastern kings who raided the cities near the Dead Sea and carried off Lot. Ellasar's location is uncertain.

senses.name: Reu
senses.note: Son of Peleg and father of Serug, in the line from Shem to Abraham; he is known only from this genealogy.

senses.name: Reuel, father-in-law of Moses
senses.note: A priest of Midian, father of Zipporah, whose daughters Moses defended at a well. He is called Jethro elsewhere in Exodus.

senses.name: Reuel, son of Esau
senses.note: A son of Esau and Basemath, whose four sons became chiefs in Edom.

senses.name: Raamah
senses.note: A son of Cush and father of Sheba and Dedan, named in the table of nations; a people of Arabia probably took his name.

senses.name: Rameses
senses.note: A city and district in the eastern Nile Delta, in the area of Goshen, where Israel settled and later built supply cities for Pharaoh; the exodus set out from there.

senses.name: the Valley of Rephaim
senses.note: A fertile valley just south-west of Jerusalem, known for its grain fields.

senses.name: Rephidim
senses.note: A camping place of Israel in the wilderness before Sinai, where there was no water and Moses struck the rock. Israel fought Amalek there. The location is uncertain.

senses.name: Erech
senses.note: An ancient city of southern Mesopotamia, known as Uruk, part of Nimrod's kingdom.

senses.name: Rezin
senses.note: The last king of Aram, ruling from Damascus. Around 734 BC he joined Pekah of Israel in attacking Judah under Ahaz; Assyria soon conquered Damascus and killed him.

senses.name: Rezeph
senses.note: A city in northern Syria conquered by the Assyrians; the Assyrian envoys list it among places whose gods could not save them.

senses.name: Aram, son of Shem
senses.note: A son of Shem in the table of nations, ancestor of the Aramean peoples.

senses.name: Aram, son of Kemuel
senses.note: A grandson of Nahor, Abraham's brother, named in a family list; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Aram
senses.note: The Aramean kingdom north-east of Israel, with Damascus as its capital, roughly modern Syria. In Isaiah its king Rezin allied with Israel against Judah.

senses.name: Sheol
senses.note: The Hebrew name for the realm of the dead, pictured as a place deep below the earth where all the dead go. Some passages, as in Genesis, render it simply as the grave.

senses.name: Shaul son of Simeon
senses.note: A son of Simeon whose mother was a Canaanite, and founder of a Simeonite clan; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Shaul of Rehoboth
senses.note: An early king of Edom from Rehoboth on the River, who ruled after Samlah and before Baal-hanan; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Saul
senses.note: The first king of Israel, from the tribe of Benjamin, whose home town was Gibeah. Several psalm headings set David's songs in the years when Saul was hunting him.

senses.name: Aram-zobah
senses.note: An Aramean kingdom north of Damascus, in modern Syria, which David fought and defeated.

senses.name: Aram-zobah
senses.note: An Aramean kingdom north of Damascus, in today's Syria, defeated by David.

senses.name: Shear-jashub
senses.note: A son of Isaiah, whose name means a remnant will return. He went with his father to meet King Ahaz.

senses.name: Sheba, son of Raamah
senses.note: A descendant of Ham through Cush and Raamah in the table of nations, probably standing for a people of Arabia.

senses.name: Sheba, son of Joktan
senses.note: A descendant of Shem through Joktan in the table of nations, probably standing for a people of southern Arabia.

senses.name: Sheba, son of Jokshan
senses.note: A grandson of Abraham and Keturah through Jokshan, and brother of Dedan.

senses.name: Sheba
senses.note: A wealthy trading kingdom, probably in south-western Arabia (modern Yemen), famous for gold, incense and spices brought north by caravan.

senses.name: Aram-naharaim
senses.note: 'Aram of the two rivers', the land of upper Mesopotamia around the Euphrates where Nahor's family lived; David later fought its forces.

senses.name: Sibmah
senses.note: A town of Moab near Heshbon, famous for its vineyards, whose ruin Isaiah laments; the exact site is uncertain.

senses.name: Shebna
senses.note: An official of King Hezekiah, first in charge of the palace and later royal secretary. Isaiah rebukes him for carving himself a grand tomb, and he goes out to meet the Assyrian envoy.

senses.name: Aran
senses.note: A son of Dishan, among the descendants of Seir the Horite; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: the Arnon
senses.note: A river and deep gorge flowing west into the Dead Sea, the traditional northern border of Moab.

senses.name: the Almighty
senses.note: A title of the God of Israel, often in the phrase God Almighty, used especially in his promises to the ancestors. The original meaning of the word behind it is uncertain.

senses.name: the Valley of Siddim
senses.note: A valley where the kings of the plain fought four eastern kings, full of tar pits; Genesis says it later lay under the Dead Sea, probably at its southern end.

senses.name: Shobal
senses.note: A son of Seir the Horite and one of the Horite chiefs living in Edom before Esau's descendants; known only from these lists.

senses.name: Arpad
senses.note: A city-state in northern Syria, north of Aleppo, conquered by Assyria. Assyrian officials named it among the cities whose gods could not save them.

senses.name: the Valley of Shaveh
senses.note: A valley also called the King's Valley, where the king of Sodom and Melchizedek met Abram after his victory; probably near Jerusalem.

senses.name: Shaveh-kiriathaim
senses.note: A plain or town east of the Dead Sea where Kedorlaomer's allies defeated the Emites; the exact site is uncertain.

senses.name: Shuah
senses.note: A son of Abraham by Keturah; he is probably the ancestor of an Arabian people.

senses.name: Arpachshad
senses.note: A son of Shem born two years after the flood, and father of Shelah. He is an ancestor of Eber and Abraham in the family line of Genesis.

senses.name: Shuni
senses.note: A son of Gad and head of a clan of that tribe; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Shua
senses.note: A Canaanite man whose daughter Judah married; she bore him Er, Onan and Shelah.

senses.name: Shur
senses.note: A desert region in the north-west of the Sinai peninsula, east of Egypt's border. Hagar fled toward it, and Israel crossed its wilderness after leaving the Red Sea.

senses.name: Ararat
senses.note: A mountainous land north of Assyria, around Lake Van in what is now eastern Turkey and Armenia, known in Assyrian records as Urartu. The ark came to rest in its mountains.

senses.name: Sitnah
senses.note: A well dug by Isaac's servants near Gerar and named "Hostility" after the local herdsmen disputed it. Its location is unknown.

senses.name: Ashbel
senses.note: A son of Benjamin who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family; ancestor of a Benjaminite clan.

senses.name: Shihor
senses.note: A branch or stretch of the Nile in Egypt, here a source of the grain that Tyre traded.

senses.name: Shiloh
senses.note: A difficult word in Jacob's blessing of Judah. Some read it as a name or title for a coming ruler, others as the town of Shiloh; this translation takes it to mean the one to whom the scepter belongs.

senses.name: Shiloh
senses.note: A town in Ephraim north of Bethel where the tabernacle stood in the time of the judges, before God abandoned it.

senses.name: Eshban
senses.note: A son of Dishon among the Horites of Seir, named only in this list.

senses.name: Shechem
senses.note: Son of Hamor the Hivite, ruler of the town of Shechem. He violated Dinah, Jacob's daughter, then sought to marry her; her brothers Simeon and Levi killed him and the men of the town.

senses.name: Shechem
senses.note: An ancient town in the hill country of central Canaan, between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim, near modern Nablus. Abram stopped there and Jacob camped outside it.

senses.name: Ashdod
senses.note: One of the five main Philistine cities, near the Mediterranean coast; the Assyrian king Sargon captured it in about 711 BC.

senses.name: Shelah
senses.note: The third son of Judah by the daughter of Shua. Judah held him back from marrying Tamar after his older brothers died, which led to Tamar's ruse.

senses.name: Shelah
senses.note: A son of Arpachshad and father of Eber, listed in the family line from Shem to Abraham. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Shiloah
senses.note: A gentle stream or channel carrying water from the Gihon spring in Jerusalem, used by Isaiah as a picture of quiet trust in the LORD.

senses.name: Salem
senses.note: The city of Melchizedek, priest-king who blessed Abraham. A psalm uses the name for Jerusalem, and it is traditionally taken as an early name for that city.

senses.name: Shillem
senses.note: A son of Naphtali who went down to Egypt with Jacob. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Solomon
senses.note: Son of David and Bathsheba and king of Israel after him, famous for his wisdom. The book of Proverbs gathers sayings under his name, and Psalm 72 is linked with him.

senses.name: Shelomith
senses.note: A woman of the tribe of Dan, daughter of Dibri, whose son by an Egyptian father blasphemed the Name. Nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Sheleph
senses.note: A son of Joktan in the line of Shem, probably the ancestor of an Arabian tribe; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Shem
senses.note: The first named of Noah's three sons, with Ham and Japheth. He is the ancestor of many peoples, including Abraham's family line.

senses.name: Shemeber
senses.note: King of Zeboiim, one of the cities of the plain allied with Sodom against the four eastern kings. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Assyria
senses.note: The land on the upper Tigris in northern Mesopotamia (modern Iraq), later the centre of a great empire. Genesis places the Tigris river to its east.

senses.name: Shammah
senses.note: A son of Reuel and grandson of Esau and Basemath, who became a chief in Edom. He is known only from these lists.

senses.name: Samuel
senses.note: The prophet and last judge of Israel, who anointed Saul and David as kings; the psalm remembers him as one who called on the LORD and was answered.

senses.name: the Asshurites
senses.note: A people descended from Dedan, grandson of Abraham and Keturah, probably in Arabia. Nothing more is known of them.

senses.name: Samlah
senses.note: A king of Edom from Masrekah, named in the list of kings who reigned before Israel had a king; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Simeon
senses.note: The second son of Jacob and Leah. With Levi he killed the men of Shechem after Dinah was violated, and Joseph later held him in Egypt as a hostage.

senses.name: Shimei son of Gershon
senses.note: A grandson of Levi through Gershon and the ancestor of a Levite clan.

senses.name: Shimron
senses.note: A son of Issachar who went down to Egypt with Jacob, founder of a clan; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Samaria
senses.note: The capital city of the northern kingdom of Israel, often standing for the whole kingdom. Isaiah warns that it will fall to Assyria, as it did in about 722 BC.

senses.name: Eshcol
senses.note: An Amorite, brother of Mamre and Aner, who was allied with Abram and went with him to rescue Lot.

senses.name: Ashkenaz
senses.note: A son of Gomer and grandson of Japheth in the table of nations. The name probably stands for a people of the north, perhaps the Scythians.

senses.name: Shinab
senses.note: King of Admah, one of the five kings of the Jordan plain who rebelled against Kedorlaomer; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Shinar
senses.note: The old name for the land of Babylonia in southern Mesopotamia, between the Tigris and Euphrates, where the tower of Babel was built.

senses.name: Seir
senses.note: The hill country south-east of the Dead Sea, first home of the Horites, where Esau settled; it became another name for Edom.

senses.name: Seir the Horite
senses.note: The ancestor of the Horites who lived in the land later called Edom before Esau's descendants; his sons were the Horite chiefs.

senses.name: Shepho
senses.note: A son of Shobal, of the Horites of Seir; known only from this list.

senses.name: Shiphrah
senses.note: One of the two Hebrew midwives who feared God and refused Pharaoh's order to kill Hebrew baby boys.

senses.name: Sharezer
senses.note: A son of the Assyrian king Sennacherib who, with his brother Adrammelech, murdered his father and fled to Ararat.

senses.name: Sarah
senses.note: Abraham's wife and half-sister, first called Sarai. Childless into old age, she bore Isaac as God had promised, and she was buried in the cave of Machpelah; Isaiah points back to her as the mother of the nation.

senses.name: Serug
senses.note: A son of Reu and father of Nahor, Abraham's grandfather, in the family line from Shem. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Sharon
senses.note: The fertile coastal plain of Israel between Joppa and Mount Carmel, known for its pastures and flowers.

senses.name: Serah
senses.note: A daughter of Asher and sister of his sons, among those who went down to Egypt with Jacob; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Sarai
senses.note: The wife of Abram and the earlier name of Sarah. Long unable to have children, she gave her slave Hagar to Abram; God later renamed her Sarah and promised her a son.

senses.name: Sirion
senses.note: The Sidonian name for Mount Hermon, the high mountain on the northern border of Israel.

senses.name: Seth
senses.note: The third son of Adam and Eve, born after Abel was killed, and father of Enosh. Genesis 5 traces the line from Adam to Noah through him.

senses.name: Asher
senses.note: Jacob's eighth son, born to Leah's slave woman Zilpah. His descendants formed one of the tribes of Israel, and Jacob's blessing promises them rich food.

senses.name: Mount Tabor
senses.note: A prominent rounded mountain in lower Galilee, south-west of the Sea of Galilee. A psalm pictures it rejoicing in God's name.

senses.name: Tidal
