senses.note: King of Goyim, one of the four eastern kings allied with Kedorlaomer against the cities of the Jordan plain; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Asherah poles
senses.note: Wooden poles or trees set up beside altars as symbols of the Canaanite goddess Asherah. Israel was told to cut them down.

senses.name: Tubal
senses.note: A son of Japheth in the table of nations, ancestor of a people.

senses.name: Tubal
senses.note: A people probably living in eastern Asia Minor (modern Turkey), named with Javan among distant nations who will hear of God's glory.

senses.name: Tubal-cain
senses.note: Son of Lamech and Zillah in Cain's line, who made tools of bronze and iron; Naamah was his sister.

senses.name: Tubal-Cain
senses.note: Son of Lamech and Zillah in Cain's line, described as the first to forge tools of bronze and iron.

senses.name: Togarmah
senses.note: A son of Gomer and great-grandson of Noah. His name was linked with a people of eastern Asia Minor, probably in the region of Armenia.

senses.name: Tola
senses.note: The eldest son of Issachar and head of a clan of that tribe.

senses.name: Tahash
senses.note: A son of Nahor by his secondary wife Reumah; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Tema
senses.note: A son of Ishmael, Abraham's son, named among Ishmael's twelve sons.

senses.name: Tema
senses.note: An oasis town in north-west Arabia on the caravan routes, probably named after Ishmael's son. Isaiah calls on its people to bring water and food to fugitives.

senses.name: Teman
senses.note: A grandson of Esau through Eliphaz and a chief in Edom. The Edomite region of Teman probably took its name from his clan.

senses.name: Tiras
senses.note: A son of Japheth, named in the table of nations; nothing more is known of him or the people descended from him.

senses.name: Abraham
senses.note: The ancestor of Israel, first called Abram, whom God called from Mesopotamia to Canaan and promised many descendants and the land. He is the father of Isaac and Ishmael, and God is later named as the God of Abraham.

senses.name: Telassar
senses.note: A place where the people of Eden lived, conquered by Assyria; probably in northern Mesopotamia. Its exact site is unknown.

senses.name: Timnah
senses.note: A town in the hill country of Judah where Judah went to shear his sheep; Tamar met him on the road there. Its exact site is uncertain.

senses.name: Timna
senses.note: A Horite woman, sister of Lotan, who became the concubine of Esau's son Eliphaz and bore Amalek. The two notes probably refer to the same woman.

senses.name: Timna, an Edomite chief
senses.note: A chief or clan of Edom named in the list of chiefs descended from Esau; it may be named after the woman Timna. Nothing more is known.

senses.name: Tamar
senses.note: The widow of Judah's sons Er and Onan. Denied his third son, she disguised herself and had twins, Perez and Zerah, by Judah, who admitted she was more righteous than he.

senses.name: Topheth
senses.note: A place in the Hinnom valley south of Jerusalem where children were burned in sacrifice. Isaiah pictures it as a pyre made ready for the king of Assyria.

senses.name: Etham
senses.note: A camping place of the Israelites after Succoth, on the edge of the wilderness during the exodus from Egypt; its exact location is unknown.

senses.name: Tirhakah
senses.note: A king of Cush who ruled Egypt as pharaoh from about 690 to 664 BC. He marched out against Sennacherib during the Assyrian campaign against Judah.

senses.name: Terah
senses.note: Son of Nahor and father of Abram, Nahor and Haran. He set out with his family from Ur of the Chaldeans toward Canaan but settled and died in Haran.

senses.name: Tarshish
senses.note: A distant sea-trading port, probably in the far west of the Mediterranean, perhaps Tartessus in Spain. Its large merchant ships became a byword for long-distance trade.

senses.name: Tarshish
senses.note: A son of Javan in the table of nations, standing for a seafaring people, probably in the far west of the Mediterranean.

senses.name: the commander-in-chief
senses.note: The Assyrian title of the army's supreme commander, sometimes given as the name Tartan; he captured Ashdod for Sargon. He is not named.

senses.name: Abram
senses.note: The earlier name of Abraham, son of Terah, who left Haran for Canaan at the LORD's call. God renamed him Abraham, "father of many nations", when he was ninety-nine.

senses.name: Beer-elim
senses.note: A place in Moab, probably near its border, where the cry of mourning is heard. Its location is uncertain.

senses.name: Beer-elim
senses.note: A place on the border of Moab, mentioned in Isaiah's lament over Moab; its location is uncertain.

senses.name: Beeri
senses.note: A Hittite, father of Judith, one of Esau's wives. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Beer-lahai-roi
senses.note: A well in the Negev between Kadesh and Bered where the angel of the LORD met Hagar. Isaac later lived near it.

senses.name: Beer-lahai-roi
senses.note: A well in the Negev between Kadesh and Bered, named by Hagar after God saw her there. Isaac later lived near it.

senses.name: Beer-lahai-roi
senses.note: A well in the Negev between Kadesh and Bered, named by Hagar after God saw her there; Isaac later lived near it. Its exact site is unknown.

senses.name: Beersheba
senses.note: A town and wells in the Negev, at the southern edge of the land; the name is explained by an oath sworn there. Abraham, Isaac and Jacob all lived or worshiped there.

senses.name: Babel
senses.note: The city in the land of Shinar where people built a tower and the LORD confused their language and scattered them. The name sounds like the Hebrew for "confuse"; it is the same name as Babylon.

senses.name: Babylon
senses.note: A great city on the Euphrates in southern Mesopotamia, first named in Nimrod's kingdom. In Isaiah it is the empire that would carry Judah into exile and was itself to fall.

senses.name: Bedad
senses.note: The father of Hadad, an early king of Edom; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Buz
senses.note: A son of Abraham's brother Nahor and Milcah, probably the ancestor of an Arabian tribe; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Agur
senses.note: Son of Jakeh, to whom Proverbs 30 is credited; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Eglaim
senses.note: A town of Moab, probably near its border, where the wailing over Moab is heard. The location is uncertain.
